c_vaccine_name: Attenuated Salmonella live vector vaccine secreting Brucella abortus BLS
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Salmonella strain secreting the Brucella abortus protective antigen BLS, used as a live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant protection against Brucella abortus 544 challenge with protection index 0.6 in spleen and 1.12 in liver; full protection against virulent Salmonella challenge with no mortality in immunized mice. [Ref:7128]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella strain engineered to secrete BLS antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Attenuated Salmonella live vector vaccine secreting Brucella abortus Omp19
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Salmonella strain secreting the Brucella abortus protective antigen Omp19, used as a live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant protection against Brucella abortus 544 challenge with protection index 0.96 in spleen and 1.14 in liver; full protection against virulent Salmonella challenge with no mortality in immunized mice. [Ref:7128]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella strain engineered to secrete Omp19 antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Attenuated Salmonella live vector vaccine secreting Brucella abortus PrpA
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Salmonella strain secreting the Brucella abortus protective antigen PrpA, used as a live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant protection against Brucella abortus 544 challenge with protection index 0.66 in spleen and 1.81 in liver; full protection against virulent Salmonella challenge with no mortality in immunized mice. [Ref:7128]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella strain engineered to secrete PrpA antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Attenuated Salmonella live vector vaccine secreting Brucella abortus SodC
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Salmonella strain secreting the Brucella abortus protective antigen SodC, used as a live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Significant protection against Brucella abortus 544 challenge with protection index 0.85 in spleen and 1.37 in liver; full protection against virulent Salmonella challenge with no mortality in immunized mice. [Ref:7128]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella strain engineered to secrete SodC antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella 18 kD outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The 18 kD outer membrane protein (OMP) was synthesized in Escherichia coli cells and used as a preparation to study its influence on protection against brucellosis. Efficacy: The 18 kD OMP protected 66.7% of experimental animals against brucellosis, compared to 78.0% protection by the commercial live vaccine. [Ref:7344]
c_preparation: OMP preparation obtained by genetic engineering technique expressed in E. coli.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella 38 kD outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The 38 kD outer membrane protein (OMP) was synthesized in Escherichia coli cells and used as a preparation to study its influence on protection against brucellosis. Efficacy: The 38 kD OMP did not provide protective activity; the infectivity index and colony forming units in spleen were higher in vaccinated animals than controls. [Ref:7344]
c_preparation: OMP preparation obtained by genetic engineering technique expressed in E. coli.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella 7α-HSDH subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated 7α-HSDH antigen as a safer vaccine candidate compared to commercial live vaccines. Efficacy: Protein with poly I:C induced higher protection than protein alone and similar protection to live attenuated vaccines. [Ref:7196]
c_preparation: Recombinant 7α-HSDH protein formulated with poly I:C adjuvant or as naked protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella A antigen conjugate vaccine
c_description: The study introduces a polysaccharide-protein conjugate vaccine based on synthetic oligosaccharides derived from Brucella O-polysaccharide (OPS) that aims to avoid false positive serodiagnostic results caused by current vaccines. Efficacy: Immunized mice developed antibodies to the Brucella A antigen that did not react in diagnostic tests based on the M antigen, indicating potential for improved vaccine specificity. [Ref:7097]
c_preparation: A chemically synthesized polysaccharide-protein conjugate vaccine targeting the Brucella A antigen, designed to not induce antibodies reactive in diagnostic tests based on the M antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella A antigen hexasaccharide and heptasaccharide conjugate vaccines
c_description: The study hypothesized that a chemically synthesized pure A antigen vaccine would allow differentiation of infected animals from vaccinated ones by using a synthetic M diagnostic antigen that does not react with antibodies generated by the vaccine. [Ref:7081]
c_preparation: Two forms of the A antigen (hexasaccharide and heptasaccharide) were chemically synthesized and conjugated to tetanus toxoid via reducing and nonreducing terminal sugars. Conjugation via the periodate oxidized terminal nonreducing monosaccharide was used to destroy terminal epitopes and focus the antibody response on internal A epitopes.
c_antigen: A antigen hexasaccharide; A antigen heptasaccharide

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 18-kDa protein DNA vaccine
c_description: A single intrasplenic injection of plasmid DNA encoding the 18-kDa protein from Brucella abortus was used to induce immune responses for monoclonal antibody production. Efficacy: The technique resulted in early, strong monoclonal antibody production, with hybridomas generated up to 25 days after a single injection, indicating persistent expression of the antigen gene. [Ref:6874]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA containing the expression vector for the 18-kDa protein in saline; administered by intrasplenic injection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 18-kilodalton outer membrane protein recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A recombinant vaccinia virus expressing an 18-kDa outer membrane protein of Brucella abortus was constructed using shuttle vector pMCO2 and vaccinia virus wild-type WR strain. Efficacy: Mice inoculated with the recombinant virus were not protected against challenge with virulent B. abortus 2308. [Ref:6868]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing the 18-kDa outer membrane protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 22.9 kDa protein vaccine
c_description: Two novel proteins from Brucella abortus strain RB51 were isolated and characterized for immunological properties. Efficacy: The 22.9-kDa protein was as effective as the live Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine in protection studies. [Ref:6869]
c_preparation: Purified 22.9-kDa protein used as protective immunogen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 31-kDa protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The 31-kDa protein, thought to be localized at or near the bacterial cell surface, was previously shown to protect against experimental brucellosis in rodents. The gene coding for this protein has been cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli, allowing production of the protein free of Brucella contaminants. Efficacy: Preliminary evidence showed protection against experimental brucellosis in rodents by the purified 31-kDa protein. [Ref:7135]
c_preparation: Recombinant 31-kDa protein expressed in E. coli from its native promoter; purified protein free of Brucella contaminants.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 32.2 kDa protein vaccine
c_description: Two novel proteins from Brucella abortus strain RB51 were isolated and characterized for immunological properties. Efficacy: The 32.2-kDa protein had a poor protective effect under similar conditions. [Ref:6869]
c_preparation: Purified 32.2-kDa protein used as immunogen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 54 kDa HtrA homologue recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Genes encoding a 54 kDa E. coli HtrA homologue were cloned into shuttle plasmids and transfected into vaccinia virus to develop recombinant vSB54. Efficacy: vSB54 induced a humoral immune response recognizing the 54 kDa HtrA homologue. [Ref:7327]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing a 54 kDa protein corresponding to the HtrA homologue.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ABC-type transporter DNA vaccine
c_description: A DNA vaccine containing an open reading frame of genomic island 3, specific for Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis, was constructed and tested. Efficacy: The vaccine induced protection in BALB/c mice against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus 2308. [Ref:6997]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the open reading frame with homology to an ABC-type transporter (pV278a) administered by intramuscular injection.
c_antigen: open reading frame with homology to an ABC-type transporter (genomic island 3)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ABOR recombinant protein subunit vaccine
c_description: A designed recombinant polypeptide composed of five Brucella abortus proteins was produced and evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The ABOR recombinant protein induced a strong Th1 immune response with high levels of specific IgG2a and proinflammatory cytokines compared to control. [Ref:7261]
c_preparation: The recombinant ABOR protein (549 amino acids) combined with chitin as an adjuvant was administered subcutaneously.
c_antigen: MOXR family ATPase-α2, T9SS C-terminal target domain-containing protein, Cobyric acid synthase, Hypothetical protein, VirB11 type IV Secretion protein (combined in ABOR recombinant polypeptide)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus acellular lipopolysaccharides subunit vaccine
c_description: This study presents the first intranasal, controlled release, subunit nanovaccine using mucoadhesive tamarind seed polymer (xyloglucan) nanoparticles produced by rapid expansion of supercritical solution technology. Efficacy: The nanovaccine elicited prolonged humoral and cell-mediated immunity, with higher mucosal IgA and IgG levels, and higher systemic IgG levels post priming and boosting compared to control. [Ref:7174]
c_preparation: Xyloglucan nanoparticles loaded separately with antigenic acellular lipopolysaccharides from Brucella abortus strain 19 and the immunoadjuvant quillaja saponin.
c_antigen: acellular lipopolysaccharides from Brucella abortus strain 19

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Adk SecB combination subunit vaccine
c_description: Combination of two recombinant proteins encoded by Brucella abortus genes Adk and SecB were cloned and expressed in E. coli and evaluated as combined subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with combined recombinant Adk and SecB proteins significantly reduced spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS control, indicating protection against B. abortus infection. [Ref:7159]
c_preparation: Combined recombinant Adk and SecB proteins purified after expression in Escherichia coli DH5α; administered intraperitoneally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Adk subunit vaccine
c_description: Two recombinant proteins encoded by Brucella abortus gene Adk were cloned and expressed in E. coli and evaluated as single subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with recombinant Adk protein significantly reduced spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS control, indicating protection against B. abortus infection. [Ref:7159]
c_preparation: Recombinant Adk protein purified after expression in Escherichia coli DH5α; administered intraperitoneally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus AfuA subunit vaccine
c_description: Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with AfuA appeared to have some effect on clearance kinetics. [Ref:6965]
c_preparation: Recombinant AfuA protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis Omp19 subunit vaccine in N-trimethyl chitosan nanoparticles
c_description: Recombinant Omp19 protein was loaded onto N-trimethyl chitosan (TMC) nanoparticles by ionic gelation with tripolyphosphate. The vaccine was administered orally and intraperitoneally. Efficacy: Oral immunization with TMC/Omp19 nanoparticles induced a remarkably high protection level against B. melitensis and B. abortus. [Ref:7044]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp19 protein encapsulated in TMC nanoparticles.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis Omp19 subunit vaccine with Freund's adjuvant
c_description: The omp19 gene was expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) and recombinant Omp19 purified. Omp19 was formulated with Freund's adjuvant for intraperitoneal administration. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization induced Th1 immune response and conferred protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge. [Ref:7044]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp19 protein combined with Freund's incomplete adjuvant (IFA).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus antigen subunit vaccine
c_description: Gold nanoparticles were synthesized and conjugated to an isolated antigen from Brucella abortus to be used as an immunomodulator in immunization and vaccination. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the gold nanoparticle-antigen conjugate produced high-titer antibodies (1:10240) and showed increased immune cell activities and serum interleukin levels; these mice were more resistant to Brucella abortus strain 82 than mice immunized by other schemes. [Ref:7243]
c_preparation: Gold nanoparticles of 15 nm diameter conjugated with the isolated Brucella abortus antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus apolipoprotein N-acyltransferase subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was designed based on a putative immunogenic epitope of the apolipoprotein N-acyltransferase (Int), identified as the target of a highly expressed small RNA during early infection of bone marrow-derived macrophages. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed reduced viable bacterial counts in liver, spleen, and axillary lymph nodes compared to non-vaccinated controls; reduced number and size of granulomas in liver. [Ref:7198]
c_preparation: Epitope-based subunit vaccine selected by immunoinformatic analysis; details on formulation or adjuvant not reported.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus AsnC subunit vaccine
c_description: Screening of Brucella protective antigens identified AsnC as a protein stimulating strong IFN-γ responses and protective efficacy. Efficacy: Mice immunized with AsnC plus adjuvant showed protection against virulent B. abortus infection comparable to licensed vaccine S19 and Cu-Zn SOD antigen. [Ref:2099]
c_preparation: Recombinant AsnC protein plus adjuvant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus asp24 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked deletion mutants of asp24 gene in Brucella abortus to develop improved live vaccine strains. Efficacy: Deltaasp24 mutants showed superior protection compared to current vaccine strains and other deletion mutants (DeltamanBA and DeltavirB2) against homologous and heterologous challenge infections. [Ref:700]
c_preparation: Live attenuated unmarked deletion mutant of asp24 gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus asp24 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate BADeltaasp24 is an unmarked deletion mutant evaluated for protection against aerosol challenge. Efficacy: BADeltaasp24 conferred superior protection to mice against homologous and heterologous aerosol challenge infection. [Ref:694]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus AspC Dps InpB Ndk subunit vaccine
c_description: The study assessed the protective efficacy of single subunit vaccines encoded by B. abortus genes aspC, dps, yaeC, and inpB, and further investigated a combined subunit vaccine consisting of purified AspC, Dps, InpB, and Ndk proteins. Efficacy: The combined subunit vaccine showed superior protective effect in mice against brucellosis compared to single antigens and was comparable to the live attenuated vaccine RB51. [Ref:7106]
c_preparation: Intraperitoneal injection of a combination of purified recombinant proteins AspC, Dps, InpB, and Ndk.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus aspC subunit vaccine
c_description: Single subunit vaccines encoded by B. abortus genes aspC, dps, yaeC, and inpB were assessed for protective efficacy. Efficacy: Single antigens (except YaeC) elicited immune responses but had lower protection compared to the combined vaccine. [Ref:7106]
c_preparation: Immunization with individual recombinant proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0263 DNA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a DNA vaccine encoding the BAB1_0263 open reading frame of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Not reported protective efficacy; only pVF278 showed protection against challenge. [Ref:2664]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the BAB1_0263 gene administered by intramuscular injection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0267 DNA vaccine
c_description: Immunization with the recombinant plasmid based on BAB1_0267 ORF was evaluated for immunogenicity. Efficacy: Did not provide significant levels of protection against Brucella abortus 2308 infection. [Ref:7071]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid DNA encoding BAB1_0267 ORF.
c_antigen: BAB1_0267 open reading frame (protein with SH3 domain)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0270 DNA vaccine
c_description: Immunization with the recombinant plasmid based on BAB1_0270 ORF was evaluated for immunogenicity and protection. Efficacy: Induced heightened resistance to Brucella abortus 2308 infection in mice. [Ref:7071]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid DNA encoding BAB1_0270 ORF.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0273 BAB1_0278 sodC DNA vaccine
c_description: New multivalent DNA vaccines were constructed by fusion of BAB1_0273 and/or BAB1_0278 ORFs from genomic island 3 and the Brucella abortus 2308 sodC gene linked by prolines and alanines. Efficacy: Vaccines conferred low levels of protection against challenge with B. abortus 2308. [Ref:7094]
c_preparation: Fusion DNA vaccines encoding BAB1_0273 and/or BAB1_0278 antigens conjugated to sodC protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1_0278 DNA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a DNA vaccine encoding the BAB1_0278 open reading frame of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Induced protection in BALB/c mice against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308. [Ref:2664]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the BAB1_0278 gene administered by intramuscular injection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BAB1-0278 Lactococcus lactis PNZ8148-Usp45 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A vector vaccine against brucellosis was developed using recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Brucella outer membrane protein BAB1-0278. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly higher total IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a levels compared to PBS controls; increased cytokine production (IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, IL-10); and reduced inflammatory response, morphological impairment, alveolar edema, and lymphocyte infiltration in spleen tissue. [Ref:7231]
c_preparation: The BAB1-0278 gene was cloned into the pNZ8148 vector, transformed into L. lactis, and the target protein was extracted and confirmed by SDS-PAGE and western blot.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus bacterioferritin DNA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was delivered using live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica serotypes O:3 and O:9 as vectors to improve protection and evaluate the role of anti-LPS antibodies. Efficacy: Induced antigen-specific Th1-type immune responses; however, only O:9 vector strains (which induce anti-LPS antibodies) conferred significant protection against B. abortus 544 infection. [Ref:1270]
c_preparation: Naked-DNA plasmids encoding bacterioferritin delivered by live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica O:3 or O:9 strains via intragastric immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP 0-70 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the effect of covalent chemical modification of Brucella abortus 19 salt-extractable proteins on immune responses. Efficacy: Acylation decreased immune responses but reduced spleen CFU and splenomegaly, indicating altered protection; monophosphoryl lipid A enhanced immunogenicity. [Ref:7332]
c_preparation: Salt-extractable proteins BCSP 0-70 and BCSP 70-100 were chemically modified with acetoacetic anhydride; monophosphoryl lipid A was used as an adjuvant to enhance immunogenicity of BCSP 0-70.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is derived from Brucella abortus strain 19 cell surface proteins. Efficacy: BCSP was immunogenic and protective in mice, showing reduced splenic bacterial load and weight compared to controls. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: Extracted Brucella cell surface protein (BCSP) used alone or in combination with other proteins or PKLPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP20 subunit vaccine
c_description: Subcomponent protein recovered from Brucella abortus strain 19 cell surface. Efficacy: BCSP20 was immunogenic and partially protective; protection thought to be due to associated immunogenic BCSP fraction. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: BCSP20 used alone or combined with other proteins or PKLPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 Cu-Zn SOD HtrA two-component systems subunit vaccine
c_description: Early vaccine development studies included a subunit vaccine prepared by salt extraction of B. abortus. Efficacy: Antigenicity was not predictive of subunit vaccine effectiveness; no clear correlation with protection. [Ref:6889]
c_preparation: Subunit vaccine containing proteins cloned from salt extract and antigenic or virulence-related proteins.
c_antigen: BCSP31; Cu-Zn SOD; HtrA; two-component systems

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The BCSP31 gene encoding a 31-kDa salt-extractable immunogenic protein was deleted from Brucella abortus strains by replacement with an antibiotic resistance marker gene. [Ref:6942]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strains with BCSP31 gene deletion constructed by electroporation and recombination; antibiotic-resistant transformants isolated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to construct a DNA vaccine encoding the antigenic surface protein BCSP31 of Brucella abortus to control brucellosis, a highly contagious zoonotic disease with high prevalence in Pakistan. Efficacy: The vaccinated groups showed significantly higher IgG titers in a dose-dependent manner compared to control. The DNA vaccine provided a log unit protection of 3.02 against Brucella abortus challenge in rabbits. [Ref:7113]
c_preparation: The BCSP31 gene was cloned into pTZ57 R/T vector, subcloned into pET-28a vector, expressed in E. coli BL21, and the purified protein was used for immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 Omp3b SOD recombinant vector live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Recombinant vector vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A live, attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vaccine candidate was constructed to express BCSP31, Omp3b, and SOD proteins of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization with the vaccine candidate significantly reduced Brucella abortus strain 544 colonization in spleen (<10^3 CFU), indicating effective protection. [Ref:7065]
c_preparation: Mixture of three delivery strains of live, attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium expressing the three Brucella abortus proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 Omp3b SOD recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to establish proof-of-concept for protective efficacy of a Salmonella-based Brucella abortus vaccine candidate in Beagles. Efficacy: Following challenge, the vaccine reduced bacterial isolation from multiple lymph nodes and organs compared to vector control; some vaccinated Beagles showed no bacterial isolates in tested tissues, indicating partial protection. [Ref:7109]
c_preparation: A mixture of three live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium delivery strains, each expressing one of the recombinant Brucella abortus proteins BCSP31, Omp3b, or superoxide dismutase (SOD), was used for subcutaneous vaccination.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 Omp3b superoxide dismutase recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Attenuated Salmonella strains expressing Brucella abortus BCSP31, Omp3b, and superoxide dismutase proteins were developed as vaccine candidates to protect against brucellosis. Efficacy: The highest dose group (1.2 × 10^6 CFU/mL) showed significantly increased immune responses and complete clearance of challenge strain from spleen, indicating effective protection. [Ref:7087]
c_preparation: A mixture of three recombinant Salmonella strains expressing the three Brucella abortus proteins was prepared at various doses for intraperitoneal immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 recombinant vector live attenuated vaccine using Salmonella choleraesuis strain chi 3781
c_type: Recombinant vector vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: An attenuated Salmonella choleraesuis strain chi 3781 mutant [delta cya-12 delta(crp-cdt)19] was engineered to express the 31-kDa protein (BCSP31) from Brucella abortus via plasmid pBA31-R7 for oral immunization. Efficacy: The recombinant Salmonella choleraesuis vaccine colonized gut mucosa and deep tissues in mice and swine; mice developed serum antibodies to BCSP31 and Salmonella endotoxin, while swine showed strong DTH responses to BCSP31 and Salmonella antigens but no significant antibody responses. [Ref:7342]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella choleraesuis chi 3781 mutant carrying recombinant plasmid pBA31-R7 expressing Brucella abortus BCSP31 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 recombinant vector vaccine using Salmonella typhimurium chi 4064
c_description: An attenuated Salmonella typhimurium chi 4064 mutant was used as a carrier for a recombinant plasmid pBA31-R7 coding for the Brucella abortus 31-kDa protein (BCSP31) to orally immunize swine. Efficacy: Orally immunized swine developed serum and intestinal antibody responses to BCSP31 and salmonella endotoxin; however, they did not develop delayed-type hypersensitivity or blastogenic responses to BCSP31. Parenteral immunization with BCSP31 plus Freund incomplete adjuvant did induce delayed-type hypersensitivity. [Ref:6936]
c_preparation: Oral administration of S. typhimurium chi 4064 carrying plasmid pBA31-R7 expressing BCSP31 protein; no adjuvant used.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BCSP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Subcomponent protein recovered from Brucella abortus strain 19 cell surface. Efficacy: BCSP31 was immunogenic and partially protective; protection attributed to associated immunogenic BCSP fraction. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: BCSP31 used alone or combined with other proteins or PKLPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus betB deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study investigated a betB deletion mutant constructed from virulent Brucella abortus 544 as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The betB mutant was predominantly cleared from mouse spleens after 2 weeks post-infection and vaccination with the live betB mutant provided effective protection against challenge with the virulent wild-type strain. [Ref:7001]
c_preparation: Live betB deletion mutant strain of Brucella abortus.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BLS recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine uses an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain as a vector to deliver the Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) antigen to goats. Efficacy: Vaccinated goats showed significantly higher interferon-γ production compared to vector control; reduced Brucella colonization in tissues; decreased Brucella antigen expression in spleen, kidney, and lymph nodes; amelioration of brucellosis-related histopathological lesions. [Ref:7187]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain expressing BLS at 5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL in 1 mL.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus bp26 and trigger factor DNA vaccine
c_description: Bison were vaccinated with eukaryotic DNA expression vectors encoding Brucella periplasmic protein bp26 and chaperone protein trigger factor (TF) to understand immune responses in wildlife where current vaccines are ineffective. Efficacy: DNA-vaccinated bison developed enhanced antibody, proliferative T cell, and IFN-γ responses compared to controls; increased percentages of CD4(+) and CD8(+) T lymphocytes observed. [Ref:6967]
c_preparation: DNA vaccines encoding bp26 and TF administered intramuscularly with CpG adjuvant at weeks 0, 2, and 4.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BP26 Omp25 L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study addresses the limitations of current Brucella abortus vaccines strain 19 and RB51, which pose risks of virulence and attenuation reversal, and explores a safer alternative using a combined subunit vaccine of three B. abortus immunogens. Efficacy: The combined subunit vaccinated mice showed superior protection (log10 reduction in bacterial load) against virulent B. abortus 544 compared to individual antigen vaccines, though protection was less than that conferred by B. abortus strain 19 vaccine. [Ref:7152]
c_preparation: A combined subunit vaccine comprising the BP26, Omp25, and L7/L12 antigens of Brucella abortus.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BP26 protein vaccine
c_description: A 26-kDa periplasmic protein (BP26) was cloned from Brucella abortus strain 19 genome and characterized; it is a novel protein with no similarity to previously sequenced genes. [Ref:7350]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BP26 RNA vaccine
c_description: This study developed novel mRNA vaccines targeting the outer membrane protein BP26 of Brucella abortus using lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA (BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP). Efficacy: The BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine induced significantly stronger humoral and cellular immune responses than alum-adjuvanted protein vaccines and markedly reduced splenic bacterial load after challenge. [Ref:7272]
c_preparation: Lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA vaccine encoding BP26 fused with Fc (BP26-Fc mRNA-LNP).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Brucella melitensis outer membrane proteins (OMPs) with molecular masses of 10 kDa 16.5 kDa 19 kDa 25-27 kDa 31-34 kDa 36-38 kDa (porin) and 89 kDa vaccine
c_description: The study identified seven surface-exposed outer membrane proteins of Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis using monoclonal antibodies generated by immunizing mice with SDS-insoluble fractions, cell walls, or whole bacterial cells. The accessibility of these proteins on rough and smooth strains was characterized, highlighting the impact of lipopolysaccharide O side chains on protein exposure relevant to vaccine development. [Ref:6922]
c_antigen: outer membrane proteins (OMPs) with molecular masses of 10 kDa, 16.5 kDa, 19 kDa, 25-27 kDa, 31-34 kDa, 36-38 kDa (porin), and 89 kDa

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BspH subunit vaccine
c_description: The secreted effector protein BspH was cloned, expressed, and purified as a recombinant protein (rBspH) to assess its immunocompetence. Efficacy: Immunization with rBspH conferred significant protection against subsequent challenge with B. abortus A19. [Ref:7288]
c_preparation: Recombinant BspH protein used for immunization; adjuvant use not reported.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus BvrR DNA vaccine
c_description: A recombinant plasmid pCDNA-BvrR was constructed by inserting the BvrR gene fragment into a pCDNA3.0 vector to evaluate immunogenicity and protective efficacy. Efficacy: The DNA vaccine pCDNA-BvrR induced a significant level of protection in BALB/c mice as shown by systemic bacterial clearance after challenge with B. abortus S19. [Ref:7117]
c_preparation: DNA vaccine encoding the BvrR gene; recombinant His6-tagged BvrR protein was expressed and purified for verification.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus bvrS/bvrR mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The bvrS/bvrR mutant is markedly attenuated while keeping a smooth lipopolysaccharide (S-LPS) and was previously shown to be attenuated. Efficacy: The bvrS mutant alone protected against virulent B. abortus but less effectively than when combined with the wbkA mutant; combination provided better protection than B. abortus strain 19 vaccine. [Ref:6914]
c_preparation: Live bvrS/bvrR mutant cells used alone or in combination with wbkA mutant or inactivated bvrS cells or purified S-LPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell surface protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated immune and protective responses induced by various concentrations of Brucella cell surface protein administered as a single or multiple inoculations. Efficacy: Protective and immune responses were dose-dependent up to an optimal concentration; higher doses decreased protection; enhanced secondary protection occurred only with suboptimal primary doses; additive protection observed with suboptimal doses in both inoculations. [Ref:6935]
c_preparation: Various concentrations of Brucella cell surface protein were used for primary and secondary inoculations.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall antigen subunit vaccine
c_description: Three major cell-wall antigen bands were isolated from Brucella abortus cell walls after SDS treatment and lysozyme hydrolysis. Efficacy: The three isolated antigen bands provided protection in mice at a level comparable to the killed whole-cell Brucella melitensis H38 reference vaccine. [Ref:7318]
c_preparation: The isolated antigen bands were injected subcutaneously into mice using Freund incomplete adjuvant.
c_antigen: three cell-wall antigens of apparent molecular weights 37000, 25000, 15000

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall fraction F8 inactivated vaccine
c_description: Experimental vaccine composed of a fraction of the bacterial cell-wall (F8) extracted from Brucella abortus 99. Efficacy: Level of primary immunity depended on dose, presence of oil adjuvant, and age of mouse; immunity with adjuvant continued beyond first month, peaked around fourth month, and remained stable for at least 7 months; booster injection reinforced immunity but did not increase it beyond a certain level. [Ref:6867]
c_preparation: Fraction F8 with or without oil adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall fraction F8 subunit vaccine
c_description: A cell wall fraction (F8) extracted by boiling sodium dodecylsulfate at 4% from Brucella abortus 99S was used as vaccine antigen. Efficacy: Protection was dose-dependent; 100 MOD of F8 gave about 35% protection (infected 46%), less effective than H38 vaccine at equivalent doses. [Ref:6876]
c_preparation: F8 fraction formulated with oil adjuvant at doses equivalent to 1 x 10^9 and 1 x 10^10 bacteria, administered once or twice at 3 month intervals.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall fraction PG subunit vaccine
c_description: Mice were vaccinated intravenously with a cell-wall fraction (PG) from Brucella abortus. Efficacy: Immune serum and splenic cells from vaccinated mice strongly reduced splenic infection over time; combined transfer showed additive effect only transiently at 2-3 weeks post-challenge when serum was injected after challenge; no additive or antagonistic effect after 21 days; liver infection not notably modified until 21 days when both helped reduce infection. [Ref:7129]
c_preparation: Cell-wall fraction (PG) from Brucella abortus used as vaccine antigen; no adjuvant mentioned.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus PG-F8 cell wall peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: The cell wall peptidoglycan fraction (PG-F8) extracted from Brucella abortus was tested as a unique antigen. Efficacy: PG-F8 conferred good dose-dependent immunity in mice. [Ref:7321]
c_preparation: Purified cell wall peptidoglycan fraction with or without oil adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cell wall subunit vaccine
c_description: Mice were vaccinated with a Brucella cell-wall fraction to induce immune protection. Efficacy: Immune serum increased the dose required to infect 50% of placentae by 50 to 70 times, decreased splenic and placental infection levels, and increased placental barrier effect protecting fetuses. Immune spleen cells restricted placental and fetal colonization frequency, decreased infection levels in spleen, placenta, and fetus, and increased barrier effect; separated B- and T-cells were less effective, especially on fetal infection. [Ref:7134]
c_preparation: Vaccine consisted of a Brucella cell-wall fraction; no adjuvant information reported.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 chemically modified salt-extractable protein (dCSP) subunit vaccine
c_description: Beef heifers were vaccinated on Day 0 with chemically modified salt-extractable protein (dCSP) from Brucella abortus Strain 19 in Freund's complete adjuvant; a booster was given six weeks later with either homologous or heterologous vaccine. Efficacy: No significant protection observed; 60 to 83% of vaccinated heifers aborted and 70-83% were culture positive after challenge, similar to controls [Ref:7133]
c_preparation: dCSP formulated with Freund's complete adjuvant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus CobB subunit vaccine
c_description: Due to drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines, screening of Brucella protective antigens as subunit vaccine candidates was focused on; CobB was identified as a protein stimulating strong IFN-γ responses and protective efficacy. Efficacy: Mice immunized with CobB plus adjuvant showed protection against virulent B. abortus infection comparable to licensed vaccine S19 and Cu-Zn SOD antigen. [Ref:2099]
c_preparation: Recombinant CobB protein plus adjuvant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus combined DNA vaccine
c_description: The study investigated whether co-delivery of the IL-15 gene with a combined DNA vaccine enhances immune response against Brucella abortus in mice. Efficacy: DNA-IL-15(+) immunization enhanced protection against Brucella infection predominantly mediated by CD8+ T cells, with contribution from CD4+ T cells. [Ref:2289]
c_preparation: A combined DNA vaccine delivered together with the IL-15 gene plasmid (DNA-IL-15(+)).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus conjugate vaccine using V3 loop peptide
c_description: Heat-inactivated Brucella abortus was used as a carrier conjugated with a 14-mer V3 loop peptide homologous to HIV-1 MN V3 loop. Efficacy: Sera from immunized mice blocked syncytium formation between CD4+ CEM cells and HIV-infected H9 cells; effective even after CD4+ T-cell depletion. [Ref:7328]
c_preparation: Conjugate of heat-inactivated Brucella abortus with V3 loop peptide.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase and interleukin-18 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the prophylactic potential of a liposome-based DNA vaccine co-expressing Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) against experimental murine brucellosis. Efficacy: Co-expression of IL-18 with SOD resulted in higher lymphoproliferative response and IFN-gamma production compared to immunization with free form SOD-DNA, indicating enhanced protection potential. [Ref:6931]
c_preparation: Liposome-mediated delivery of DNA constructs pVsod (encoding SOD of Brucella abortus) and pVIL18-sod (encoding mouse IL-18 and SOD of Brucella abortus) using Escherichia coli lipid liposome (escheriosome) as the delivery vehicle.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase DNA vaccine fused to IL-2
c_description: The study evaluated a DNA vaccine expressing a fusion protein of Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase antigen and IL-2 to enhance immune response and protection. Efficacy: Both DNA vaccines induced SOD-specific antibody and cytotoxic T cell responses; pSecTag-SOD-IL2 induced higher IFN-gamma but lower T cell proliferation compared to pSecTag-SOD; increased resistance to B. abortus challenge was observed with pSecTag-SOD-IL2 but not statistically significant compared to pSecTag-SOD. [Ref:6915]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA encoding a secretory fusion protein of SOD and IL-2 (pSecTag-SOD-IL2) compared to plasmid encoding SOD alone (pSecTag-SOD).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD recombinant Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is based on recombinant Lactococcus lactis secreting Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) used as an oral antigen delivery system. Efficacy: Vaccinated animals were protected against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308; protection was mildly improved with co-administration of IL-12 expressing L. lactis. [Ref:6972]
c_preparation: Oral administration of Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 transformed with pSEC derivatives encoding SOD.

c_vaccine_name: Escheriosome-encapsulated Brucella abortus Cu-Zn SOD subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to investigate the immunogenic potential of fusogenic liposomes (escheriosomes) encapsulated recombinant Cu-Zn SOD protein alone or combined with recombinant IL-18. Efficacy: Immunization with liposome-encapsulated rSOD alone or combined with rIL-18 increased resistance in mice against challenge with B. abortus 544. [Ref:6966]
c_preparation: Recombinant Cu-Zn SOD protein encapsulated in fusogenic liposomes (escheriosomes).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase synthetic peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: Three synthetic peptides based on the amino acid sequence of Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase were selected for their predicted hydrophilicity, flexibility, and antigenicity and used as vaccines singly or in combination with or without monophosphoryl lipid A adjuvant. Efficacy: Peptide 3 plus monophosphoryl lipid A afforded a 2 log reduction in bacterial load; peptide 3 without adjuvant afforded 1 log reduction; peptides 1 and 2 and recombinant SOD vaccine afforded no protection; salt-extractable proteins vaccine afforded 3 log reduction. [Ref:7325]
c_preparation: Peptides 1, 2, and 3 administered singly or combined, with or without monophosphoryl lipid A adjuvant.
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase synthetic peptides (peptide 1, peptide 2, peptide 3)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase DNA vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA vaccine encoding Brucella abortus Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase. Efficacy: The DNA vaccine induced a strong, significant level of protection against challenge with B. abortus strain 2308, comparable to protection induced by B. abortus vaccine strain RB51. [Ref:564]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA carrying the SOD gene (pcDNA-SOD) administered by intramuscular injection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus pcDNA-SOD DNA vaccine with BPPcysMPEG
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA vaccine encoding Brucella abortus Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase using BPPcysMPEG as an adjuvant. Efficacy: The pcDNA-SOD/BPPcysMPEG formulation induced improved protection against virulent B. abortus 2308 challenge compared to pcDNA-SOD alone. [Ref:7016]
c_preparation: Intranasal coadministration of plasmid pcDNA-SOD with the TLR2/6 agonist adjuvant BPPcysMPEG.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus SFV-SOD recombinant vector RNA vaccine
c_description: Constructed replication-deficient Semliki Forest virus particles carrying recombinant RNA encoding Brucella abortus Cu,Zn superoxide dismutase. Efficacy: SFV-SOD particles induced significant protection in BALB/c mice against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 compared to control virus particles. [Ref:6902]
c_preparation: Recombinant Semliki Forest virus particles (SFV-SOD particles) expressing the SOD protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Immunization with Escherichia coli DH5alpha expressing Brucella abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase induces a protective immune response in mice. Efficacy: Induction of protective immune response previously reported; current study shows induction of specific cytotoxic T cells. [Ref:6920]
c_preparation: Live Escherichia coli DH5alpha expressing Brucella abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase recombinant vector live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Recombinant vector vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Vaccination of mice with live Escherichia coli expressing Brucella Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase induced protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge. Efficacy: Induced a significant level of protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge, though less than that of Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine. [Ref:7358]
c_preparation: Live Escherichia coli expressing Brucella Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) fusion protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase recombinant vector vaccine (vaccinia virus, vUBSOD)
c_description: Genes encoding B. abortus Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase were cloned into shuttle plasmids and transfected into vaccinia virus to develop recombinant vUBSOD. Efficacy: vUBSOD did not induce a humoral immune response against B. abortus proteins. [Ref:7327]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing the 28 kDa protein composed of B. abortus Cu/Zn-SOD and a portion of vaccinia virus TK gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus cysteine synthase A subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant cysteine synthase A (rCysK) of Brucella abortus was generated in Escherichia coli and purified by metal affinity chromatography to homogeneity. Efficacy: Significant protection against virulent B. abortus strain 544 challenge was observed in all rCysK immunized groups compared to PBS control; the best protection was in mice immunized with rCysK plus aluminium hydroxide gel (1.064 units of protection). [Ref:6989]
c_adjuvant: yes; Freund's adjuvant; aluminium hydroxide gel; no
c_preparation: rCysK was formulated with Freund's adjuvant, aluminium hydroxide gel, or without any adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus D15 protein subunit vaccine
Brucella abortus D15 subunit vaccine
c_description: Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with D15 appeared to have some effect on clearance kinetics. [Ref:6965]
c_preparation: Recombinant D15 protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus delta norD delta znuA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine znBAZ was developed by deleting norD and znuA genes from Brucella abortus and inserting lacZ as a marker gene to create a highly attenuated strain. Efficacy: znBAZ was significantly more protective than the conventional RB51 vaccine by more than four orders of magnitude and was completely cleared from mouse spleens within eight weeks post-vaccination. [Ref:7069]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletions in norD and znuA genes and lacZ marker.
c_antigen: norD deletion; znuA deletion; lacZ marker gene

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus delta virB2 vaccine
c_description: The attenuated mutant B. abortusΔvirB2 is a virB2 gene deletion mutant studied as a candidate vaccine. Efficacy: The mutant B. abortusΔvirB2 was progressively killed inside mature osteoclasts, mimicking infection kinetics in macrophages. [Ref:7150]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain B. abortusΔvirB2.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus dihydrolipoamide succinyltransferase subunit vaccine
c_description: The recombinant dihydrolipoamide succinyltransferase (rE2o) of Brucella abortus was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli and purified by metal affinity chromatography. It is immunoreactive with brucellosis positive cattle sera. Efficacy: The rE2o vaccine provided partial protection against challenge with pathogenic Brucella abortus in BALB/c mice. [Ref:6979]
c_adjuvant: yes; Freund's adjuvant and aluminium hydroxide gel
c_preparation: Recombinant rE2o protein formulated with two different adjuvants: Freund's adjuvant and aluminium hydroxide gel.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus double mutant znBAZ live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A newly developed Brucella abortus double mutant (znBAZ) vaccine was used with an oral prime and nasal boost regimen. Efficacy: znBAZ conferred nearly complete protection against pulmonary challenge with wild-type B. abortus 2308, with protective efficacy >2800-fold better than the RB51 vaccine; CD8+ T cells were critical for protection, while CD4+ T cells were not essential in znBAZ-vaccinated mice. [Ref:7151]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant znBAZ administered mucosally (oral prime, nasal boost).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus FlgJ subunit vaccine
c_description: Flagellar proteins of Brucella abortus were screened for protective antigens; FlgJ was identified as a candidate inducing protective immune responses. Efficacy: Immunization with FlgJ plus adjuvant provided protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection in mice. [Ref:6981]
c_preparation: Recombinant his-tagged FlgJ protein expressed in Escherichia coli and purified; administered with adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus FliN subunit vaccine
c_description: Flagellar proteins of Brucella abortus were screened for protective antigens; FliN was identified as a candidate inducing protective immune responses. Efficacy: Immunization with FliN plus adjuvant provided protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection in mice. [Ref:6981]
c_preparation: Recombinant his-tagged FliN protein expressed in Escherichia coli and purified; administered with adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ghost vaccine lysed by GI24 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus cells were lysed by the N-terminal 24-amino acid fragment (GI24) of PMAP-36 to create a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization with the vaccine candidate provided significant protection against systemic infection with virulent B. abortus 544. [Ref:7066]
c_preparation: Vaccine candidate prepared by lysing B. abortus cells with GI24 peptide fragment.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GI24-lysed inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the efficacy of a vaccine candidate composed of Brucella abortus cells lysed by GI24 as a potential vaccine against brucellosis in Korean black goats. Efficacy: Three of five goats immunized with the GI24-lysed vaccine were completely protected against challenge. Group B showed significantly lower infection index and tissue colonization compared to controls. [Ref:7123]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of approximately 3 × 10^9 GI24-lysed Brucella abortus cells administered subcutaneously.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus glucokinase subunit vaccine
c_description: A recombinant subunit vaccine molecule comprising the truncated region of glucokinase (r-glk) gene from Brucella abortus strain 19 was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21DE3 host to engineer a safe and effective vaccine candidate for animals and humans. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed specific antibody titer of 1:64,000 with predominant IgG2a and IgG2b isotypes indicating Th1 response; in vitro cell viability of 81.20% and 78.5% against lethal challenge of Brucella abortus 544 and Brucella melitensis 16M respectively; significantly protected mice after intraperitoneal challenge with no signs of necrosis or vacuolization in liver and spleen tissues compared to controls. [Ref:7015]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant glucokinase protein expressed in E. coli BL21DE3.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate-dehydrogenase DNA vaccine
c_description: The study identified and characterized the Brucella abortus GAPDH gene and expressed it as a recombinant protein. The GAPDH gene was shown to be a single copy in the genome and functionally complemented E. coli gap mutants. Efficacy: Partial protection was induced in mice against experimental Brucella abortus infection when the GAPDH DNA vaccine was co-administered with IL-12 plasmid. [Ref:1484]
c_preparation: DNA vaccine formulation co-administered with a murine interleukin-12-expressing plasmid.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GntR DNA vaccine
c_description: The recombinant DNA vaccine pVGntR was constructed based on the transcriptional regulator GntR of Brucella abortus to improve protective immunity and reduce residual virulence compared to conventional vaccines. Efficacy: pVGntR provided significantly greater protection than the conventional RB51 vaccine against wild-type Brucella abortus challenge. [Ref:7088]
c_preparation: Recombinant DNA plasmid vaccine encoding GntR

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL DNA vaccine
c_description: The GroEL gene from Brucella abortus was amplified and cloned into mammalian expression vectors pCMV-link and pCMV-tPA to create DNA vaccines. Efficacy: Neither immunisation route with the GroEL DNA vaccine induced significant protective immunity against Brucella abortus. [Ref:2292]
c_preparation: Two constructs were made: pCMV-link encoding a non-secreted form of GroEL and pCMV-tPA encoding a secreted form; the pCMV-link construct produced higher protein levels.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL/GroES/HtrA baculovirus-expressing insect-cell subunit vaccine
c_description: Baculovirus recombinants expressing individual, divalent or trivalent B. abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and/or HtrA were used as immunogens. Efficacy: No protection against B. abortus virulent strain 2308 challenge was observed. [Ref:6885]
c_preparation: Protein-expressing whole insect cells combined with complete Freund's adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus purified recombinant GroEL/GroES/HtrA subunit vaccine
c_description: Purified recombinant B. abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and/or HtrA were administered. Efficacy: No protection against B. abortus virulent strain 2308 challenge was observed. [Ref:6885]
c_preparation: Purified proteins combined with Ribi adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL recombinant vector and subunit vaccine
c_description: Mice primed with vaccinia virus-GroEL recombinant and boosted with purified GroEL combined with Ribi adjuvant. Efficacy: No protective immunity was induced. [Ref:6885]
c_preparation: Vaccinia virus recombinant prime followed by purified protein plus Ribi adjuvant boost.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL baculovirus recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop genetically engineered Brucella abortus vaccines by cloning and expressing heat shock protein genes GroEL, GroES, and HtrA using the BAC-TO-BAC Baculovirus System. [Ref:6872]
c_preparation: Recombinant baculoviruses expressing Brucella abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and HtrA were produced in insect cell lines (Sf9 and Trichoplusia ni) under optimized conditions for protein expression.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL vaccinia recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The groEL gene encoding the antigenic heat shock protein GroEL from Brucella abortus was subcloned into vaccinia virus via homologous recombination and expression was confirmed by Western blotting. Efficacy: No significant level of protection was demonstrable despite induction of specific antibodies. [Ref:6873]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing Brucella abortus GroEL protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL Lactococcus lactis recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study explores a safer vaccination strategy against Brucella abortus by using Lactococcus lactis as a food-grade live vector to deliver the GroEL heat-shock protein antigen. [Ref:6916]
c_preparation: Genetically modified Lactococcus lactis strains producing Brucella abortus GroEL protein, either intracellularly or secreted; only the secreted form was stably produced.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroEL subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Brucella abortus GroEL protein produced and purified for evaluation as a vaccine antigen. Efficacy: Not directly reported; induced Th1-type immune responses and DTH reactions. [Ref:7353]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein expressed in E. coli and purified by affinity chromatography.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroES recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop genetically engineered Brucella abortus vaccines by cloning and expressing heat shock protein genes GroEL, GroES, and HtrA using the BAC-TO-BAC Baculovirus System. [Ref:6872]
c_preparation: Recombinant baculoviruses expressing Brucella abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and HtrA were produced in insect cell lines (Sf9 and Trichoplusia ni) under optimized conditions for protein expression.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus GroES subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Brucella abortus GroES protein produced and purified for evaluation as a vaccine antigen. Efficacy: Not directly reported; induced Th1-type immune responses and DTH reactions. [Ref:7353]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein expressed in E. coli and purified by affinity chromatography.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus heat-inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study investigates heat-inactivated Brucella abortus as a potential vaccine candidate capable of inducing a strong cellular immune response associated with IFN-gamma production and cytotoxic T-cell development. Efficacy: Heat-inactivated B. abortus induced IL-12 secretion by monocytes, which enhanced IFN-gamma mRNA expression in T cells and increased NK cell cytolytic activity, indicating potential for directing immune response towards Th1-Tc1 differentiation. [Ref:7351]
c_preparation: Heat-inactivated whole Brucella abortus bacteria were used to stimulate human monocytes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus HlyD subunit vaccine
c_description: HlyD was selected as a conserved antigen candidate from compositive reverse vaccinology screening Efficacy: HlyD substantially reduced the organ bacterial load of B. abortus S19 in mice and provided varying degrees of protection [Ref:7192]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Hsp60 peptide PEP1 vaccine
c_description: A novel PrPC-binding peptide, PEP1, derived from Brucella abortus Hsp60 was identified through computational docking and structure-guided approaches to target receptor-mediated mucosal antigen uptake. Efficacy: Fusion of PEP1 to a model protein resulted in increased mucosal IgA and systemic IgG responses compared to the untargeted protein. [Ref:7295]
c_preparation: PEP1 was fused to a model protein to enable receptor-mediated targeting to intestinal M-cell-associated regions.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus hsp60 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study suggests that hsp60 is a highly immunogenic heat shock protein produced by Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis, with higher production in B. abortus. The lower production of hsp60 by B. melitensis may contribute to its greater virulence. The authors propose hsp60 as a good antigenic candidate for engineering a subunit vaccine against Brucella. [Ref:6933]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus HtrA baculovirus recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop genetically engineered Brucella abortus vaccines by cloning and expressing heat shock protein genes GroEL, GroES, and HtrA using the BAC-TO-BAC Baculovirus System. [Ref:6872]
c_preparation: Recombinant baculoviruses expressing Brucella abortus heat shock proteins GroEL, GroES, and HtrA were produced in insect cell lines (Sf9 and Trichoplusia ni) under optimized conditions for protein expression.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 inactivated cell envelope vaccine
c_description: Cell envelopes from virulent strain 2308 were used as nonliving vaccine antigens administered with various adjuvants. Efficacy: Equivalent protection at 1 week post-infection regardless of adjuvant used. [Ref:414]
c_adjuvant: yes; phosphate-buffered saline, incomplete Freund adjuvant, or trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Cell envelopes administered in phosphate-buffered saline, incomplete Freund adjuvant, or TDM and MDP adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus inactivated oil adjuvant vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an experimentally developed inactivated oil adjuvant Brucella abortus vaccine in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced spleen weight and bacterial load compared to unvaccinated controls after challenge (p < 0.001), indicating protective efficacy. [Ref:7268]
c_preparation: The vaccine contained 1.5 × 10^7 inactivated Brucella abortus biovar 3 cells per 0.1 ml dose with an oil adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the immune response of sheep to intestinal infusion of killed Brucella abortus cells. [Ref:7320]
c_preparation: Killed (inactivated) Brucella abortus cells administered via intestinal infusion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus killed vaccine with T150R1 block-polymer adjuvant
c_description: Chickens were injected subcutaneously at one day of age with oil-in-water emulsions containing the nonionic block polymer T150R1. Efficacy: Chickens treated with T150R1 polymer developed higher IgM antibody titers to sheep erythrocytes and killed Brucella abortus compared to untreated controls. [Ref:6899]
c_preparation: Oil-in-water emulsions of the nonionic block polymer T150R1 combined with killed Brucella abortus antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus inactivated vaccine conjugated with HIV-1 gp120 V3 loop peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was developed by conjugating an 18-amino-acid peptide from the V3 loop of HIV-1 gp120 to inactivated Brucella abortus to induce HIV-specific immune responses. Efficacy: The vaccine induced virus-specific cytotoxic T-lymphocyte responses recognizing naturally processed HIV envelope epitopes; CTL priming occurred even in CD4+ T-cell depleted mice. [Ref:7346]
c_preparation: Conjugate of inactivated Brucella abortus organisms with an 18-amino-acid peptide from the HIV-1 MN strain gp120 V3 loop.
c_antigen: 18-amino-acid peptide from the V3 loop of HIV-1 gp120 (MN strain)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus inactivated whole cell, cell envelope, or outer membrane protein vaccine
c_description: Various nonliving antigen preparations from strain 2308 were tested with or without adjuvants. Efficacy: Equivalent protection observed with all antigen preparations and adjuvant conditions. [Ref:414]
c_adjuvant: yes; phosphate-buffered saline or trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Killed whole cells, cell envelopes, or outer membrane proteins administered in phosphate-buffered saline or with TDM and MDP adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus influenza viral vector recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study explored increasing protective efficacy of the novel influenza viral vector based Brucella abortus vaccine (Flu-BA) in pregnant heifers by simultaneous subcutaneous and conjunctival administration. Efficacy: Provided protection from abortion (88.8%), infection of heifers (100%), and fetuses/calves (100%) compared to negative control. [Ref:7068]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector based vaccine administered concurrently via conjunctival and subcutaneous routes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus influenza viral vector vaccine expressing L7/L12 and Omp16
c_description: A novel influenza viral vector Brucella abortus vaccine expressing ribosomal proteins L7/L12 or Omp16 was created to provide cross-protection against Brucella melitensis in cattle. Efficacy: Provided 100% protection against abortion in vaccinated pregnant heifers and 90-100% cross-protection of heifers and their calves or fetuses after challenge with B. melitensis 16M; protection comparable to commercial B. abortus strain 19 vaccine; significant reduction in infection and colonization indices in tissues (P=0.02 to P<0.0001). [Ref:7038]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus L7/L12 or Omp16 proteins formulated with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 hot-SDS-insoluble cell-envelope fraction (PG) subunit vaccine
c_description: A vaccine (PG) composed of the insoluble residue of strain 2308 cell envelopes extracted with hot sodium dodecyl sulfate was compared to native cell envelope vaccines. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with PG showed protective immunity equivalent to native cell envelope vaccine; in cattle, PG without adjuvant induced negligible immune responses; revaccination with PG in adjuvant enhanced antibody production. [Ref:7136]
c_adjuvant: yes; oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Vaccines were administered by injection in an oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide or without adjuvant.
c_antigen: insoluble residue of cell envelopes; porin; group 3 proteins; O polysaccharide

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus killed cells inactivated vaccine
c_description: Vaccination with killed cells of Brucella abortus evoked cross-reacting antibodies in guinea pigs. Efficacy: Only the homologous antigen (Brucella abortus killed cells) effectively produced protective immunity to Brucella abortus in guinea pigs. [Ref:6881]
c_preparation: Killed cells preparation

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus killed vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was developed to address brucellosis in wildlife reservoirs, particularly elk, where no effective vaccines currently exist. Efficacy: Demonstrated protection in mice equal to RB51 vaccine; partial protection observed in elk. [Ref:7130]
c_preparation: Killed Brucella abortus vaccine compounded with montmorillonite clay as a carrying agent for mucosal delivery.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus HSA-L7/L12 and lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the protection of a combination of recombinant HSA-L7/L12 fusion protein with LPS in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: The combination of tHSA-L7/L12 fusion protein with LPS and B. abortus S19 induced higher protection against virulent B. abortus 544 challenge than other groups (P = 0.005). [Ref:6956]
c_preparation: Recombinant HSA-L7/L12 fusion protein expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and purified by affinity chromatography; LPS extracted by n-butanol and purified by ultracentrifugation; combined for immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 and Omp16 H5N1/H1N1 influenza recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study presents a new candidate vector vaccine against Brucella abortus consisting of recombinant influenza A viruses expressing Brucella L7/L12 and Omp16 proteins. Efficacy: The vaccine provided a high level of protectiveness against B. abortus infection comparable to the commercial B. abortus strain 19 vaccine and superior to the strain 19 vaccine combined with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant. [Ref:7005]
c_preparation: A bivalent vaccine formulation composed of a mixture of recombinant influenza A subtype H5N1 and H1N1 viruses expressing Brucella L7/L12 and Omp16 proteins, combined with adjuvants Montanide Gel01 or chitosan to increase effectiveness.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study tested nucleic acid vaccination using the Brucella abortus ribosomal L7/L12 gene expressed in muscle cells of mice. Efficacy: Mice inoculated with pcDNA3-encoded L7/L12 gene showed significant protection against B. abortus S2308 infection; p6-L7/L12 did not confer significant protection compared to positive controls. [Ref:2290]
c_preparation: The L7/L12 gene was delivered via eukaryotic expression plasmids pcDNA3 (human CMV promoter) and p6 (bovine MHC 1 promoter) by single intramuscular injection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 OMP22 OMP25 OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Four recombinant proteins (L7/L12, OMP22, OMP25, OMP31) were cloned, expressed, purified, and combined as a subunit vaccine to evaluate protective efficiency against B. abortus infection. Efficacy: The combined subunit vaccine induced significantly higher protection in mice against brucellosis compared to single subunit vaccines and showed protection comparable to the RB51 vaccine. [Ref:7200]
c_preparation: Combined subunit vaccine composed of four recombinant Brucella abortus proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy of a divalent fusion protein comprising L7/L12 and Omp25 antigens of Brucella abortus in the presence of murine IFN-gamma. Efficacy: The vaccine candidate alone provided significant protection (log protection unit 2.16, p=0.0001) against B. abortus 544; co-administration with IFN-gamma enhanced protection (log protection unit 2.4, p=0.0001). Minimal or no therapeutic effect was observed when administered with IFN-gamma post-infection. [Ref:7110]
c_preparation: A recombinant fusion protein of L7/L12 and Omp25 was used alone or in combination with recombinant murine IFN-gamma.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 recombinant vector live attenuated vaccine using Salmonella Typhimurium
c_type: Recombinant vector vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study employed the Brucella abortus L7/L12 antigen cloned into a prokaryotic expression vector under a beta-lactamase secretory signal and transformed into an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain to deliver the antigen. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant reduction in Brucella colonization in spleen and liver tissues after challenge with virulent B. abortus compared to controls. [Ref:7153]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain JOL1800 (∆lon, ∆cpxR, ∆asd, and ∆rfaL) transformed with plasmid pJHL65::L7/L12 secreting the L7/L12 antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Lactococcus lactis recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study introduces the concept of using food-grade lactic acid bacteria (Lactococcus lactis) as a carrier for the Brucella abortus ribosomal protein L7/L12 antigen to develop oral live vaccines against brucellosis. [Ref:6880]
c_preparation: The L7/L12 gene was expressed in Lactococcus lactis under a nisin-inducible promoter, producing the antigen in cytoplasmic, secreted, and cell-wall-anchored forms using different signal peptides and fusion constructs to enhance yield and targeting.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 vaccinia recombinant vector vaccine (WRL7/L12)
c_description: The Brucella abortus L7/L12 gene encoding ribosomal protein L7/L12 was cloned into vaccinia virus by homologous recombination to produce the WRL7/L12 recombinant. Efficacy: Mice inoculated with WRL7/L12 produced antibodies specific to vaccinia virus and L7/L12 antigens but were not protected against virulent Brucella abortus 2308 challenge. [Ref:6903]
c_preparation: Recombinant vaccinia virus expressing Brucella abortus L7/L12 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 Flu-NS1-124 H5N1/H1N1 influenza recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Novel candidate vaccines were generated based on recombinant influenza A viruses expressing Brucella ribosomal protein L7/L12 from the NS1 open reading frame. Efficacy: Highest antibody response to Brucella antigen was observed with L7/L12 expressing constructs; protective efficacy in guinea pigs was comparable to commercial live B. abortus strain 19 vaccine. [Ref:7007]
c_preparation: Four recombinant influenza A viral constructs of subtypes H5N1 or H1N1 expressing L7/L12 were produced; mono- or bivalent vaccine formulations administered via prime-boost intranasal, conjunctival, or subcutaneous immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 and Omp16 influenza recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study introduces a novel influenza viral vector vaccine expressing Brucella ribosomal L7/L12 or Omp16 proteins combined with the adjuvant Montanide Gel01, designed for immunization of pregnant heifers. Efficacy: The vector vaccine provided good protection against Brucella abortus 544 infection, preventing abortion and reducing infection indices in heifers and their fetuses or calves; protection was comparable to commercial vaccines Brucella abortus strain 19 and strain RB51. [Ref:7017]
c_preparation: Influenza A viral vector expressing Brucella L7/L12 or Omp16 proteins formulated with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 ribosomal protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Ribosomal preparations have been used as vaccines against several pathogens including B. abortus, conferring a high degree of protection. Efficacy: Not directly reported; inferred protection based on induction of Th1 response. [Ref:7330]
c_preparation: Recombinant L7/L12 ribosomal protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 SOmp2b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study designed a fusion protein combining L7/L12 and SOmp2b antigens, both conserved and immunogenic in Brucella pathogens, as a potential vaccine candidate. [Ref:7102]
c_preparation: The fusion protein L7/L12-SOmp2b was cloned into pET28a vector and expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3), then purified using Ni-NTA column.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: The Brucella abortus L7/L12 ribosomal gene was amplified and expressed as a fusion protein in E. coli, purified, and confirmed by Western blot. [Ref:7331]
c_preparation: Recombinant L7/L12 fusion protein purified by affinity chromatography.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus liposomal L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study addresses limitations of current vaccines such as short-term immunity and hypersensitivity; it evaluates a liposomal form of recombinant ribosomal L7/L12 protein as a candidate vaccine. Efficacy: Liposomal rL7/L12 vaccine showed better systemic clearance of bacterial load after challenge compared to free antigen and standard S-19 vaccine. [Ref:6924]
c_preparation: Recombinant L7/L12 protein encapsulated in liposomes; compared to free antigen and IFA-L7/L12 combination.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide (LPS) epitopes including O-polysaccharide (A and C) core oligosaccharide (R1 and R2) lipid A (LA1 LA2 LA3) lipid A-associated outer membrane protein (LAOmp3-1 and LAOmp3-2) vaccine
c_antigen: lipopolysaccharide (LPS) epitopes including O-polysaccharide (A and C), core oligosaccharide (R1 and R2), lipid A (LA1, LA2, LA3), lipid A-associated outer membrane protein (LAOmp3-1 and LAOmp3-2)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide Neisseria meningitidis outer membrane vesicle conjugate subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop an efficacious vaccine against brucellosis using antigenic determinants of Brucella cell wall, specifically LPS, conjugated to Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B OMV as a carrier protein. Efficacy: The LPS-OMV conjugate induced the highest anti-LPS IgG titers, approximately 5-fold and 1.3-fold higher than LPS alone and LPS + OMV noncovalent complex, respectively, with a 100-120-fold rise of anti-LPS IgG in mice after the third injection. [Ref:7026]
c_preparation: Brucella abortus LPS was conjugated to Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B outer membrane vesicle (OMV) using carbodiimide and adipic acid-mediated coupling and linking.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide Neisseria meningitidis outer membrane vesicle noncovalent complex subunit vaccine
c_description: A noncovalent complex of Brucella abortus LPS and Neisseria meningitidis OMV was evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The LPS + OMV complex induced higher IgG titers than LPS alone but lower than the conjugated LPS-OMV vaccine. [Ref:7026]
c_preparation: LPS combined with OMV without covalent conjugation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and O-polysaccharide (OPS) antigens were extracted from a pathogenic strain of Brucella abortus and encapsulated within multilamellar liposome vesicles to evaluate their effectiveness as vaccine carriers. Efficacy: Liposome-encapsulated LPS and OPS induced significantly higher and more sustained IgG antibody levels compared to free antigens; multiple injections of liposome-encapsulated OPS improved its immunogenicity. [Ref:6893]
c_preparation: LPS and OPS antigens encapsulated within multilamellar liposomes; compared to free LPS and OPS antigens.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide vaccine
c_description: Formaldehyde fixation of Salmonella typhimurium LPS to ribosomes purified from Brucella abortus was used to induce an immune response. Efficacy: The complex induced a primary IgM response and upon revaccination elevated IgM titers and induced IgG antibodies to the O antigens of LPS. [Ref:7263]
c_preparation: LPS complexed with Brucella abortus ribosomes (heterologous ribosomal particles).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus TNP-conjugated lipopolysaccharide carrier vaccine
c_description: The study investigates the carrier nature of lipopolysaccharide from Brucella abortus (LPS-BA) in evoking humoral immune responses, suggesting that LPS-BA can substitute for whole Brucella abortus organisms in vaccine development. Efficacy: TNP-LPS-BA generated anti-TNP antibody responses in various mouse strains including immunodeficient mice, with higher titers of IgG1, IgG2a, and IgG2b antibodies in C3H/HeJ mice compared to TNP-LPS from E. coli; LPS-BA stimulated B cells more effectively than LPS-EC in C3H/HeJ mice. [Ref:7343]
c_preparation: Trinitrophenyl (TNP)-conjugated LPS from Brucella abortus (TNP-LPS-BA) was used to immunize mice.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus live attenuated vaccine with wbdR acetyl-transferase gene insertion
c_description: The study introduced the wbdR acetyl-transferase gene from Escherichia coli O157:H7 into Brucella abortus chromosome II, generating a modified O-polysaccharide antigenic structure with N-acetyl-perosamine replacing N-formyl-perosamine. Efficacy: The wbdR constructs produced chronic infections in mice and elicited antibody responses distinguishable from wild-type strains, indicating potential for vaccine development. [Ref:7107]
c_preparation: Live Brucella abortus constructs with chromosomal insertion of wbdR gene, some with deletion of the native wbkC formyltransferase gene, producing modified lipopolysaccharide structures.
c_antigen: wbdR acetyl-transferase gene; deletion of wbkC formyltransferase gene

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Lumazine Synthase Spike receptor binding domain subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was designed by covalently coupling the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein to the multimeric Lumazine Synthase protein from Brucella abortus to increase immunogenicity. Efficacy: Particles with a high RBD to BLS ratio (6-7 RBD molecules per BLS decamer) elicited significantly higher humoral immune responses and high titers of neutralizing IgGs compared to RBD alone or particles with lower RBD to BLS ratios. [Ref:7199]
c_preparation: Multimeric particles produced by transpeptidation reaction between RBD expressed in Pichia pastoris and Brucella abortus Lumazine Synthase (BLS), forming decameric 170 kDa particles with varying RBD to BLS ratios.
c_antigen: Lumazine Synthase; Spike receptor binding domain (RBD)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase subunit live attenuated vaccine using Lactococcus lactis vector
