c_description: This study aimed to develop a recombinant Lactococcus lactis live vector secreting Brucella abortus lumazine synthase (BLS) protein as a potential oral vaccine against brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant BLS-specific IgG1 and IgG2a antibody responses compared to controls; increased levels of IFN-γ, TNFα, IL-4, and IL-10 cytokines were observed; vaccinated mice exhibited less severe spleen injuries and reduced inflammatory damage. [Ref:7221]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing and secreting the BLS protein, delivered orally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus lumazine synthase subunit vaccine
c_description: The immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (rBLS) was evaluated in mice. Efficacy: Immunization with rBLS protected mice against challenge with B. abortus 544; protection levels in the spleen were similar across all adjuvants, while only BLS-Al and BLS-IFA were effective in the liver. [Ref:6895]
c_adjuvant: yes; aluminum hydroxide gel; monophosphoryl lipid A; incomplete Freund's adjuvant
c_preparation: rBLS was administered alone or with aluminum hydroxide gel (BLS-Al), monophosphoryl lipid A (BLS-MPA), or incomplete Freund's adjuvant (BLS-IFA).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus malate dehydrogenase and outer membrane proteins 10 and 19 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated a combination vaccine of three recombinant Brucella abortus proteins (Mdh, Omp10, Omp19) loaded into chitosan nanoparticles for intranasal immunization. Efficacy: Increased antigen-specific total IgG, predominantly IgG1; significant increase of anti-Mdh IgA but not anti-Omp IgA; spleenocytes produced significant IFN-γ and IL-4 indicating mixed Th1-Th2 response. [Ref:7143]
c_preparation: Cocktail of recombinant Mdh, Omp10, and Omp19 proteins loaded in chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally.
c_antigen: malate dehydrogenase (Mdh), outer membrane protein 10 (Omp10), outer membrane protein 19 (Omp19)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Mdh chitosan nanoparticle subunit vaccine (CNs-Mdh)
c_description: This study aimed to investigate mucosal immune responses induced by Brucella abortus malate dehydrogenase antigen loaded in mucoadhesive chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally in a BALB/c mouse model. Efficacy: CNs-Mdh induced significantly higher IL-6 production in THP-1 cells compared to controls; in mice, IL-4 and IgG-secreting cells increased significantly at 4 and 6 weeks post-immunization; Mdh-specific IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a antibodies increased with a predominant IgG1 response; mucosal IgA responses were significantly elevated in nasal washes, genital secretions, fecal extracts, and sera compared to controls. [Ref:7125]
c_preparation: Malate dehydrogenase antigen was loaded into mucoadhesive chitosan nanoparticles (CNs-Mdh) for intranasal immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus manB core mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The manB(core) mutant was tested as a rough vaccine candidate in mice. Efficacy: Ineffective as a vaccine against Brucella abortus in mice. [Ref:6890]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough lipopolysaccharide mutant with manB(core) gene disruption.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus manBA deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked deletion mutants of manBA gene in Brucella abortus as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: Provided less protection compared to Deltaasp24 mutants against heterologous challenge. [Ref:700]
c_preparation: Live attenuated unmarked deletion mutant of manBA gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Mdh subunit vaccine
c_description: Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with recombinant Mdh resulted in the most significant reduction in bacterial colonization compared to other antigens tested. [Ref:6965]
c_preparation: Recombinant Mdh protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus membrane blebs subunit vaccine
c_description: Membrane blebs were obtained from Brucella abortus 2308 and analyzed by proteomics to identify proteins including known immunogens. Efficacy: Mice immunized with 2308 membrane blebs showed protective immune responses similar to the Brucella abortus RB51 vaccine control, with significant reduction in spleen CFUs after challenge (P < 0.05). [Ref:7149]
c_preparation: Acellular vaccine composed of membrane blebs derived from Brucella abortus 2308.
c_antigen: SodC; Omp2b; Omp2a; Omp10; Omp16; Omp19

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus membrane fusogenic protein delta live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The Δmfp::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus was evaluated as a live vaccine candidate due to its reduced virulence and persistence in mouse models. Efficacy: The Δmfp::kan strain induced greater protection than the RB51 vaccine and similar protection to the S19 vaccine in mouse models. [Ref:7023]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Δmfp::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus MltA subunit vaccine
c_description: Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with MltA appeared to have some effect on clearance kinetics. [Ref:6965]
c_preparation: Recombinant MltA protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus multi-epitope DNA vaccine
c_description: A novel recombinant multi-epitope DNA vaccine was developed using bioinformatics to predict epitopes from Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase and open reading frames of genomic island-3 of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: The vaccine induced a statistically significant level of protection in BALB/c mice against B. abortus 2308 challenge. [Ref:7079]
c_preparation: Multi-epitope DNA plasmid vaccine chimera encoding and expressing 21 epitopes.
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase; BAB1_0260; BAB1_0270; BAB1_0273; BAB1_0278 epitopes

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus multi-epitope outer membrane proteins recombinant vector vaccine based on Lactococcus lactis
c_description: The study developed a novel vaccine strategy using genetically modified Lactococcus lactis to produce a multi-epitope outer membrane proteins (OMPs) peptide of Brucella abortus for oral administration. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed reduced spleen morphological damage, less inflammation, lymphocyte infiltration, and lesions compared to controls. [Ref:7244]
c_preparation: Oral administration of genetically modified Lactococcus lactis expressing a 39 kDa multi-epitope OMPs protein encoded by a plasmid constructed via reverse vaccinology.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus multi-epitope subunit vaccine fused to IgG Fc
c_description: The vaccine was designed using an immunoinformatics approach to identify and analyze antigenic epitopes of Brucella abortus, including epitopes recognized by cytotoxic T cells, T helper cells, and B cells. Molecular adjuvants human β-defensins 3 and PADRE were added at the N-terminus, and a mouse IgG Fc fragment was fused at the C-terminus to enhance immunogenicity, creating the MEV-Fc vaccine. Efficacy: Immunosimulation predicted strong cellular and humoral immune responses induced by the MEV-Fc vaccine. [Ref:7232]
c_preparation: Chimeric peptide vaccine composed of multiple linked epitopes with molecular adjuvants (hBD-3 and PADRE) at the N-terminus and fused to mouse IgG Fc at the C-terminus.
c_antigen: multiple epitopes recognized by cytotoxic T cells, T helper cells, and B cells; fused to IgG Fc fragment

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus multivalent DNA and subunit vaccine
c_description: The study designed a multivalent vaccine construct named S22 based on the immunogenic potential of three selected ORFs of Brucella abortus using immunoinformatic methods. Efficacy: The vaccine did not demonstrate substantial protective response against Brucella abortus in vivo. [Ref:7262]
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated as a protein subunit (S22) and a DNA construct (pVS22), and evaluated alone and in combination using a DNA prime-protein boost immunization strategy.
c_antigen: three selected open reading frames (ORFs) of Brucella abortus

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus mutant A19mut2 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate A19mut2 was developed by replacing the formyltransferase gene wbkC in Brucella abortus A19 with the acetyltransferase gene wbdR from E. coli O157, resulting in a modified O-polysaccharide that does not induce antibodies against wild-type Brucella LPS, enabling DIVA (Differentiating Infected from Vaccinated Animals) capability. Efficacy: A19mut2 showed decreased residual virulence compared to A19 but induced significant humoral and cellular immune responses similar to A19; protection efficacy against B. abortus S2308 NalR infection was comparable to A19 immunization. [Ref:7229]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with modified lipopolysaccharide due to gene replacement.
c_antigen: wbkC gene replaced by wbdR gene (modified O-polysaccharide)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus N-formylperosamine polymer AcrA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study engineered a glycoprotein by expressing Campylobacter jejuni oligosaccharyltransferase PglB and acceptor protein AcrA in Yersinia enterocolitica O9 cells, transferring a polymer of N-formylperosamine identical to Brucella abortus O polysaccharide onto AcrA. Efficacy: The glycoprotein induced an IgG response recognizing Brucella O antigen but did not confer protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in mice. [Ref:6973]
c_preparation: Recombinant glycoprotein consisting of N-formylperosamine polymer conjugated to AcrA protein produced in Yersinia enterocolitica O9.
c_antigen: N-formylperosamine polymer conjugated to AcrA protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus native cell envelope subunit vaccine
c_description: Vaccines composed of native cell envelopes or outer membrane proteins of smooth strain 2308 were compared to a vaccine composed of the insoluble residue (PG) of strain 2308 cell envelopes extracted with hot sodium dodecyl sulfate. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with native cell envelopes displayed protective immunity equivalent to PG vaccine; in cattle, native cell envelope antigens induced significantly higher titers of whole cell agglutinins over 3 months than PG. [Ref:7136]
c_adjuvant: yes; oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide
c_preparation: Vaccines were given by injection in an oil base adjuvant containing trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide or without adjuvant.
c_antigen: outer membrane proteins; porin; group 3 proteins; O polysaccharide

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Ndk subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective effect of recombinant protein encoded by Brucella abortus 544 ndk gene against B. abortus infection in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: rNdk immunized mice showed significantly lower spleen proliferation and bacterial burden compared to control (MBP-immunized) mice after virulent B. abortus challenge (P < 0.01). [Ref:7025]
c_preparation: Recombinant Ndk protein was cloned and expressed using a pMAL expression system and purified for immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 45/20 non-agglutinogenic extract subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated immunisation using non-agglutinogenic extracts derived from Brucella abortus strain 45-20. [Ref:7309]
c_preparation: Non-agglutinogenic extracts of Brucella abortus strain 45-20 were used as the vaccine formulation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O polysaccharide vaccine
c_description: The study investigated whether antibody alone could prevent infection with Brucella abortus by using monoclonal antibodies specific to the O polysaccharide. Efficacy: 82% of mice infected with 100 CFU of B. abortus preincubated with IgG2a MAb were free of infection up to 6 weeks; higher challenge doses reduced efficacy; IgG1 MAb and convalescent serum diminished but did not prevent infection. [Ref:7014]
c_preparation: Passive administration of O polysaccharide-specific IgG2a and IgG1 monoclonal antibodies and convalescent-phase serum.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-antigen polysaccharide conjugate vaccine
c_description: The study developed a bioconjugate vaccine using an O-linked glycosylation system applied to Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O:9, which has O-antigen polysaccharide identical to Brucella abortus, to create a safe vaccine candidate avoiding culture of highly pathogenic B. abortus. Efficacy: The vaccine elicited B. abortus OPS-specific serum IgG, significantly reduced bacterial loads in spleen, mitigated infection, prevented severe tissue damage, and protected mice against lethal challenge with B. abortus strain A19. [Ref:7163]
c_preparation: Bioconjugate vaccine produced by glycosylation of Y. enterocolitica O:9 with O-antigen polysaccharide from B. abortus.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-antigen subunit vaccine produced by engineered Escherichia coli
c_description: A bioconjugate vaccine against Brucella abortus was developed using engineered Escherichia coli as a safer chassis to produce the vaccine, overcoming pathogenicity issues of Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 used previously. Efficacy: The bioconjugate vaccine provided protective roles against both lethal and non-lethal challenges of Brucella abortus A19 strain. [Ref:7218]
c_preparation: The vaccine was prepared by modularizing and reassembling the O-polysaccharide (OPS) gene cluster of Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 in E. coli, followed by protein glycosylation using the PglL system to create the bioconjugate vaccine.
c_antigen: O-antigen polysaccharide from Yersinia enterocolitica O:9; protein glycosylation system (PglL system)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus O-polysaccharide subunit vaccine; Brucella suis O-polysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: Purified OPS from Brucella abortus 1119-3 and Brucella suis 1330 were evaluated as vaccines in field trials in Venezuela for protection of swine against Brucella suis challenge. Efficacy: Gilts vaccinated with OPS showed no serologic reactions, no abortions (100% protection), and litter sizes of 10 to 12 pigs. [Ref:7356]
c_preparation: Purified O-polysaccharide at doses of 100 to 500 micrograms; administered intramuscularly or orally; one or three doses.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Ohr subunit vaccine
c_description: The Brucella abortus ohr gene encoding the organic hydroperoxide resistance protein was cloned, expressed as a maltose fusion protein in Escherichia coli, purified, and evaluated for immunogenicity. Efficacy: Immunization with recombinant Ohr protein induced significantly higher protection against virulent Brucella abortus infection compared to control mice immunized with maltose-binding protein. [Ref:7046]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant Ohr protein treated with adjuvant and administered intraperitoneally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp10 recombinant vector live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to investigate the possibility of using recombinant Lactococcus lactis as a live vector to produce recombinant Brucella abortus Omp10 protein as an oral vaccine against brucellosis. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with L. lactis-pNZ8148-Omp10-Usp45 showed significantly higher Omp10-specific total IgG and IgG1 compared to PBS controls. Vaccinated mice had significantly elevated cytokine levels and reduced inflammatory response, morphological damage, alveolar edema, and lymphocyte infiltration after challenge. [Ref:7237]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Omp10 protein using the pNZ8148 vector with Usp45 signal peptide was constructed and administered orally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 and L7/L12 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This study analyzed the duration of antigen-specific humoral and T-cell immune responses and protectiveness of a recently-developed influenza viral vector Brucella abortus vaccine expressing Omp16 and L7/L12 proteins with Montadine Gel01 adjuvant in cattle. Efficacy: Prime-boost vaccination provided significant protection against B. abortus infection at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post-booster; 57.1 to 71.4% of vaccinated animals showed no signs of infection; severity and colonization rates were significantly lower in vaccinated diseased animals; good protection also observed in pregnant heifers, their fetuses, and calves; 71.4% of vaccinated heifers calved successfully versus 100% abortion in controls. [Ref:7054]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus proteins Omp16 and L7/L12 combined with Montadine Gel01 adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus OMP16 and porcine epidemic diarrhea virus PEDVS recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A novel recombinant Lactobacillus casei strain expressing PEDVS protein of PEDV and OMP16 protein of Brucella abortus strain was constructed as a candidate vaccine. Efficacy: The vaccine induced higher levels of humoral, cellular, and mucosal immunity compared to other recombinant protein controls. [Ref:7189]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactobacillus casei expressing OMP16 and PEDVS proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 L7/L12 Omp19 Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated an improved commercial Brucella abortus vaccine based on influenza viral vectors expressing Brucella immunodominant proteins, with improved formulation and route of administration. Efficacy: Protection levels against B. melitensis 16M infection were 0-20% in sheep and 20-40% in goats over 6 months; infection severity and Brucella colonization significantly reduced in vaccinated animals compared to controls. [Ref:7160]
c_preparation: Vaccine administered thrice concurrently via subcutaneous and conjunctival routes at 21-day intervals; control group received 20% Montanide Gel01 adjuvant in phosphate-buffered saline.
c_antigen: Omp16; L7/L12; Omp19; Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 L7/L12 Omp19 SOD recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The Flu-BA vaccine was improved by adding two additional proteins (Omp19 and SOD) and modifying the immunization method to maximize efficacy and safety. Efficacy: Prevented abortion in 66.7% of pregnant sheep and 77.8% of pregnant goats; complete protection (absence of live B. melitensis 16M) in 55.6% of sheep and 66.7% of goats; protection of fetuses in 72.7% of lambs and 90.0% of yeanlings; significantly reduced infection severity and colonization compared to controls; protection parameters comparable to commercial B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:7092]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector expressing Brucella abortus proteins Omp16, L7/L12, Omp19, and SOD; administered thrice at 21-day intervals with 20% Montanide Gel01 adjuvant via simultaneous subcutaneous and conjunctival routes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 Omp19 Omp28 L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective efficiency of a combination of four recombinant Brucella abortus proteins as a combined subunit vaccine against B. abortus infection. Efficacy: CSV-treated macrophages showed increased IFN-γ and IL-12 production and decreased IL-10; enhanced nitric oxide production indicating activation of bactericidal mechanisms; immunized mice showed increased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, MCP-1), higher IFN-γ than IL-10, and elevated IgG2a titers compared to IgG1, suggesting effective immune activation. [Ref:7183]
c_preparation: A combined subunit vaccine composed of four recombinant proteins: Omp16, Omp19, Omp28, and 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp16 Flu-NS1-124-Omp16 H5N1 influenza recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Novel candidate vaccines were generated based on recombinant influenza A viruses expressing Brucella outer membrane protein Omp16 from the NS1 open reading frame. Efficacy: Highest T-cell immune response observed with Omp16 expressing constructs, comparable to commercial live B. abortus strain 19 vaccine; protective efficacy in guinea pigs comparable to commercial vaccine. [Ref:7007]
c_preparation: Four recombinant influenza A viral constructs of subtypes H5N1 or H1N1 expressing Omp16 were produced; mono- or bivalent vaccine formulations administered via prime-boost intranasal, conjunctival, or subcutaneous immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19 and D15 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) was designed using reverse vaccinology methodology focusing on Omp19 and D15 antigens to prevent Brucella infection. Efficacy: The MEV exhibited a significant level of immunogenicity based on in silico analyses. [Ref:7275]
c_adjuvant: yes; adjuvants added to N-terminal of vaccine peptide (specific adjuvant names not reported)
c_preparation: The MEV construct consists of 387 amino acids including 2 CTL epitopes, 2 HTL epitopes, and 2 linear B cell epitopes from Omp19 and D15, connected by GGGS and EAAAK linkers; adjuvants were added to the N-terminal to enhance immunogenicity.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19 and P39 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant proteins Omp19 and P39 from Brucella abortus, individually and as a cocktail, against B. abortus 544 and B. melitensis 16M infection in a BALB/c mouse model. Efficacy: The rOmp19+rP39 cocktail induced significantly higher protection against B. abortus 544 and B. melitensis 16M infection compared to individual proteins, with log units of protection in spleen and liver significantly greater in the cocktail group. [Ref:7057]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins Omp19 and P39 were used individually and combined as a cocktail for intraperitoneal immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19-P39 chimeric rOP subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant chimeric protein consisting of Omp19 and P39 domains of Brucella abortus was expressed in E. coli, purified under denaturing conditions, and refolded to a dynamic form for immunization. Efficacy: Vaccination with rOP reduced bacterial CFU significantly (P<0.01) in macrophage cell lines and organs of mice after challenge with virulent Brucella species; rOP with Freund's adjuvants showed higher and faster bacterial reduction; anti-rOP antisera and antisera from rOP+adjuvant groups enhanced protection of macrophages against Brucella challenge. [Ref:7095]
c_preparation: rOP alone or formulated with adjuvants Aluminum hydroxide gel, Freund's Complete Adjuvant, or Incomplete Freund's Adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus OMP19 Lactobacillus casei pT1NX recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The gene encoding OMP19 antigen was amplified and cloned into expression vector pT1NX, then transformed into Lactobacillus casei by electroporation to create a recombinant probiotic vector vaccine. Efficacy: Mice orally immunized with the recombinant vaccine showed very good protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus 544 compared to negative controls. [Ref:7162]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactobacillus casei expressing OMP19 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp19 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine uses an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain as a vector to deliver the Brucella outer-membrane protein 19 (Omp19) antigen to goats. Efficacy: Vaccinated goats showed significantly higher serum IgG titers and interferon-γ production compared to vector control; reduced Brucella colonization in tissues; decreased Brucella antigen expression in spleen, kidney, and lymph nodes; amelioration of brucellosis-related histopathological lesions. [Ref:7187]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain expressing Omp19 at 5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL in 1 mL.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25 and L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: Currently used Brucella abortus strain 19 and RB51 vaccines are live attenuated strains but pose risks such as attenuation reversal and virulence; recombinant subunit vaccines are considered a safe and competent alternative. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the combined Omp25+L7/L12 vaccine exhibited superior Log10 protection against virulent Brucella abortus 544 compared to individual vaccines. [Ref:7158]
c_preparation: A divalent recombinant vaccine consisting of Omp25 and L7/L12 proteins of Brucella abortus was formulated and evaluated individually and in combination.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus omp25 recombinant vector vaccine (Lactococcus lactis, oral delivery)
c_description: The study developed a novel oral antigen delivery system using Lactococcus lactis transformed with a plasmid encoding the Brucella abortus omp25 antigen to target mucosal immunity. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant omp25-specific IgG1 antibody production, increased IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-4, and IL-10 cytokine levels, and reduced spleen injury, alveolar edema, lymphocyte infiltration, and morphological damage compared to controls, indicating protective potential. [Ref:7227]
c_preparation: Oral vaccination with Lactococcus lactis transformed with pNZ8148 plasmid encoding omp25 (pNZ8148:omp25); control groups included free pNZ8148 and phosphate-buffered saline.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine
c_description: This study developed novel mRNA vaccines targeting the outer membrane protein Omp25 of Brucella abortus using lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA (Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP). Efficacy: The Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP vaccine induced significantly stronger humoral and cellular immune responses than alum-adjuvanted protein vaccines and markedly reduced splenic bacterial load after challenge. [Ref:7272]
c_preparation: Lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated nucleoside-modified mRNA vaccine encoding Omp25 fused with Fc (Omp25-Fc mRNA-LNP).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the immunogenic potential of recombinant Omp25 and its protective efficacy against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in Balb/c mice. Efficacy: Intradermal immunization significantly reduced splenic colonization of Brucella abortus; protection comparable to that of Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine. [Ref:6974]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp25 administered via intraperitoneal and intradermal routes; dosage reduction observed with intradermal immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp25c subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to examine the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of Omp25c, a conserved porin protein paralogous to Omp25 and Omp31, as a vaccine candidate against Brucella infections. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed protection against Brucella abortus challenge comparable to the S19 vaccine strain. [Ref:7105]
c_preparation: Recombinant unlipidated Omp25c protein (rOmp25c) was produced and administered intraperitoneally in BALB/c mice along with Freund's adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp28 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and protective ability of recombinant Omp28 from Brucella abortus as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: rOmp28-immunized mice showed 20-fold higher IgG1 and IgG2a titers compared to controls; spleen proliferation and bacterial burden were approximately 1.5-fold lower than PBS-treated mice after challenge. [Ref:6983]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp28 protein expressed in Escherichia coli and purified; no adjuvant mentioned.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp2b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to analyze the secondary and tertiary structures of Brucella abortus Omp2b protein and predict T-cell and B-cell epitopes using bioinformatics tools to support its potential as a vaccine antigen. [Ref:7059]
c_preparation: Cloning and expression of the short form of Omp2b (SOmp2b) was performed using pET28a expression vector in Escherichia coli BL21, followed by purification of recombinant SOmp2b protein under denaturation conditions using Ni-NTA column.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Omp3b/BCSP31/SOD attenuated Salmonella recombinant vector vaccine mixture
c_description: This study aimed to assess the protective efficacy of a novel Brucella vaccine formulation in goats using a Salmonella-based delivery system expressing recombinant Brucella abortus Omp3b, BCSP31, and SOD proteins. Efficacy: 40% of vaccinated animals were protected against B. abortus infection. The infection index and colonization of B. abortus in tested tissues were significantly lower in vaccinated goats compared to controls. [Ref:7141]
c_preparation: A mixture of three Brucella vaccine strains using a Salmonella-based delivery system, each expressing one of the recombinant B. abortus proteins Omp3b, BCSP31, or SOD, administered at 3.0 × 10^9 CFU/mL.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus OmpA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the use of Brucella abortus outer membrane protein A (OmpA) as a candidate subunit vaccine in a mouse infection model. Efficacy: Mice treated with recombinant OmpA showed significant protection compared to controls treated with MBP or PBS. [Ref:7052]
c_preparation: Recombinant OmpA protein fused to maltose binding protein (MBP) was cloned, overexpressed, and purified from Escherichia coli.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus rough-strain outer membrane–peptidoglycan complex subunit vaccine
c_description: The OM-PG from rough strains of Brucella abortus was tested for its ability to induce lymphocyte responsiveness in cattle. Efficacy: Frequency of lymphocyte responsiveness increased with dose and with two inoculations compared to single inoculations; OM-PG from a rough transposon mutant induced comparable responsiveness to that from a spontaneous rough mutant; differences in lymphocyte specificity compared to strain 19 vaccine. [Ref:6962]
c_preparation: OM-PG preparations emulsified in a commercial adjuvant; doses ranged from 400 to 8000 micrograms; administered in single or two inoculations.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 19 delta live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The Δomp19::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus was evaluated as a live vaccine candidate due to its attenuation and residual virulence in mouse models. Efficacy: The Δomp19::kan strain induced protection similar to that of the RB51 vaccine in mouse models. [Ref:7023]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Δomp19::kan mutant strain of Brucella abortus.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 19 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study assessed immune responses induced by recombinant outer membrane protein 19 of Brucella abortus loaded into chitosan nanoparticles for intranasal immunization. Efficacy: Increased antigen-specific total IgG, predominantly IgG1; significant mucosal IgA responses detected in sera, nasal washes, genital secretions, and fecal excretions; spleenocytes produced significant IFN-γ and IL-4 indicating mixed Th1-Th2 response. [Ref:7143]
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp19 protein loaded in chitosan nanoparticles administered intranasally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 25 subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus outer membrane protein 31 subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus Omp2b porin subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus 60 kDa chaperonin GroEL subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus fumarate reductase flavoprotein subunit subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus F0F1-type ATP synthase alpha subunit subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus cysteine synthase A subunit vaccine
c_description: Live attenuated vaccines S19 and RB51 are used to control bovine brucellosis but have safety issues for humans and pregnant cattle; this study aims to identify novel candidate proteins from B. abortus cell envelope for safer vaccine development. [Ref:6921]
c_preparation: Identification of immunogenic proteins from B. abortus cell envelope using proteomic techniques including 2-DE, MALDI-TOF MS, and LC-MS/MS; Western blot analyses with sera from infected bovine and human patients identified immunogenic proteins.
c_antigen: outer-membrane protein 25; outer-membrane protein 31; Omp2b porin; 60 kDa chaperonin GroEL; fumarate reductase flavoprotein subunit; F0F1-type ATP synthase alpha subunit; cysteine synthase A

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain S19 outer membrane protein cationic liposome subunit vaccine (S19-OMP-liposome)
c_description: The study evaluated a vaccine formulation consisting of outer membrane protein from Brucella abortus strain S19 entrapped in a commercial cationic liposome used as an adjuvant and delivery system. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the S19-OMP-liposome showed enhanced protection compared to mice inoculated with S19 OMP alone, live B. abortus S19 vaccine, or liposome alone (P<0.05); the S19-OMP-liposome was safer than the live vaccine as indicated by spleen weight differences (P<0.01). [Ref:7070]
c_preparation: Outer membrane protein of Brucella abortus strain S19 entrapped in a commercial cationic liposome.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane proteins from smooth strain 2308 and rough strain 45/20 of Brucella abortus were used to study immune responses in cattle. [Ref:7257]
c_preparation: Outer membrane proteins isolated from Brucella abortus strains 2308 and 45/20.
c_antigen: outer membrane proteins; group 2 (porins); group 3 proteins

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Outer Membrane Proteins and Lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate humoral immunity induced by Brucella abortus LPS and OMPs using Serum Bactericidal Assay (SBA). Efficacy: The combined vaccine group showed the highest titer of 1/64 and vaccine efficacy of 87.71%. [Ref:7250]
c_preparation: Three groups of rabbits were injected with either 25 μg LPS, 50 μg OMPs, or a combined vaccine of LPS and OMPs, administered three times every two weeks.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus outer membrane proteins subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the immune response induced by outer membrane proteins compared to whole live bacteria of Brucella abortus. Efficacy: OMP-inoculated group showed higher IFN-gamma production than bacteria-infected group, indicating potential for immune response induction. [Ref:6950]
c_preparation: Outer membrane proteins of Brucella abortus used for inoculation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus outer membrane vesicle vaccine
c_description: Native OMVs from wild-type Brucella abortus were characterized and shown to enhance bacterial invasion and intracellular survival in macrophages and increase pathogenicity in mice. Efficacy: Native OMVs showed low yield and limited immunogenicity; no effective protection reported. [Ref:7289]
c_preparation: Biological nanoparticles (outer-membrane vesicles) derived from wild-type Brucella abortus.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 99 outer membrane vesicle vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) were derived from Brucella abortus strain 99 using ultracentrifugation. Efficacy: OMVs showed immuno-reactivity with mice antisera and induced specific high-titer immune responses. [Ref:7051]
c_preparation: Isolated OMVs characterized as spherical 20-300 nm structures rich in proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 and lumazine synthase DNA vaccine
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins of Brucella abortus was constructed and evaluated. Efficacy: Single DNA immunization was less effective than DNA prime followed by adenovirus boost in reducing bacterial load. [Ref:7101]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 and lumazine synthase adenovirus vector vaccine
c_description: A recombinant adenovirus vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins of Brucella abortus was constructed and evaluated. Efficacy: Single adenovirus immunization was less effective than DNA prime followed by adenovirus boost in reducing bacterial load. [Ref:7101]
c_preparation: Recombinant adenovirus vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 and lumazine synthase
c_description: The study constructed recombinant adenovirus and plasmid DNA vaccines co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins of Brucella abortus to evaluate immunogenicity and protection. Efficacy: The DNA priming followed by adenovirus boosting strategy significantly reduced the numbers of Brucella abortus in the mouse model. [Ref:7101]
c_preparation: Two molecular vaccines were constructed: a recombinant adenovirus vaccine and a plasmid DNA vaccine co-expressing P39 and lumazine synthase proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus P39 Yersinia recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was delivered using live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica serotypes O:3 and O:9 as vectors to improve protection and evaluate the role of anti-LPS antibodies. Efficacy: Induced antigen-specific Th1-type immune responses; the O:9 vector carrying pCIP39 conferred the best and highly significant protection against B. abortus 544 infection. [Ref:1270]
c_preparation: Naked-DNA plasmids encoding P39 delivered by live attenuated Yersinia enterocolitica O:3 or O:9 strains via intragastric immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus protein-bound peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: Vaccination one month before pregnancy decreased frequency of placental colonization and number of brucella per infected placenta and per spleen in pregnant mice. Efficacy: PG fractions protected mice as well as H38 killed and B19 attenuated living vaccines. [Ref:7312]
c_preparation: Protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fractions extracted from Brucella abortus

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus per mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The per mutant was evaluated as a rough vaccine candidate in mice. Efficacy: Induced protection against Brucella abortus but less than the standard smooth vaccine strain 19; afforded similar protection to strain 19 against Brucella ovis. [Ref:6890]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough lipopolysaccharide mutant with per gene disruption.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus B19 phenol-insoluble fraction vaccine
c_description: This prospective phase IV study involved vaccination of professionally exposed subjects who were negative to an intradermal test for previous contamination. Efficacy: Clinical effectiveness could not be accurately evaluated due to insufficient subject numbers; seropositivity reached 80% after primary vaccination but decreased after 18 months. [Ref:6896]
c_preparation: Vaccine composed of the phenol-insoluble fraction of Brucella abortus biotype 1 (B19 strain).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 Δpgm live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The deltapgm strain is a phosphoglucomutase gene deletion mutant of Brucella abortus S2308 that synthesizes an incomplete O antigen resulting in a rough lipopolysaccharide phenotype. It was developed to overcome disadvantages of the S19 vaccine such as virulence in humans and interference with immune screening. Efficacy: Vaccination with the deltapgm strain induced protection levels comparable to those induced by the S19 vaccine. [Ref:1909]
c_preparation: Live rough-phenotype mutant strain with inability to assemble complete O side chain in LPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 Δpgk live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A pgk deletion mutant of Brucella abortus strain 2308 was constructed to test the role of PGK in pathogenesis and as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The Delta pgk mutant strain exhibited extreme attenuation and induced protective immunity superior to that conferred by commercial strain 19 or RB51 vaccines in both immunocompetent and immunocompromised mice. [Ref:1811]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus Delta pgk mutant strain.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus pncA mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The pncA mutant of Brucella abortus showed defective intracellular replication and reduced virulence in mice but retained the ability to confer protection against virulent B. abortus strain 544. Efficacy: The pncA mutant showed a 1.5-log reduction in bacterial load in mouse spleens after 10 weeks and fully retained protective ability against virulent B. abortus strain 544. [Ref:6900]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus polyclonal anti-idiotype antibody subunit vaccine
c_description: Polyclonal goat anti-idiotypic antibodies mimicking Brucella abortus antigens were generated from rabbit polyclonal idiotypes specific for a partially purified extract of B. abortus (PX III). Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed greater than 90% reduction of bacteria in the spleen compared to unvaccinated controls after challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308. [Ref:6959]
c_preparation: Purified anti-idiotypic antibodies obtained by two-step immunoaffinity column chromatography.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus polysaccharide cross-reacting with Yersinia subunit vaccine
c_description: Immune sera cross-reacting with Yersinia polysaccharide reduced dissemination of Brucella abortus 544 infection and caused a shift of bacteria from spleen to liver when injected simultaneously with intravenous challenge. Efficacy: Induced early effect of reduced bacterial numbers in spleen due to shift to liver but did not induce late clearance effect. [Ref:7311]
c_preparation: Polysaccharide antigen cross-reacting with Yersinia used to generate immune serum.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: Mice vaccinated with a protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan Brucella fraction produced immune sera that completely stopped dissemination of Brucella abortus 544 infection to the spleen. Efficacy: Immune serum prevented dissemination of infection to the spleen and helped destroy intracellular bacteria, leading to nearly complete clearance by day 49 postchallenge. [Ref:7311]
c_preparation: Protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fraction of Brucella used to generate immune serum.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus protein-bound cell wall peptidoglycan fraction vaccine
c_description: A protein-bound peptidoglycan fraction (PG) was used to immunize mice intravenously or subcutaneously. Efficacy: Transferred lymph node and spleen cells conferred immunity reducing Brucella counts; lymph node cells were more efficient; immunity increased for about 21 days post-transfer; immunity was partially abrogated by anti-Thy serum treatment; genetic background influenced response. [Ref:7194]
c_preparation: Protein-bound peptidoglycan fraction derived from Brucella abortus cell wall; administered intravenously or subcutaneously.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 proteinase K-treated lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: Lipopolysaccharide extracted from Brucella abortus strain 2308 and treated with proteinase K. Efficacy: PKLPS was immunogenic and protective, reducing splenic bacterial load and weight. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: PKLPS used alone or combined with other proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study assessed the effect of MPL and TDM adjuvants on protective responses of the proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide vaccine in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccination reduced spleen weights and Brucella CFU compared to controls; MPL did not enhance suppression of splenic infection with this vaccine; TDM increased mean CFU when combined with proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide. [Ref:6898]
c_adjuvant: yes; monophosphoryl lipid A; trehalose dimycolate
c_preparation: Proteinase-K-treated lipopolysaccharide given alone or combined with MPL or TDM adjuvants.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus PrpA Salmonella Typhimurium recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine uses an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain as a vector to deliver the Brucella proline racemase subunit A (PrpA) antigen to goats. Efficacy: Vaccinated goats showed significantly higher interferon-γ production compared to vector control; reduced Brucella colonization in tissues; decreased Brucella antigen expression in spleen, kidney, and lymph nodes; amelioration of brucellosis-related histopathological lesions. [Ref:7187]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain expressing PrpA at 5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL in 1 mL.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus PrpA recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector constitutively expressing heterologous Brucella abortus PrpA protein was used to investigate safety, humoral and cellular immunity, and protective efficacy. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significantly quicker anti-Salmonella IgG responses and increased protection against Salmonella challenge compared to Salmonella vector only. [Ref:7099]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella abortus PrpA protein (ST-PrpA)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus PrpA subunit vaccine
c_description: Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with PrpA appeared to have some effect on clearance kinetics. [Ref:6965]
c_preparation: Recombinant PrpA protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus purified killed vaccine
c_description: A purified killed vaccine was developed for potential immunization of humans against brucellosis. Efficacy: The purified whole-culture vaccine immunized mice better than crude killed organisms, extracted washed organisms, or extracted culture supernatant vaccines. [Ref:7308]
c_preparation: Prepared by adding sodium dodecyl sulphate to intact cultures of virulent Brucella abortus grown in a defined medium containing erythritol; bacterial debris removed; immunogen precipitated with ethanol and redissolved in buffer.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus rBCSP20 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant form of BCSP20 protein. Efficacy: Recombinant BCSP20 did not consistently induce protection comparable to BCSP or PKLPS. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: Recombinant protein used alone or combined with other recombinant proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus rBCSP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant form of BCSP31 protein. Efficacy: Recombinant BCSP31 did not induce protection comparable to native BCSP or PKLPS. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: Recombinant protein used alone or combined with other recombinant proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus rBCSP45 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant form of BCSP45 protein. Efficacy: Recombinant BCSP45 did not show protective efficacy comparable to native BCSP or PKLPS. [Ref:6961]
c_preparation: Recombinant protein used alone or combined with other recombinant proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant BCSP20 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant proteins rBCSP20, rBCSP31, and rBCSP45 were chemically modified to assess modulation of immune responses. Efficacy: Chemical modification had no effect on protection induced by recombinant proteins. [Ref:7332]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins were modified with succinic and dodecanoyl anhydrides.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus recombinant SodC RibH Ndk L7/L12 MDH subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective efficacy of a combination of five recombinant Brucella abortus proteins cloned and expressed in a pMal vector system and purified for vaccination. Efficacy: The combination vaccine significantly reduced bacterial colonization in the spleen with a log protection unit of 1.31, comparable to protection conferred by the live attenuated vaccine RB51. [Ref:7119]
c_preparation: The five recombinant proteins were combined and administered intraperitoneally into BALB/c mice.
c_antigen: superoxide dismutase (SodC), riboflavin synthase subunit beta (RibH), nucleoside diphosphate kinase (Ndk), 50S ribosomal protein (L7/L12), malate dehydrogenase (MDH)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Flu-BA recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Previously developed and evaluated in cattle; this study aimed to establish proof-of-concept efficacy in sheep and goats. Efficacy: Complete protection in 57.1% of sheep and 42.9% of goats against B. melitensis 16M challenge; significantly lower infection index and tissue colonization compared to negative controls. [Ref:7074]
c_preparation: Influenza viral vector based Brucella abortus vaccine administered with Montanide Gel01 adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strains 19 and 45/20 ribosomal preparation vaccine
c_description: Ribosomes were isolated from Brucella abortus strains 19 and 45/20 and studied for their immunological properties. Efficacy: Ribosomes from Brucella abortus S19 induced agglutinins reacting with smooth Brucella strains; those from strain 45/20 induced agglutinins reacting with rough Brucella strains; cattle vaccinated with S19 or 45/20 vaccines developed precipitins to ribosomal components early in the immune response. [Ref:7336]
c_preparation: Ribosomal preparations free of detectable lipopolysaccharide-protein agglutinogen, containing 2-3 immunodiffusion-reactive components.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 ribosomal fraction subunit vaccine
c_description: Ribosome preparations derived from Brucella abortus strain 19 cells were examined for immunizing activity. Efficacy: Immunity to challenge by virulent Brucella abortus 544 organisms was at least as effective as live strain 19 vaccine in mice and guinea pigs. [Ref:7334]
c_preparation: Ribosome preparations incorporated in Freund's incomplete adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ribosomal protein L9 DNA vaccine
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine encoding ribosomal protein L9 of Brucella abortus (pVaxL9) was generated to evaluate its immunogenicity and protective efficacy. Efficacy: The L9 based DNA vaccine conferred significant protection against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in mice; groups receiving pVaxL9 priming plus recombinant L9 boosting and those immunised with electroporation showed better protection. [Ref:7010]
c_preparation: Intramuscular immunisation of pVaxL9 plasmid DNA; boosting with recombinant L9 protein in some groups; in vivo electroporation used in some immunisation groups.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ribosomal protein L9 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified ribosomal protein L9 from the stationary-phase exoproteome of Brucella abortus as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Recombinant L9-immunized mice were protected against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 544. [Ref:6999]
c_preparation: Recombinant ribosomal protein L9 was produced and used for immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus RNase E defective strain vaccine
c_description: The study generated a Brucella abortus strain encoding a defective version of RNase E lacking the C-terminal portion (rne-tnc), which was attenuated in a mouse model of infection. Efficacy: The rne-tnc strain was attenuated in the mouse model, indicating reduced virulence. [Ref:7173]
c_antigen: RNase E (defective version lacking C-terminal portion)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus ΔrpoE1 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a Brucella abortus strain lacking the alternative sigma factor σ(E1) (ΔrpoE1), which is part of the general stress response system and required for persistence in mice. Efficacy: Mice immunized with ΔrpoE1 completely resisted wild-type infection and showed reduced splenomegaly and bacterial burden compared to wild-type infected mice. [Ref:7067]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus ΔrpoE1 mutant strain without adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus salt extractable periplasmic protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immune and protective responses induced by vaccination with six salt-extractable periplasmic protein fractions from Brucella abortus strain 19. Efficacy: Vaccines prepared from BCSP70 and BCSP100 were moderately protective and immunogenic; subfractions BCSP100-A through BCSP100-D were not protective without MPL; MPL enhanced protection or was neutral with BCSP70, BCSP100, BCSP100-C, and BCSP100-D; some subfractions increased bacterial survival and splenomegaly. [Ref:7345]
c_adjuvant: yes; monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) from Salmonella typhimurium Re mutant strain
c_preparation: Vaccines were prepared from BCSP70 and BCSP100 protein fractions and four subfractions (BCSP100-A through BCSP100-D) purified by anion-exchange HPLC; some formulations included monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) as an immune response modifier.
c_antigen: salt-extractable periplasmic proteins (BCSP70, BCSP100, and subfractions BCSP100-A, BCSP100-B, BCSP100-C, BCSP100-D)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus salt-extractable protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the effect of monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) and trehalose dimycolate (TDM) as adjuvants on the protective responses of the salt-extractable protein vaccine in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccination with salt-extractable protein reduced spleen weights and Brucella CFU compared to controls; MPL enhanced suppression of splenic infection when combined with salt-extractable protein; TDM had no effect on CFU with salt-extractable protein. [Ref:6898][Ref:7313]
c_adjuvant: yes; monophosphoryl lipid A; trehalose dimycolate
c_preparation: Salt-extractable protein given alone or combined with MPL or TDM adjuvants.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus SecB subunit vaccine
c_description: Two recombinant proteins encoded by Brucella abortus gene SecB were cloned and expressed in E. coli and evaluated as single subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with recombinant SecB protein significantly reduced spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS control, indicating protection against B. abortus infection. [Ref:7159]
c_preparation: Recombinant SecB protein purified after expression in Escherichia coli DH5α; administered intraperitoneally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus smooth lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with Quillaja saponin
c_description: The vaccine candidate combines Brucella abortus S19 smooth lipopolysaccharide with Quillaja saponin to create a green vaccine aimed at mucosal brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccination conferred significant protection with a 130-fold reduction in lung bacterial burden and a 55.74-fold reduction in spleen bacterial burden compared to PBS controls. [Ref:7223]
c_preparation: Two doses of sLPS combined with Quillaja saponin administered intranasally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus smooth lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with Quillaja saponin-Xyloglucan mix
c_description: The vaccine candidate combines Brucella abortus S19 smooth lipopolysaccharide with a Quillaja saponin and Xyloglucan mix to create a green vaccine aimed at mucosal brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccination resulted in the highest reduction in splenic Brucella loads with a 364.6-fold decrease in bacterial titer compared to non-vaccinated animals. [Ref:7223]
c_preparation: Two doses of sLPS combined with Quillaja saponin-Xyloglucan mix administered intranasally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus SOD/Omp19/BLS/PrpA Salmonella recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: An attenuated live Salmonella Typhimurium vector delivering heterologous Brucella immunogenic proteins SOD, Omp19, BLS, and PrpA formulated with purified Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide was developed to generate a safe and effective anti-Brucella vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccinated guinea pigs showed a protective index of 1.52 based on differential splenic bacterial counts and reduced histopathological lesions compared to non-immunized controls. [Ref:7098]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella proteins SOD, Omp19, BLS, and PrpA combined with purified Brucella abortus lipopolysaccharide.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus SOD Salmonella recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The vaccine uses an attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain as a vector to deliver the Brucella Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD) antigen to goats. Efficacy: Vaccinated goats showed significantly higher serum IgG titers and interferon-γ production compared to vector control; reduced Brucella colonization in tissues; decreased Brucella antigen expression in spleen, kidney, and lymph nodes; amelioration of brucellosis-related histopathological lesions. [Ref:7187]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium strain expressing SOD at 5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL in 1 mL.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus soluble antigen subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the effects of five different adjuvants on immune responses in cattle injected with a Brucella abortus soluble antigen. Efficacy: Immunized steers showed significantly higher antibody responses than controls and BASA alone groups. Lymphoproliferation and delayed-type hypersensitivity responses were greatest in groups receiving strain 19 and BASA with DDA. IL-1 induction was highest with BASA + DDA; IL-2 release was greatest in strain 19 vaccinated steers. Suppressor T cell responses were notable in strain 19, BASA + Bordetella pertussis, and BASA + Propionibacterium acnes groups. [Ref:6928]
c_adjuvant: yes; muramyl dipeptide; Freund's incomplete adjuvant; dimethyl-dioctadecyl ammonium bromide (DDA); Bordetella pertussis; Propionibacterium acnes
c_preparation: Brucella abortus soluble antigen (2 mg protein) was administered subcutaneously with one of five adjuvants: muramyl dipeptide, Freund's incomplete adjuvant, dimethyl-dioctadecyl ammonium bromide (DDA), Bordetella pertussis, or Propionibacterium acnes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus soluble fraction vaccine
c_description: The study describes a soluble fraction (ABS) from smooth Brucella abortus phenol-protected suspensions containing proteins, lipids, sugars, and RNA, which is non-toxic and immunizes mice against B. abortus challenge. Efficacy: ABS immunization protected mice against B. abortus challenge. [Ref:7335]
c_preparation: ABS is a complex of protein, lipid, sugar, and RNA derived from phenol-water fractions of B. abortus and B. melitensis; it can be bound to sheep erythrocytes using chromium chloride for hemagglutination tests.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 soluble protein extract subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the adjuvant effects of DDA alone or combined with TDM or MDP on immune responses to a soluble protein extract of gamma irradiated Brucella abortus strain 19. Efficacy: The highest and most sustained antibody responses were elicited by the S19 vaccine; among SPEBA groups, SPEBA with DDA + TDM induced higher antibody levels and stronger delayed-type hypersensitivity responses than other adjuvant combinations. [Ref:6927]
c_adjuvant: yes; dimethyl dioctadecyl ammonium bromide (DDA); trehalose dimycolate (TDM); muramyl dipeptide (MDP)
c_preparation: Soluble protein extract of gamma irradiated Brucella abortus strain 19 (2 mg protein per dose) administered subcutaneously with adjuvants DDA alone, DDA + TDM, or DDA + MDP.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus soluble protein extract subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immunization of cattle with a Brucella abortus soluble protein extract vaccine augmented by recombinant bovine IL 2. Efficacy: SPEBA vaccine alone provided limited protection; co-administration with rBoIL 2 improved antibody responses and lymphoproliferation but protection against abortion was not as strong as with S19 plus rBoIL 2. [Ref:6910]
c_preparation: Subunit vaccine consisting of 2 mg soluble protein extract administered with or without recombinant bovine IL 2.
c_antigen: soluble protein extract of Brucella abortus (SPEBA)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 104M vaccine
c_type: Whole organism vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the protective efficacy and safety of Brucella abortus strain 104M administered by intratracheal aerosol delivery, intranasal instillation, or subcutaneous injection in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed no abnormal clinical symptoms or significant body weight changes. Spleen weights post-challenge were significantly lower in immunized groups compared to controls. Bacterial loads in spleens decreased over time and were significantly lower than controls after challenge. High titers of specific antibodies were detected, peaking at week 8. Cytokine levels (IFN-γ, IL-18) were elevated pre-challenge and modulated post-challenge. No significant differences were observed among immunization routes. The vaccine showed obvious protective efficacy against aerosol challenge. [Ref:7172]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 104M delivered via three routes: intratracheal aerosol, intranasal instillation, and subcutaneous injection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 BA vaccine
c_description: The study investigated immune activation in mice vaccinated with Brucella abortus 19 BA. Efficacy: Not directly reported; the study observed antigen-specific activation of lymphocytes indicating immune response. [Ref:7176]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 bacterial ghost vaccine
c_description: The study developed a Brucella abortus A19 bacterial ghost vaccine using a double inactivation strategy combining biological lysis and hydrogen peroxide treatment to ensure complete inactivation and safety. Efficacy: Immunization with A19BG conferred a similar level of protection as the existing A19 vaccine against Brucella melitensis M28 in both guinea pigs and cattle. [Ref:7197]
c_preparation: The vaccine was prepared by sequential biological lysis and hydrogen peroxide treatment resulting in bacterial ghosts with typical morphology and genetic stability.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus INTA2 live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Whole organism vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus INTA2 is a novel mutant strain constructed by inactivation of two B. abortus strain 19 genes, bp26 and bmp18, replacing bp26 with the luciferase gene as a marker, aiming to reduce residual virulence and allow differentiation from field strains. Efficacy: INTA2 showed significantly reduced bacterial load in spleens during early infection and no splenomegaly, indicating reduced residual virulence; provided similar protection levels against virulent challenge as strain 19. [Ref:6884]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant strain with bp26 replaced by luciferase gene and partial deletion of bmp18, lacking drug resistance markers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 bp26-luciferase omp19 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: INTA 2 is a double mutant derived from M1-luc with most of omp19 deleted without introduction of genetic markers. Efficacy: Protection against abortion was 45.5% in heifers vaccinated with INTA 2, lower than S19 and M1-luc; in mice, I2 was more attenuated than S19 with no reduction in protection. [Ref:6930]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant strain with bp26 replaced by luciferase gene and omp19 deleted.
c_antigen: omp19 deletion mutant derived from M1-luc

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutants of Brucella abortus S19, a vaccine strain, were generated by gene replacement to study their survival and pathogenicity. Efficacy: The S19 Cu-Zn SOD mutant showed approximately 10-fold lower splenic levels than the parental strain through 26 days postinfection in mice, indicating reduced survival; infection declined sharply thereafter with no organisms detected by 105 days. [Ref:6908]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 with Cu-Zn SOD gene deletion replaced by a kanamycin resistance marker.
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (Cu-Zn SOD) deletion mutant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 cyclic beta-1,2-glucan synthetase mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A cyclic beta-1,2-glucan synthetase mutant was generated from the Brucella abortus attenuated vaccinal strain 19 (S19) to investigate its role in virulence and vaccine efficacy. Efficacy: The mutant was completely cleared from mouse spleens after 4 weeks but retained full protective ability against virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308 challenge. [Ref:6878]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletion of cyclic beta-1,2-glucan synthetase gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19 Δ31K live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Genetic mutant derived from strain 19 with 31K deletion was inoculated subcutaneously in calves to study bacterial survival and immune response. Efficacy: Cleared bacteria from lymph nodes more rapidly than virulent strain 2308; less lymphoid destruction; antibody titers did not persist for 16 weeks. [Ref:6897]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vaccine derived from strain 19 with 31K gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19Δper outer membrane vesicle vaccine
c_description: The study explores outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) extracted from Brucella abortus S19Δper as an alternative subunit vaccine candidate to address safety issues associated with the live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine. Efficacy: OMVs immunized mice showed reduced splenic weight index and lower Brucella abortus strain 544 counts compared to unimmunized mice, indicating good protective efficacy; OMVs S19Δper induced higher IgG titers but conferred nearly equal protection as OMVs S19. [Ref:7177]
c_preparation: OMVs derived from the LPS defective S19Δper strain, characterized by higher OMV release and more homogeneous populations compared to parent strain S19 OMVs.
c_antigen: LPS defective S19Δper outer membrane proteins

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19Δper live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A modified Brucella abortus strain 19 mutant (S19Δper) with intermediate rough phenotype and residual O-polysaccharide was developed by deletion of the perosamine synthetase gene to reduce residual virulence and enable DIVA capability. Efficacy: S19Δper conferred protection in mice similar to the parental S19 vaccine strain. [Ref:7028]
c_preparation: Live attenuated S19Δper mutant with intermediate rough lipopolysaccharide phenotype.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19 ΔSOD live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Genetic mutant derived from strain 19 with SOD deletion was inoculated subcutaneously in calves to study bacterial survival and immune response. Efficacy: Cleared bacteria from lymph nodes more rapidly than virulent strain 2308; less lymphoid destruction; antibody titers did not persist for 16 weeks. [Ref:6897]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vaccine derived from strain 19 with SOD gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus A19-ΔVirB12 vaccine
c_description: The A19-∆VirB12 vaccine strain is a recently developed Brucella abortus vaccine strain carrying a deletion of the VirB12 gene, which complicates serological differentiation from wild-type infections. [Ref:7303]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19 ΔvjbR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A vjbR knockout mutant was generated in the Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine to improve safety and efficacy. Efficacy: A single dose of the encapsulated mutant conferred higher levels of protection against wild-type challenge compared to the nonencapsulated vaccine. [Ref:2096]
c_adjuvant: yes; vitelline protein B (nonimmunogenic eggshell precursor protein of Fasciola hepatica)
c_preparation: The vaccine was delivered either encapsulated in alginate microspheres containing vitelline protein B as a sustained-release vehicle or nonencapsulated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus S19-GFP live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A prototype Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine expressing green fluorescent protein (S19-GFP) was constructed to serve as a marker vaccine. Efficacy: S19-GFP protected mice against virulent Brucella abortus challenge to the same extent as the parental S19 vaccine. [Ref:6957]
c_preparation: The S19-GFP vaccine maintained all biochemical characteristics of the parental S19 vaccine and expressed GFP allowing identification under ultraviolet light.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 htrA gene deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: An htrA deletion mutant was created in the bovine vaccine strain Brucella abortus S19 by replacing most of the htrA gene with a kanamycin resistance gene. Efficacy: The htrA mutant showed significantly reduced spleen colonization at 1 week and enhanced clearance at 4 and 7 weeks post-infection compared to parental strain; colonization was equivalent at 2 and 3 weeks. [Ref:7349]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 with htrA gene deletion; kanamycin-resistant, ampicillin-sensitive.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 live attenuated vaccine expressing Mycobacterium bovis MPB83 fusion proteins
c_description: The immunodominant MPB83 antigen from Mycobacterium bovis was expressed as chimeric fusion proteins with β-galactosidase, outer membrane lipoprotein OMP19, or periplasmic protein BP26 in Brucella abortus strain 19, driven by each gene's own promoter. Efficacy: Recombinant S19 strains induced specific INF-γ production against MPB83; fusion to BP26 resulted in weaker immune response; no effect on bacterial survival or infection pattern. [Ref:6955]
c_preparation: Recombinant B. abortus S19 strains carrying genes coding for MPB83 fused to β-galactosidase, OMP19, or BP26 expressed from replicative or integrative plasmids; OMP19-MPB83 processed as a lipoprotein.
c_antigen: MPB83; fusion partners β-galactosidase, OMP19, BP26

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 live attenuated vaccine expressing Trypanosoma cruzi repetitive antigen
c_description: A vector was developed to express foreign antigens in the Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine by cloning regulatory sequences and signal peptide of the bcsp31 gene into a broad-host-range plasmid, enabling expression of a Trypanosoma cruzi repetitive antigen. Efficacy: The recombinant antigen induced a good antibody response against the Trypanosoma cruzi antigen; expression did not alter bacterial growth or cause toxicity. [Ref:7357]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein expressed and secreted into the Brucella periplasmic space using plasmid pBEV in the live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella abortus strain 19 were evaluated as an alternative subunit vaccine candidate. Efficacy: OMVs S19 immunized mice showed reduced splenic weight index and lower bacterial counts after challenge, indicating protective efficacy similar to OMVs S19Δper. [Ref:7177]
c_preparation: OMVs isolated from the parent strain S19, characterized by higher polydispersity index compared to S19Δper OMVs.
c_antigen: outer membrane proteins and LPS of Brucella abortus strain 19

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 phage lysate vaccine with aluminium hydroxide gel adjuvant
c_description: The study introduces a phage lysate vaccine generated using brucellaphage 'ϕLd' lysing Brucella abortus strain 19 cultures, adsorbed on aluminium hydroxide gel as an adjuvant. Efficacy: The aluminium hydroxide gel adsorbed lysate vaccine exhibited dose-dependent protective potency, with the highest dose showing greater protection than the standard S19 vaccine. [Ref:7040]
c_preparation: Lysate prepared from 24 h incubated Brucella abortus S19 broth cultures (~10^8 CFU/ml), adsorbed on aluminium hydroxide gel (0.1% aluminium concentration) with antigenic dose of 0.52 μg protein and 60 μg carbohydrate (CHO).
c_antigen: immuno-dominant polypeptides of approximately 16, 19 and 23 kDa

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 recombinant vector vaccine expressing Babesia bovis RAP1 (S19pBB-RAP1, beta-galactosidase fusion)
c_type: Whole organism vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus strain 19 live vaccine was used as a vector to express the Babesia bovis rhoptry-associated protein 1 (RAP1) as a fusion protein to increase immunogenicity by association with lipid moiety of OMP19 or beta-galactosidase amino acids. Efficacy: Mice immunized with recombinant strains developed specific humoral immune responses predominantly IgG2a against RAP1 and specific cellular immune responses to recombinant RAP1 were elicited in vitro. [Ref:6929]
c_preparation: Recombinant strains of B. abortus S19 expressing RAP1 fused either to the aminoterminal of outer membrane lipoprotein OMP19 (S19pBB19-RAP1) or to the first amino acids of beta-galactosidase (S19pBB-RAP1) were generated using plasmid expression systems.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 rfbD deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study developed a rfbD gene deleted mutant of Brucella abortus strain 19 to overcome shortcomings of the parental S19 vaccine such as residual virulence, abortion induction, and sero-diagnostic interference. Efficacy: S19ΔR showed a protective index of 1.90 against virulent Brucella abortus challenge in mice. [Ref:7148]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain S19ΔR exhibiting rough LPS phenotype confirmed by acriflavine dye-agglutination and LPS-SDS-PAGE analysis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine conjunctival
c_description: The vaccine has been used safely for about 100 years; conjunctival form used to provide mucosal immunity and short-term antibody response. Efficacy: No antibody response detected; threshold of 30 ICFTUs observed in one animal. [Ref:7265]
c_preparation: Two-dose conjunctival vaccine from vaccine brand B.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine mglA deletion mutant
c_description: The study evaluates the effect of mglA gene deletion on oxidative stress tolerance and survival within macrophages compared to the parental strain. Efficacy: The ∆mglA 3.14 mutant exhibited increased tolerance to H2O2 but did not show improved survival inside murine macrophages compared to the parental strain. [Ref:7166]
c_preparation: Live Brucella abortus strain 19 with mglA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine pulsed with lytic brucellaphage
c_description: The live attenuated Brucella abortus strain 19 organisms commonly used as a vaccine were employed to deliver a broad acting lytic brucellaphage inside phagocytes in vivo to reach virulent Brucella hiding intracellularly. Efficacy: The phage pulsed vaccine induced sustained and significantly high titers of anti-Brucella antibodies compared with untreated animals and animals vaccinated with S19 vaccine alone. [Ref:7208]
c_preparation: Brucella abortus strain 19 vaccine pulsed with lytic brucellaphage (phage pulsed vaccine preparation).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 virB5 gene deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A gene deletion mutant strain of Brucella abortus strain 19 with virB5 deletion was constructed as a molecular tag vaccine. [Ref:6977]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 wbkA gene deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to create a gene knockout mutant of Brucella abortus strain 19 by deleting the wbkA gene, which encodes part of the LPS O-chain, to reduce diagnostic interference and maintain attenuation. Efficacy: The wbkA mutant induced a splenocyte proliferative response in mice comparable or superior to parental S19 and RB51 strains, indicating immunogenicity. [Ref:7161]
c_preparation: A wbkA gene knockout mutant of Brucella abortus strain 19 was constructed to produce a strain deficient in LPS O-chain structure.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19 wzm gene deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Allelic exchange plasmids of wzm gene were constructed and partially knocked out in Brucella abortus S19 to evaluate effects on immunity induction. Efficacy: Immunity-eliciting ability was similar to wzt mutant but reduced compared with the S19 strain. [Ref:7002]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19-BA lipopolysaccharide vaccine
c_description: The study compared different lipopolysaccharide (LPS) preparations from Brucella abortus vaccine strain 19-BA on hematopoiesis in mice. Efficacy: LPS from B. abortus vaccine strain 19-BA had a less pronounced disturbing effect on hematopoiesis than LPS from B. melitensis virulent strain 565; none stimulated formation of transitory endogenous colonies in mouse spleen. [Ref:7255]
c_preparation: LPS preparations obtained by Boivin's technique, Westphal's technique, and mild alkaline hydrolysis of Boivin's active complex.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19-BA multiresistant vaccine
c_description: The study showed the possibility of preparing a Brucella abortus vaccine strain 19-BA with multiresistance to antibiotics by spontaneous induction of rifampicin resistance and transformation with a nonconjugative hybrid plasmid pOVI conferring resistance to multiple antibiotics. Efficacy: Immunization with the multiresistant vaccine strain GSA1 and the initial strain 19-BA was demonstrated in guinea pigs. [Ref:6925]
c_preparation: Live vaccine strain 19-BA with induced multiresistance to rifampicin, tetracycline, doxycycline, ampicillin, and streptomycin.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 19-BA vaccine
c_description: The vaccine strain 19-BA was administered to animals 3, 12, and 28 days after exposure to Artemisia absinthium pollen to study combined hypersensitivity. [Ref:7359]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308 ΔBAB1_0542 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The ABC transporter ATPase gene (BAB1_0542) of Brucella abortus strain 2308 was inactivated by deleting a 446-bp fragment, generating a mutant strain S2308ΔATP with a rough phenotype and attenuated virulence. Efficacy: The mutant strain S2308ΔATP showed attenuated virulence in vitro and in vivo; immunization with S2308ΔATP protected mice from challenge with virulent strain; complemented strain restored smooth phenotype and survival comparable to wild type. [Ref:6991]
c_preparation: Mutant strain S2308ΔATP with ABC transporter ATPase gene deletion, exhibiting rough phenotype and altered growth rate compared to wild type.
c_antigen: ABC transporter ATPase gene (BAB1_0542) deletion mutant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 delta ery live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A Brucella abortus 2308 ery promoter mutant (Δery) was constructed to overcome drawbacks of current vaccines S19 and RB51, aiming for a safer and more potent vaccine that allows differentiation between natural and vaccinated infection. Efficacy: The Δery mutant showed significantly attenuated growth in macrophages and mice and induced high protective immunity in mice against virulent Brucella abortus 2308 infection. [Ref:7011]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant with deletion in ery promoter (Δery mutant).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308ΔgntR bacterial ghost vaccine
