c_description: The study aimed to generate Brucella abortus ghosts by homologous recombination and bacterial ghost technologies to create a safe vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The 2308ΔgntR ghost induced high protective immunity against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain S2308 in BALB/c mice. [Ref:7169]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of bacterial ghosts derived from Brucella abortus strain 2308 with a gntR gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 delta gntR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The 2308ΔgntR mutant is a Brucella abortus strain 2308 with deletion of the transcriptional regulator gene gntR, which down regulates expression of virulence-related genes and attenuates virulence. Efficacy: The 2308ΔgntR mutant induced high protective immunity in BALB/c mice challenged with wild-type B. abortus 2308. [Ref:7093]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with gntR gene deletion; no adjuvant reported.
c_antigen: gntR deletion; regulated genes include omp25, virB1, vjbR, dnaK, htrA, hfq

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 delta NodV delta NodW live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a double deletion mutant of virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308, deleting the NodV and NodW genes encoding a two-component regulatory system on chromosome II, constructed to reduce virulence and allow serological differentiation from infected animals. Efficacy: The mutant showed significantly reduced survival in macrophages and mice, no splenomegaly in inoculated mice, and conferred high protective immunity against challenge with wild-type strain 2308 in BALB/c mice. [Ref:7077]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant strain 2308 with deletions in NodV and NodW genes; no adjuvant reported.
c_antigen: NodV and NodW (two-component regulatory system genes deleted)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 wbkA mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The Brucella abortus 2308 wbkA mutant (2308ΔwbkA) was constructed to evaluate its virulence and potential as a vaccine. Efficacy: The 2308ΔwbkA mutant showed attenuated survival in macrophages and mice and induced high protective immunity against wild-type infection. [Ref:7036]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletion of wbkA gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 2308 znuA purE double mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A double mutant strain was constructed from Brucella abortus 2308 by deleting znuA and purE genes to create a new, safe live vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Two doses of the double mutant conferred 0.79 log protection, similar to S19 vaccine; single dose of znuA mutant also conferred similar protection. [Ref:6947]
c_preparation: Live attenuated double mutant strain of Brucella abortus 2308 with deletions in znuA and purE genes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus 2308-SB6 ΔwboA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed as a rough-mutant strain with wboA gene deletion from Brucella abortus 2308 parent strain to evaluate effects of genetic background on virulence, pathogenicity, and protective immunity. Efficacy: Showed longer survival time in mice (11 weeks) but offered less protection against challenge compared to some other mutants. [Ref:6988]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 45/20 inactivated vaccine with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants
c_description: The study evaluated killed Brucella abortus strain 45/20 cells combined with immunopotentiators as a vaccine. Efficacy: Protection induced by bacterins containing 50 to 1,000 microgram of TDM or TDM-MDP was comparable to that of live strain 19 vaccine; bacterins with MDP alone were less effective. [Ref:7317]
c_preparation: 300 microgram of killed strain 45/20 cells in 1% oil emulsion with TDM, MDP, or both.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 45/20 outer membrane protein inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated nonliving vaccines derived from Brucella abortus rough strain 45/20 containing porin and other outer membrane protein antigens combined with trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide adjuvants. Efficacy: Outer membrane proteins induced highest antibody titers; increasing mineral oil improved antibody responses; immune responses sustained longer than 3 months after two vaccinations; no ill effects observed. [Ref:7310]
c_adjuvant: yes; trehalose dimycolate and muramyl dipeptide (N-acetylmuramyl-L-alpha-aminobutyryl-D-isoglutamine)
c_preparation: Vaccines contained trehalose dimycolate and a derivative of muramyl dipeptide at fixed doses; antigen types included whole cell, outer membrane, and detergent-extracted outer membrane proteins; mineral oil quantity was varied.
c_antigen: porin; outer membrane proteins; outer membrane; whole cell (rough strain 45/20)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 45/20 whole-cell vaccine
c_description: Whole cells of Brucella abortus strain 45/20 were combined with trehalose dimycolate or muramyl dipeptide as immunoadjuvants. Efficacy: Oil emulsions of whole cells with muramyl dipeptide reduced mean splenic Brucella by 95.1%; oil emulsions with trehalose dimycolate reduced mean splenic Brucella by 99.3% compared to controls; saline suspensions were not significantly effective. [Ref:7316]
c_preparation: Whole cells combined with trehalose dimycolate or muramyl dipeptide in oil emulsions; also tested as saline suspensions.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 544 inactivated vaccine
c_description: A purified killed vaccine developed for use in man from the smooth strain 544 and previously tested in mice. Efficacy: Highly active and immunizing in mice and guinea-pigs; immunization in guinea-pigs without adjuvant; activity enhanced by water-in-oil emulsions. [Ref:7306]
c_preparation: Whole-culture extract; activity enhanced by water-in-oil emulsions; no adjuvant required for immunization in guinea-pigs.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 544 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Mice were infected intravenously with small numbers of live CO2-dependent Brucella abortus 544 used as vaccinal strain. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed accelerated decrease in bacterial counts preventing multiplication of challenge strain in spleens and livers compared to normal mice. [Ref:7337]
c_preparation: Live CO2-dependent Brucella abortus 544 bacteria.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 82 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the combined use of a live Brucella abortus strain 82 vaccine and a homologous lysed antigen (glucopeptide) to enhance immune response. Efficacy: The combined administration increased the number of immune animals by 1.5-2 times compared to animals receiving only one preparation. [Ref:7314]
c_preparation: Live brucellosis vaccine from Brucella abortus strain 82 combined sequentially with a lysed low-molecular Brucella component (glucopeptide).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain 82-PS vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the immunopotentiation of the live Brucella abortus strain 82-PS vaccine by various adjuvants. Efficacy: Adjuvants enhanced both humoral and cellular immune responses, correlating with increased protection against experimental challenge; highest protection was observed with TNF-beta or polyoxidonium combined with the vaccine. [Ref:6952]
c_adjuvant: yes; larifan; polyoxidonium; natrium thiosulphate; TNF-beta; Ribi adjuvant system
c_preparation: Live Brucella abortus strain 82-PS vaccine combined with different adjuvants including larifan, polyoxidonium (PO), natrium thiosulphate (NT), TNF-beta, and Ribi adjuvant system (RAS).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain A19 btpB deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A btpB mutant strain of Brucella abortus strain A19 (ΔbtpB) was constructed by homologous recombination to investigate its biological characteristics, virulence, and immunogenicity. Efficacy: ΔbtpB showed reduced virulence with weaker splenic pathological damage and significantly lower splenic bacterial load compared to wild-type A19, indicating accelerated clearance in the host. [Ref:7297]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain A19 with btpB gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain A19 delta VirB12 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The A19-delta VirB12 deletion mutant of Brucella abortus was constructed by homologous recombination technology. Efficacy: The A19-delta VirB12 mutant provided statistically significant protection against Brucella abortus 2308 challenge, comparable to the parental A19 strain. [Ref:7006]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with VirB12 gene deletion, administered intraperitoneally at 5.0 x 10^4 CFU dose.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain A19 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The live B. abortus A19 strain vaccine is a widespread vaccine in China but has residual virulence concerns. Efficacy: The combined low dose live vaccine plus inactivated vaccine group showed splenic bacterial burden and spleen weight equivalent to the high dose live vaccine group; both conferred protective immunity against B. abortus strain 2308 challenge. [Ref:7203]
c_preparation: Live B. abortus A19 strain at 10^5 CFU/mL (low dose) or 10^6 CFU/mL (high dose) was used alone or combined with inactivated B. abortus A19 strain at 10^9 CFU/mL.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain A19 vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus strain A19 is a spontaneously attenuated vaccine strain that has been used in vaccination of cattle against brucellosis. [Ref:7139]
c_antigen: eryC; eryD; eryF; outer membrane protein; 2-isopropylmalate synthase; citramalate synthase; GntR family transcriptional regulator; ABC transporters

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain BA15 cydC cydD double deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed from virulent Brucella abortus biovar 1 field isolate (BA15) by deleting genes encoding ATP-binding cassette-type transporter (cydC and cydD). Efficacy: Highly attenuated; cleared from spleens by 4 weeks post-inoculation; no splenomegaly; induced long-term protective immunity; provided significantly better protection than commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine. [Ref:7050]
c_preparation: Live double deletion mutant without adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain BA15 cydC purD double deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed from virulent Brucella abortus biovar 1 field isolate (BA15) by deleting genes encoding ATP-binding cassette-type transporter (cydC) and phosphoribosylamine-glycine ligase (purD). Efficacy: Highly attenuated; cleared from spleens by 4 weeks post-inoculation; no splenomegaly; induced long-term protective immunity; provided significantly better protection than commercial Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine. [Ref:7050]
c_preparation: Live double deletion mutant without adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain delta eipB delta per delta wadC live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study engineered a recombinant Brucella abortus strain Bru-M3 by deleting eipB, per, and wadC genes to remodel noncanonical LPS and produce outer-membrane vesicles (OMVs) at higher yield and enhanced immunogenicity compared to wild-type OMVs. Efficacy: OMVBru-M3 vaccination conferred better protection against Brucella abortus challenge, improved bacterial clearance, and reduced tissue damage compared to wild-type OMVs. [Ref:7289]
c_preparation: Biological nanoparticles (outer-membrane vesicles) derived from the recombinant Bru-M3 strain (OMVBru-M3).
c_antigen: eipB deletion; per deletion; wadC deletion; noncanonical lipopolysaccharide (LPS) remodeling

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus Δpgm recombinant vector vaccine expressing E. coli O157:H7 EspA, Intimin, Tir and H7 flagellin
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A bivalent vaccine was developed to prevent transmission from cattle to humans of Brucella abortus and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC). Efficacy: Mice immunized with BabΔpgm(EITH7) cleared intestinal E. coli O157:H7 infection three times faster (4 days) than mice immunized with BabΔpgm carrier strain (12 days); also elicited protective immune response against Brucella abortus infection. [Ref:7027]
c_preparation: A 66kDa chimeric antigen composed of EspA, Intimin, Tir, and H7 flagellin (EITH7) from STEC was constructed and expressed in Brucella abortus Δpgm vaccine strain (BabΔpgm).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain IVK15 delta cydC live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked mutant by deleting cydC gene encoding ATP-binding cassette transporter protein from virulent Brucella abortus isolate IVK15 from Korean cow. Efficacy: Provided better protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 than commercial B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine in mice. [Ref:7063]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain IVK15ΔcydC.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain IVK15 delta cydD live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked mutant by deleting cydD gene encoding ATP-binding cassette transporter protein from virulent Brucella abortus isolate IVK15 from Korean cow. Efficacy: Provided better protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 than commercial B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine in mice. [Ref:7063]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain IVK15ΔcydD.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain M-1 BP26-deficient live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A genetically engineered Brucella abortus mutant strain M-1 lacking BP26 expression was evaluated for protective properties compared to the parental S19 vaccine strain. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with M-1 were similarly protected as those vaccinated with S19 against challenge. [Ref:7354]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain M-1 mutant vaccine deficient in BP26 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 beta-galactosidase live virulent vaccine
c_description: Recombinant strain RB51 constructed to express E. coli beta-galactosidase under Brucella groE or sodC promoters. Efficacy: Recombinant RB51 expressing beta-galactosidase maintained attenuation and protective efficacy against B. abortus 2308 challenge. [Ref:6870]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain RB51 bacteria transformed with plasmids expressing beta-galactosidase.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 cydC cydD double deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. Efficacy: Single immunization with mutants induced lower protection than parental RB51; booster immunization with mutants provided significant protection against both homologous B. abortus and heterologous B. canis challenge. [Ref:7042]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 cydC deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. Efficacy: Single immunization with mutants induced lower protection than parental RB51; booster immunization with mutants provided significant protection against both homologous B. abortus and heterologous B. canis challenge. [Ref:7042]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated.
c_antigen: cydC deletion; cydD deletion; purD deletion; cydC cydD double deletion; cydC purD double deletion

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 cydC purD double deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. Efficacy: Single immunization with mutants induced lower protection than parental RB51; booster immunization with mutants provided significant protection against both homologous B. abortus and heterologous B. canis challenge. [Ref:7042]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 cydD deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. Efficacy: Single immunization with mutants induced lower protection than parental RB51; booster immunization with mutants provided significant protection against both homologous B. abortus and heterologous B. canis challenge. [Ref:7042]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 delta leuB recombinant FliC FSH beta live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This vaccine candidate is a Brucella abortus strain RB51 with a leuB gene deletion expressing Salmonella typhimurium FliC protein conjugated to porcine follicle stimulating hormone beta subunit (FSHβ) DNA sequences, designed as an immunocontraceptive and protective vaccine. Efficacy: Significant reduction in fertility characteristics observed in both male and female mice. [Ref:7186]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 ΔleuB genetically engineered to express Salmonella FliC conjugated to FSHβ DNA sequences.
c_antigen: leuB deletion; Salmonella typhimurium FliC; porcine follicle stimulating hormone beta subunit (FSHβ)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 delta leuB recombinant FliC GnRH live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: This vaccine candidate is a Brucella abortus strain RB51 with a leuB gene deletion expressing Salmonella typhimurium FliC protein conjugated to gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH) DNA sequences, designed as an immunocontraceptive and protective vaccine. Efficacy: Significant reduction in fertility characteristics observed in both male and female mice. [Ref:7186]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 ΔleuB genetically engineered to express Salmonella FliC conjugated to GnRH DNA sequences.
c_antigen: leuB deletion; Salmonella typhimurium FliC; gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 HSP65 live virulent vaccine
c_description: Recombinant strain RB51 constructed to express M. bovis HSP65 under Brucella groE promoter. Efficacy: Expression of HSP65 did not alter attenuation or vaccine efficacy of strain RB51 against B. abortus 2308 challenge. [Ref:6870]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain RB51 bacteria transformed with plasmids expressing HSP65.
c_antigen: 65-kDa heat shock protein (HSP65) of Mycobacterium bovis

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 live attenuated vaccine expressing ESAT-6 fusion protein
c_description: A recombinant RB51 strain expressing ESAT-6, a protective protein of Mycobacterium bovis, as a fusion protein with the signal sequence and additional amino terminal amino acids of SOD. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with RB51ESAT showed significantly enhanced protection against Brucella challenge compared to strain RB51 alone. [Ref:6888]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 strain genetically modified to express ESAT-6 fusion protein.
c_antigen: ESAT-6 (Mycobacterium bovis protective protein); Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase signal sequence fusion

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 live attenuated vaccine gamma irradiated recombinant
c_description: Brucella abortus strain RB51 is an attenuated rough mutant used as a live vaccine against bovine brucellosis. A recombinant RB51 strain expressing E. coli beta-galactosidase was gamma-irradiated to eliminate replicative ability while retaining metabolic activity and antigen expression. Efficacy: Gamma-irradiated recombinant RB51 induced significant protection against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus in mice, whereas heat-killed vaccine did not. [Ref:6913]
c_preparation: Gamma-irradiated recombinant RB51 strain expressing beta-galactosidase; irradiated at minimum 300 kilorads to abolish replication but maintain metabolic activity and antigen synthesis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 live attenuated vaccine overexpressing Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase and Mycobacterium 85A protein
c_description: A recombinant RB51 strain engineered to overexpress Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase and simultaneously express 85A, a protective protein of Mycobacterium spp. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with RB51SOD/85A showed significantly enhanced protection against Brucella challenge compared to strain RB51 alone. [Ref:6888]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 strain genetically modified to overexpress SOD and express 85A protein.
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); 85A (Mycobacterium spp. protective protein)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine overexpressing sodC and wboA
c_description: The vaccine was developed to protect elk from Brucella abortus infection, addressing the expanding range of infected elk in the Greater Yellowstone Area and the risk of transmission to cattle. Efficacy: The recombinant vaccine did not protect elk against brucellosis after experimental challenge. [Ref:7061]
c_preparation: Recombinant live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51 overexpressing superoxide dismutase and glycosyltransferase genes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 overexpressing sodC and wboA vaccine
c_description: Investigated as a recombinant RB51 strain vaccine candidate to improve immune response and protection in bison. Efficacy: RB51+sodC,wboA vaccinated bison did not have greater protection from abortion or infection compared to nonvaccinates; less efficacious than parental RB51 strain. [Ref:890]
c_preparation: 7.4 x 10^10 CFU of RB51+sodC,wboA administered to bison.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 purD deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Brucella abortus attenuated strain RB51 vaccine is widely used for prevention of bovine brucellosis but has drawbacks including residual virulence; gene deletion mutants of RB51 were constructed to increase safety. Efficacy: Single immunization with mutants induced lower protection than parental RB51; booster immunization with mutants provided significant protection against both homologous B. abortus and heterologous B. canis challenge. [Ref:7042]
c_preparation: Live attenuated RB51 mutants with single deletions (ΔcydC, ΔcydD, ΔpurD) and double deletions (ΔcydCΔcydD, ΔcydCΔpurD) were generated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 purD mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study used transposon mutagenesis to create purD and purF gene mutants of the Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine to further attenuate the strain. Efficacy: Immunization with purD mutant protected mice against virulent B. abortus strain 544 challenge at a level similar to the parent RB51 strain; mutants showed significantly decreased intracellular survival and lowered persistence in mice. [Ref:7022]
c_preparation: Mutants of RB51 strain with disrupted purD or purF genes were constructed and characterized.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51 purF mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study used transposon mutagenesis to create purF and purD gene mutants of the Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine to further attenuate the strain. Efficacy: Immunization with purF mutant protected mice against virulent B. abortus strain 544 challenge at a level similar to the parent RB51 strain; mutants showed significantly decreased intracellular survival and lowered persistence in mice. [Ref:7022]
c_preparation: Mutants of RB51 strain with disrupted purF or purD genes were constructed and characterized.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus RB51 recombinant vaccine expressing LLO, BAX and SMAC
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The RB51 strain is a live attenuated vaccine with low side effects but insufficient protective efficacy. To enhance efficacy and safety, RB51 was genetically modified to express Listeria monocytogenes listeriolysin O (LLO), and apoptotic proteins BAX and SMAC. Efficacy: Recombinant RB51 strains expressing mLLO and BAX-SMAC showed higher cytotoxicity, reduced macrophage survival, and increased apoptosis and necrosis compared to parental RB51. Vaccination with RB51-mLLO-BAX-SMAC enhanced Th1 immune response in mice, indicating improved potency. [Ref:7202]
c_preparation: RB51 was transformed with two broad-host-range plasmids: pbbr1ori-LLO containing LLO, and pBlu-mLLO-BAX-SMAC containing mutant LLO and BAX-SMAC fusion gene, generating recombinant RB51 strains.
c_antigen: listeriolysin O (LLO); mutant LLO (mLLO); BAX; SMAC

c_vaccine_name: Methanol-killed Brucella abortus RB51 polyanhydride VPEAR vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Whole organism vaccine
c_description: The study reports fabrication of an implantable single dose polyanhydride-based, methanol-killed RB51 antigen containing delivery platform (VPEAR) for vaccination against bovine brucellosis. Efficacy: Initial vaccination with VPEAR did not induce measurable RB51-specific IFN-γ or IgG responses in peripheral blood; however, a subsequent booster with live RB51 induced an anamnestic response comparable in magnitude and kinetics to live RB51 vaccination alone; IgG titers were significantly higher in VPEAR vaccinated animals after booster. [Ref:7140]
c_preparation: Polyanhydride-based implantable delivery platform containing methanol-killed RB51 antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51leuB live attenuated vaccine over-expressing SOD
c_description: A recombinant Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph was engineered to over-express SOD alone to protect against Brucella suis infection. Efficacy: Significant protection compared to control; less effective than the strain over-expressing SOD and WboA. [Ref:6964]
c_preparation: Strain RB51leuB with an antibiotic-resistance marker free plasmid over-expressing SOD.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51leuB live attenuated vaccine over-expressing SOD and L7/L12
c_description: A recombinant Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph was engineered to over-express SOD and L7/L12 ribosomal protein to protect against Brucella suis infection. Efficacy: Significant protection compared to control; less effective than the strain over-expressing SOD and WboA. [Ref:6964]
c_preparation: Strain RB51leuB with an antibiotic-resistance marker free plasmid over-expressing SOD and L7/L12.
c_antigen: Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); L7/L12 ribosomal protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51leuB live attenuated vaccine over-expressing SOD and WboA
c_description: An improved recombinant Brucella abortus strain RB51 leucine auxotroph (strain RB51leuB) was developed to over-express homologous proteins SOD, L7/L12, and WboA to protect against Brucella suis infection. Efficacy: All vaccine groups significantly protected mice compared to controls (P<0.05); the strain RB51leuB/SOD/WboA vaccine provided significantly better protection than strains RB51leuB/SOD or RB51leuB/SOD/L7/L12. [Ref:6964]
c_preparation: Strain RB51leuB was used as a platform with an antibiotic-resistance marker free plasmid to construct strains over-expressing SOD alone, SOD and L7/L12, or SOD and WboA.
c_antigen: Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); L7/L12 ribosomal protein; glycosyl-transferase (WboA)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51WboA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study complemented the Brucella abortus strain RB51 vaccine with a functional wboA gene to restore O-antigen synthesis and investigate effects on phenotype and vaccine efficacy. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with RB51WboA showed better protection against challenge with virulent Brucella abortus strain 2308 compared to those vaccinated with RB51. [Ref:189]
c_preparation: Live RB51 strain complemented with functional wboA gene (RB51WboA).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain RB51WboAKF live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine strain RB51WboAKF was generated by overexpressing the wbkF gene in Brucella abortus strain RB51 complemented with wboA gene (RB51WboA) to increase O-polysaccharide synthesis. Efficacy: Immunization with RB51WboAKF conferred enhanced protection against virulent B. abortus 2308, B. melitensis 16M, and B. suis 1330 challenge compared to RB51 and RB51WboA vaccine strains. [Ref:7127]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain RB51WboAKF with overexpression of wbkF gene and complemented wboA gene, phenotypically rough but expressing higher levels of O-polysaccharide.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain S19-RB6 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed as a rough-mutant strain with wboA gene deletion from Brucella abortus strain S19 parent strain to evaluate effects of genetic background on virulence, pathogenicity, and protective immunity. Efficacy: Shorter survival time in mice (less than 6 weeks) but offered better protection against Brucella abortus 2308 challenge than some other mutants; did not induce abortion in pregnant sheep. [Ref:6988]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain S2308 Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase deletion mutants of Brucella abortus S2308, a virulent strain, were generated by gene replacement to analyze survival and pathogenicity. Efficacy: The S2308 Cu-Zn SOD mutant showed lower splenic levels and reduced spleen weights in infected mice compared to wild-type S2308, indicating reduced survival and pathogenicity. [Ref:6908]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella abortus strain S2308 with Cu-Zn SOD gene deletion replaced by a kanamycin resistance marker.
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (Cu-Zn SOD) deletion mutant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus strain znBAZ live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The live, double-mutant B. abortus (znBAZ) strain was used for mucosal vaccination to induce protection against pulmonary challenge with wild-type Brucella. Efficacy: The znBAZ strain resulted in nearly complete protection of mice against pulmonary challenge with wild-type Brucella, associated with a dominant CD8+ T cell response; NK cell depletion impaired dendritic cell activation and migration and reduced CD8+ T cell numbers threefold. [Ref:7193]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus T cell peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify MHC-I- and MHC-II-restricted T cell epitopes of Brucella abortus and evaluate their vaccine potential in mice as a safer alternative to current animal vaccines that cause abortions and are pathogenic to humans. Efficacy: Mice immunized with peptide formulations showed significantly higher splenocyte proliferation and IFN-γ production and significant protection compared to PBS controls. The DNA vaccine construct also conferred significant protection (1.66 protection units) compared to PBS and empty vector controls. [Ref:7039]
c_preparation: Selected peptides were co-administered either entrapped in PLG microparticles (EPLG-Pep) or adsorbed on PLG microparticles (APLG-Pep).
c_antigen: MHC-I- and MHC-II-restricted T cell peptides

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus translation initiation factor 3 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Semliki Forest virus (SFV) particles carrying RNA encoding Brucella abortus translation initiation factor 3 (IF3) were constructed as a replication-deficient vector vaccine. Efficacy: Mice immunized with SFV-IF3 showed significant resistance to challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 (P<0.01). [Ref:6939]
c_preparation: Infectious but replication-deficient SFV particles encoding IF3 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus translation initiation factor 3 subunit vaccine
c_description: The infC gene encoding IF3 was cloned, sequenced, and expressed in Escherichia coli to produce recombinant protein. Efficacy: Previous reports indicated immunoprotective capacity; current study showed strong lymphocyte proliferation and gamma interferon production upon stimulation. [Ref:6940]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant Brucella IF3 protein was used.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus truncated Omp2b subunit vaccine; Brucella abortus truncated Omp2b DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immunogenicity and protective efficacy of truncated Omp2b from Brucella abortus using three immunization regimens: Protein/Protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/Protein. Efficacy: Protein/Protein and DNA/Protein vaccination regimens conferred protection levels against B. abortus challenge comparable to the licensed B. abortus strain RB51 vaccine. [Ref:7083]
c_preparation: Protein subunit vaccine and DNA vaccine formulations of truncated Omp2b were used in different prime-boost combinations.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus U-Omp19 subunit vaccine (co-delivered with OVA/Trypanosoma cruzi antigens)
c_description: The study investigated the use of the outer membrane protein U-Omp19 from Brucella spp. co-administered subcutaneously with an antigen to enhance antigen-specific T helper 1 immune responses. Efficacy: Co-administration of U-Omp19 with Trypanosoma cruzi antigens conferred protection against virulent parasite challenge, reducing parasitemia and weight loss, and increasing survival in mice. [Ref:7053]
c_preparation: Recombinant U-Omp19 protein co-delivered subcutaneously with an antigen (OVA or Trypanosoma cruzi antigens).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus UvrA subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Brucella abortus proteins UvrA, GroES, and GroEL were produced as fusion proteins in E. coli and purified for evaluation as potential vaccine antigens. Efficacy: Not directly reported; proteins induced T cell proliferation and Th1 cytokine secretion, and elicited DTH responses, suggesting potential protective capacity. [Ref:7353]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion proteins expressed in E. coli and purified by affinity chromatography.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus virB2 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked deletion mutants of virB2 gene in Brucella abortus as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: Provided less protection compared to Deltaasp24 mutants against heterologous challenge. [Ref:700]
c_preparation: Live attenuated unmarked deletion mutant of virB2 gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus virB4 mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The virB4 mutant is an intracellular growth-defective mutant of Brucella abortus used to study abortion induction. Efficacy: The virB4 mutant did not induce abortion in pregnant mice. [Ref:6901]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus VirB8 subunit vaccine
c_description: VirB8 was selected as a conserved antigen candidate from compositive reverse vaccinology screening Efficacy: VirB8 substantially reduced the organ bacterial load of B. abortus S19 in mice and provided varying degrees of protection [Ref:7192]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus VirJ subunit vaccine
c_description: Current vaccines are ineffective in chronically infected animals; this study uses recombinant in vivo-induced antigens identified by IVIAT to develop potential vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccination with VirJ appeared to have some effect on clearance kinetics. [Ref:6965]
c_preparation: Recombinant VirJ protein expressed and purified from E. coli, adjuvanted, and delivered subcutaneously with two boosts.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus wbkA mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The rough wbkA mutant is attenuated and previously shown to be a better vaccine than RB51 in mice. Efficacy: The wbkA mutant alone protected against virulent B. abortus but less effectively than when combined with the bvrS mutant; combination provided better protection than B. abortus strain 19 vaccine. [Ref:6914]
c_preparation: Live wbkA mutant cells used alone or in combination with live bvrS mutant, inactivated bvrS cells, or purified S-LPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus wbkC gene disruption live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Rough mutants of Brucella abortus were generated by disruption of the wbkC gene, which encodes the formyltransferase enzyme involved in LPS biosynthesis. Efficacy: The wbkC mutant strains were attenuated in macrophages and mice; they induced lower protective immunity in C57BL/6 mice than the smooth vaccine strain S19 but similar protection to the rough vaccine RB51. [Ref:6953]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella abortus wboA deletion mutant vaccine
c_description: The study investigates rough wboA mutants derived from Brucella abortus 2308 and Brucella melitensis 16M, which lack O polysaccharide due to deletion of the wboA gene essential for O chain synthesis. Efficacy: Rough B. abortus wboA mutants were more sensitive to bactericidal action of serum than rough B. melitensis mutants; OPS-deficient B. melitensis mutants were more resistant than B. abortus mutants; complement deposition and killing occurred via classical and MBL-mediated pathways. [Ref:6877]
c_preparation: Rough mutants of Brucella abortus and Brucella melitensis with wboA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Ag85A DNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to explore whether the Ag85A DNA vaccine could mount a more efficient protective immune response through new RNA sensor and signal transduction pathways of antigen presentation. Efficacy: Not directly reported; however, increased expression of RNA sensors and adaptors and increased MHC II expression suggest enhanced antigen presentation potential. [Ref:7104]
c_preparation: Ag85A gene fragment containing multiple point mutations was designed and synthesized and transfected into dendritic cell line DC2.4 by CRISPR/Cas9.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella antigens vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to prepare an absorbable, injectable, and biocompatible hydroxypropyl chitin (HPCT) thermosensitive hydrogel as a novel adjuvant for Brucella antigens to improve upon alum's disadvantages. Efficacy: HPCT hydrogel as an adjuvant showed better specific antibody expression levels and cytokine (Interleukin-4, Interferon-γ) expression levels than alum, indicating enhanced immunization efficacy. [Ref:7258]
c_adjuvant: yes; hydroxypropyl chitin thermosensitive hydrogel (HPCT hydrogel)
c_preparation: HPCT hydrogel was synthesized by etherification modification of marine natural polysaccharide chitin to obtain hydroxypropyl chitin; the hydrogel demonstrated reversible temperature sensitivity and could load and continuously release bovine serum albumin as a model protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella AtpA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. [Ref:7212]
c_antigen: AtpA; AtpD; DnaK; BAbS19_II02030; Muri; AcpP; GroES

c_vaccine_name: Brucella AtpD subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. [Ref:7212]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BAbS19_II02030 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. [Ref:7212]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella bacterioferritin DNA vaccine
c_description: Eukaryotic expression vector pCIBFR encoding bacterioferritin constructed and verified for protein expression in COS-7 cells. Efficacy: Induced a strong and long-lived memory immune response lasting at least 3 months; elicited a typical T-helper 1-dominated immune response; did not induce moderate protection against B. abortus 544 challenge. [Ref:2291]
c_preparation: Intramuscular injection of plasmid DNA vector pCIBFR, administered three times at 3-week intervals.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BhuA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safer and more effective vaccine alternative to commercial live vaccines by evaluating BhuA antigen with or without adjuvant. Efficacy: Immunization with BhuA protein plus poly I:C induced higher protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus than protein alone and comparable protection to live attenuated vaccines. [Ref:7196]
c_preparation: Recombinant BhuA protein formulated with poly I:C adjuvant or as naked protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BP26 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study addresses the urgent need for a safe and effective human vaccine against brucellosis and explores recombinant protein-based subunit vaccines as promising candidates. Efficacy: The vaccine candidate induced strong cellular immune responses and high levels of specific antibodies, suggesting potential protective efficacy. [Ref:7240]
c_preparation: Recombinant BP26 protein expressed in prokaryotic systems combined with the CpG-ODN adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella BtuB and LptD RNA vaccine
c_description: The study designed a novel multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting the extracellular proteins BtuB and LptD of Brucella, aiming to stimulate cellular and humoral immunity using immunoinformatics tools. [Ref:7241]
c_preparation: The vaccine was constructed from five cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes, ten helper T lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes, and eight B cell epitopes derived from BtuB and LptD proteins; codon optimization and in silico cloning indicated efficient transcription and translation in E. coli; secondary and tertiary structures were predicted and docked with TLR-4; molecular dynamics simulation confirmed vaccine stability.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis BLSOmp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Polymeric antigen BLSOmp31 is an immunogenic vaccine candidate that confers protection against Brucella canis in mice. This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of BLSOmp31 adsorbed to aluminum hydroxide gel in Beagle dogs. Efficacy: The vaccine elicited specific antibodies 3 weeks after the first immunization; annual booster induced comparable antibody responses. Antibodies showed high complement-dependent bactericidal activity against B. canis and enhanced bacterial uptake and destruction by neutrophils. Specific IgG was detected in preputial secretions of most immunized dogs. Humoral response did not interfere with routine agglutination tests. [Ref:7078]
c_preparation: BLSOmp31 antigen adsorbed to aluminum hydroxide gel (BLSOmp31-AH).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Canine brucellosis caused by Brucella canis currently lacks a vaccine; this study evaluates Omp31 as a candidate antigen for vaccine development. Efficacy: Recombinant Omp31 with different adjuvants and the prime-boost strategy conferred protection against B. canis infection in mice. [Ref:7020]
c_adjuvant: yes; incomplete Freund adjuvant; aluminum hydroxide; Quil A; Montanide IMS 3012 VGPR
c_preparation: Recombinant Omp31 antigen formulated with various adjuvants (incomplete Freund adjuvant, aluminum hydroxide, Quil A, Montanide IMS 3012 VGPR); plasmid pCIOmp31 DNA vaccine; and a prime-boost strategy with pCIOmp31 plasmid followed by recombinant Omp31 protein boost.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis strain RM-6-66 aqueous ether extract vaccine
c_description: The study examined immunogenic properties of aqueous ether extracts prepared from Brucella canis strain RM-6-66 cells. Efficacy: The aqueous ether-extracted material protected mice against Brucella suis infections. [Ref:7307]
c_preparation: Aqueous ether extract prepared from Brucella canis strain RM-6-66 cells grown on tryptose agar, ether removed, clarified by centrifugation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis strain RM6/66 delta vjbR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate is a live attenuated strain of Brucella canis RM6/66 with a deletion in the vjbR gene developed to protect against canine brucellosis, a disease with no current vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant protection against organ colonization and histopathologic lesions after challenge; booster or adjuvant did not enhance protection. [Ref:7165]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella canis RM6/66 ΔvjbR strain administered at 10^9 CFU by intraperitoneal and subcutaneous routes; adjuvant addition or booster dose did not improve protection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis virB10 mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A non-polar virB10 mutant was constructed in Brucella canis to reduce virulence. Efficacy: The virB10 mutant was cleared by day 21 post-infection and significantly reduced CFU recovery after challenge with wild-type B. canis at day 15, indicating protective immunity. [Ref:6982]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella canis virB10 mutant strain.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella canis virB11 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A virB11 deletion mutant was constructed in Brucella canis to reduce virulence. Efficacy: The virB11 mutant was cleared by day 21 post-infection; no significant reduction in CFU after challenge reported. [Ref:6982]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella canis virB11 deletion mutant strain.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella chemical inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to determine the optimal inoculation dose of the Brucella chemical vaccine. Efficacy: The 1 mg dose produced the highest percentage of seroconversions, highest agglutinin titers, and longest persistence of antibodies among the tested doses. [Ref:7319]
c_preparation: Chemical vaccine administered intramuscularly at doses ranging from 0.5 mg to 2 mg.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella DnaK subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified potential antigenic peptides from Brucella proteins through proteome and peptidome analyses, aiming to find candidate targets for subunit vaccine design. [Ref:7212]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella EipB subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to encapsulate recombinant EipB protein into PLGA nanoparticles to develop a new vaccine candidate addressing limitations of existing Brucellosis vaccines. Efficacy: Vaccine candidate conferred higher than 90% protection from Brucella infection in challenge experiments. [Ref:7247]
c_preparation: Recombinant EipB protein produced by recombinant DNA technology was encapsulated into PLGA nanoparticles using double emulsion solvent evaporation technique; nanoparticles characterized for size (~274 nm), morphology, zeta potential, polydispersity, release profile (56.1% release by day 14), and encapsulation efficiency.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella FliC subunit vaccine
c_description: The study tested FliC antigen as a potential safer vaccine candidate against brucellosis. Efficacy: FliC protein plus poly I:C provided higher protection than protein alone and comparable to live attenuated vaccines. [Ref:7196]
c_preparation: Recombinant FliC protein with or without poly I:C adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella four antigen recombinant vector live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A novel anti-Brucella vaccine was developed utilizing rough Salmonella delivering four Brucella antigens to overcome residual virulence and abortion issues of current live Brucella vaccines. Efficacy: Partial protection observed with 33.3% (2/6) of vaccinated midterm pregnant guinea pigs protected from abortion after challenge; lower Brucella recovery in spleen and liver and reduced histopathological burden compared to controls. [Ref:7122]
c_preparation: Rough Salmonella vector delivering four Brucella antigens administered intraperitoneally at 4 × 10^8 CFU.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella GroEL subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identifies GroEL as a Brucella immunodominant antigen using nanobody technology and MALDI-TOF-MS, suggesting its potential as a candidate antigen for next generation vaccine development. [Ref:6975]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella hfq deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The hfq gene, encoding a bacterial chaperone protein involved in stress survival and regulation of virulence genes, was deleted to create a mutant strain. Efficacy: The hfq-deletion mutant induced protective immune responses against challenge with wild-type Brucella 16M, demonstrating significant attenuation and protection. [Ref:7058]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella strain with hfq gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella IL-12 immunotherapy
c_description: The study investigates the role of IL-12 treatment in enhancing immunity against Brucella infection in susceptible mice. Efficacy: IL-12 treatment resulted in a 1000-fold reduction in bacterial CFU during primary infection and increased survival following secondary challenge. [Ref:6923]
c_preparation: Recombinant IL-12 administered to mice.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella L7/L12 DNA vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the ability of a DNA vaccine encoding the L7/L12 protein of Brucella sp. to induce cellular and humoral immune responses. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed lower bacterial cfu compared to control groups, indicating vaccine efficiency. [Ref:2102]
c_preparation: DNA vaccine encoding L7/L12 gene delivered by intramuscular injection; three vaccinations at 3 week intervals.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella L7/L12 TOmp31 SOmp2b subunit vaccine
c_description: A cocktail protein vaccine composed of recombinant Brucella L7/L12 ribosomal protein, truncated outer membrane protein 31 (TOmp31), and SOmp2b was formulated with two different adjuvants to evaluate protective efficacy. Efficacy: Both vaccine regimens conferred protection levels comparable to live vaccines against Brucella challenge; the formulation with CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70VG induced higher protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus than the Poly (I:C) formulation. [Ref:7114]
c_adjuvant: yes; CpG ODN 1826 + Montanide ISA 70VG or Poly (I:C)
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated with either CpG ODN 1826 plus Montanide ISA 70VG adjuvants or Poly (I:C) adjuvant.
c_antigen: L7/L12 ribosomal protein; truncated outer membrane protein 31 (TOmp31); SOmp2b recombinant protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella L7/L12 truncated Omp31 DNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate and compare the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the L7/L12-TOmp31 construct administered as DNA/DNA and DNA/protein vaccine regimens. Efficacy: The DNA/Pro regimen provided higher protection levels against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge compared to the DNA/DNA regimen. [Ref:7033]
c_preparation: The vaccine was administered as a DNA priming followed by protein boosting regimen (DNA/Pro) or DNA alone (DNA/DNA).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella live attenuated vaccine using rough Salmonella vector
c_description: An anti-Brucella vaccine candidate was developed using a rough Salmonella vector delivering Brucella antigens to mimic active intracellular Brucella infection, aiming to provide significant protection with a single dose and improved safety. [Ref:7100]
c_preparation: Live rough Salmonella bacterial vector delivering Brucella antigens; administered orally or subcutaneously.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella live attenuated vaccine using virmugen gene mutants
c_description: Live attenuated vaccines are generated by mutation of genes encoding virulence factors ("virmugens") that have been proven feasible in animal models to make live attenuated vaccines by knocking out these genes. [Ref:6987]
c_antigen: virmugen genes related to carbohydrate or nucleotide transport and metabolism; genes involving cell membrane biogenesis

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase and Shiga toxin type 2 B subunit subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel immunogen was engineered by inserting the B subunit of Shiga toxin type 2 at the amino termini of Brucella lumazine synthase, creating a chimera designed to induce strong and long-lasting neutralizing antibodies. Efficacy: Immunized mice were completely protected against intravenous Stx2 challenge; immune sera transfer conferred complete protection to weaned mice against oral EHEC challenge. [Ref:7000]
c_preparation: Chimera consisting of the B subunit of Shiga toxin type 2 fused to Brucella lumazine synthase, a highly stable dimer of pentamers serving as a scaffold for foreign antigen display.
c_antigen: B subunit of Shiga toxin type 2; brucella lumazine synthase

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase OVA(257-264) subunit vaccine
c_description: The study introduces a polymeric protein chimera based on Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) fused with the OVA(257-264) peptide, designed to induce immunity without adjuvants. Efficacy: Immunization induced rapid activation and proliferation of OVA(257-264)-specific CD8+ T cells, generation of CD8+ effector cells, and a strong peptide-specific cytotoxic response dependent on TLR4 signaling. [Ref:6984]
c_preparation: A decameric BLS protein with covalently attached OVA(257-264) peptide, administered without adjuvants.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase Stx2 B subunit subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel immunogen was developed based on the B subunit of Shiga toxin 2 (Stx2B) and the enzyme lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) to protect against Stx2-associated damage. Efficacy: Pups born to immunized dams showed comparable anti-Stx2B antibody titers, were totally protected against lethal systemic Stx2 injection up to 2-3 months postpartum, resisted oral EHEC challenge without symptoms, and survived subsequent intravenous Stx2 challenge due to prolonged active immunity. [Ref:7004]
c_preparation: Chimeric protein combining Brucella lumazine synthase and Shiga toxin 2 B subunit.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) scaffold platform characterization
c_description: The enzyme lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) is highly immunogenic due to its homodecameric structure and stability, making it a candidate scaffold for subunit vaccine design by displaying multiple copies of foreign peptides. [Ref:486]
c_preparation: Chimeric proteins were engineered to display ten copies of a desired peptide (up to 27 residues) on the BLS scaffold without disrupting folding or stability; mixtures of chimeras were reassembled to control stoichiometry and spatial arrangement of different peptides.
c_antigen: lumazine synthase (BLS); foreign peptides up to 27 residues

c_vaccine_name: Brucella lumazine synthase, proline racemase subunit A, lipoprotein outer membrane protein-19, and Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase live attenuated vaccine delivered by Salmonella vector with Brucella lipopolysaccharide adjuvant
c_description: A combination of four attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium live vector strains delivering heterologous Brucella antigens was developed to create a cross-protecting vaccine against multispecies brucellosis. Efficacy: Significant reduction of splenic Brucella abortus 544 colonization compared to non-immunized and Salmonella-only immunized mice; rough Salmonella variant with LPS enhanced delivery efficacy. [Ref:7085]
c_preparation: Formulations included smooth and rough variants of Salmonella delivery vectors, with or without purified Brucella lipopolysaccharide (LPS); rough Salmonella variant combined with LPS was administered intraperitoneally.
c_antigen: lumazine synthase; proline racemase subunit A; lipoprotein outer membrane protein-19; Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase

c_vaccine_name: Brucella M epitope oligosaccharide vaccine
c_description: The study reports an efficient synthetic approach to oligosaccharides modeling the M epitope of the Brucella O-polysaccharide, which is unique to Brucella and characterized by α-(1→3)-linkage between d-perosamine units. [Ref:7249]
c_preparation: Synthesized protected oligosaccharides including a disaccharide, two trisaccharides, and a tetrasaccharide assembled via five glycosylation steps using α-(1→3)-linked disaccharide thioglycoside as the key donor block.
c_antigen: M epitope of the Brucella O-polysaccharide (α-(1→3)-linked d-perosamine oligosaccharides)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis 16M delta vjbR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR was evaluated for safety and efficacy in pregnant sheep, a natural host species, to address the limitations of the current live-attenuated vaccine Rev. 1 which causes abortions in pregnant animals. Efficacy: 16MΔvjbR provided protection comparable to Rev. 1 with no statistical difference in colonization of target organs after challenge. [Ref:7164]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR strain administered subcutaneously at 1 × 10^10 CFU/ml.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus 7α-HSDH subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using 7α-HSDH antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses and protection levels comparable to commercial vaccines B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 and B. abortus strain RB51. [Ref:7170]
c_preparation: 7α-HSDH protein antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus BhuA subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using BhuA antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses but did not show protection comparable to commercial vaccines. [Ref:7170]
c_preparation: BhuA protein antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus FliC 7α-HSDH BhuA subunit vaccine
c_description: Due to safety problems with live attenuated vaccines Rev. 1 and RB51, safer and efficient vaccines are needed; this study evaluates two novel multi-peptide vaccine candidates composed of epitopes from FliC, 7α-HSDH, and BhuA proteins. Efficacy: Multi-epitope antigens with and without poly I:C provided cross protection against B. melitensis 16M and B. abortus 544 infections. [Ref:7138]
c_preparation: Multi-epitope antigens formulated with and without the adjuvant poly I:C.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus FliC subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using FliC antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses and protection levels comparable to commercial vaccines B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 and B. abortus strain RB51. [Ref:7170]
c_preparation: FliC protein antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus FliC subunit vaccine with Mannosylated Chitosan Nanoparticles adjuvant
c_description: FliC protein, a virulence factor of Brucella, was selected as a promising antigen for vaccine development due to drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: Immunization with FliC and FliC-MCN conferred significant protection against Brucella melitensis 16 M and Brucella abortus 544 infections. [Ref:7156]
c_preparation: FliC protein was cloned, expressed, purified, and loaded onto Mannosylated Chitosan Nanoparticles to create a targeted vaccine delivery system.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus L7/L12 truncated Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated a fusion protein vaccine based on truncated Omp31 and L7/L12 antigens, which are immunodominant and conserved in human Brucella pathogens. Efficacy: Vaccination provided significant protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge in mice. [Ref:7024]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein combining truncated Omp31 and L7/L12 antigens.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus poly B multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using poly B multi-epitope antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses and protection levels comparable to commercial vaccines B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 and B. abortus strain RB51. [Ref:7170]
c_preparation: poly B multi-epitope antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus poly T multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed nanoparticle-based vaccine candidate using poly T multi-epitope antigen absorbed by calcium phosphate nanoparticles to induce immune responses and protection against B. melitensis and B. abortus. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant cellular and humoral immune responses and protection levels comparable to commercial vaccines B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 and B. abortus strain RB51. [Ref:7170]
c_preparation: poly T multi-epitope antigen adsorbed onto calcium phosphate nanoparticles of about 90 nm size with spherical shape and smooth surface.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus Urease subunit vaccine
c_description: This study evaluated the vaccine potential of urease antigen formulated in trimethyl chitosan (TMC) nanoparticles against brucellosis. Efficacy: Intraperitoneal immunization with TMC/Urease nanoparticles induced high specific IgG levels and resulted in a high degree of protection against virulent B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge. [Ref:7103]
c_preparation: Urease antigen was loaded into TMC nanoparticles to create a nanoparticle formulation (TMC/Urease).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus virB10 Omp31 Omp16 subunit recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study designed a multi-epitope vaccine targeting B. melitensis and B. abortus using virB10, Omp31, and Omp16 antigens, incorporating predicted T lymphocyte, cytotoxic T cell, and IFN-γ epitopes. The 50S L7/L12 ribosomal protein from Mycobacterium tuberculosis was included as a bovine TLR4 and TLR9 agonist to enhance immune stimulation. Efficacy: The construct showed stable interaction with bovine TLR4 and TLR9 receptors, suggesting potential to induce immune responses. No in vivo efficacy data reported. [Ref:7219]
c_adjuvant: yes; 50S L7/L12 Ribosomal protein from Mycobacterium tuberculosis (bovine TLR4 and TLR9 agonist)
c_preparation: The multi-epitope construct was linked with GPGPG, AAY, and KK linkers, cloned into the pET-32a shuttle vector using BamHI and HindIII restriction sites, and expressed as a soluble ∼82 kDa protein in Escherichia coli SHuffle host.
c_antigen: virB10; Omp31; Omp16; 50S L7/L12 Ribosomal protein from Mycobacterium tuberculosis

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis asp24 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked deletion mutants of asp24 gene in Brucella melitensis to develop improved live vaccine strains. Efficacy: Deltaasp24 mutants showed superior protection compared to current vaccine strains and other deletion mutants (DeltamanBA and DeltavirB2) against homologous and heterologous challenge infections. [Ref:700]
c_preparation: Live attenuated unmarked deletion mutant of asp24 gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis asp24 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate BMDeltaasp24 was evaluated in pregnant goats, the natural host species for Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: BMDeltaasp24 was protective against abortion and infection in the majority of pregnant goats and was more efficacious than BMDeltavirB2 against challenge infection. [Ref:6918]
c_preparation: Unmarked deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine strain BMDeltaasp24.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BacA gene deletion vaccine
c_description: This study investigated the role of BacA gene deletion in Brucella melitensis LPS to understand its effect on immune response modulation, aiming to advance bacterial vaccines and adjuvants by modifying lipid A. Efficacy: LPS from BacA gene deletion mutant disrupted immune suppression and promoted inflammatory factor production, contrasting with wild-type LPS which suppressed immune response. [Ref:7269]
c_preparation: Lipopolysaccharide extracted from Brucella melitensis BacA gene deletion mutant (Bm-ΔBacA) used to stimulate immune cells.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BMEI1090-BMEI1091 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The GR026 mutant is an attenuated bioluminescent Brucella melitensis strain with mutation in BMEI1090-BMEI1091 genes. Efficacy: The mutant was attenuated in IRF-1(-/-) mice; vaccination conferred protection against virulent challenge. [Ref:6917]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain expressing bioluminescence.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis bp26 DNA vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis 16M genome was screened for immunogenic proteins; bp26 was identified as a protective antigen. Efficacy: bp26 DNA vaccine conferred protection against wild-type B. melitensis 16M challenge. [Ref:6909]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant plasmid encoding bp26 used for intramuscular DNA immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BP26 recombinant vector vaccine (invasive E. coli, inv/hly-engineered)
c_description: Current Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine has many disadvantages prompting development of alternative vaccines and delivery systems. Efficacy: Invasive E. coli vaccine expressing BP26 induced significant protection against B. melitensis challenge in mice. [Ref:6976]
c_preparation: Escherichia coli DH5α engineered to express inv gene from Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and hly gene from Listeria monocytogenes, carrying plasmid expressing B. melitensis BP26.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Brucella abortus Brucella suis subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to discover antigen candidates conserved among the three pathogenic Brucella species to develop a safe and potent subunit vaccine overcoming drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: Not reported; next step is to test antigen candidates experimentally. [Ref:7120]
c_preparation: Not reported; planned to test some of the identified antigens using an appropriate antigen delivery system.
c_antigen: 34 potential antigens associated with bacterial adhesion, invasion, evasion, and adaptation to intracellular environment

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BtpA Omp16 Omp28 virB10 Omp25 Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study designed a multiepitope peptide-based vaccine targeting IFN-γ epitopes, T cell cytotoxicity, and T lymphocytes using antigens BtpA, Omp16, Omp28, virB10, Omp25, and Omp31 from B. melitensis, B. abortus, and B. suis. [Ref:7207]
c_adjuvant: yes; PADRE sequence as Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) and TLR4 agonist
c_preparation: The vaccine construct included 389 amino acids linked by AAY, GPGPG, and EAAAK peptides, incorporated the PADRE sequence as a TLR2 and TLR4 agonist, resulting in a soluble, nonallergenic, antigenic protein of 41.3 kDa.
c_antigen: BtpA; Omp16; Omp28; virB10; Omp25; Omp31

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis BtuB subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. [Ref:6992]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis cell wall peptidoglycan subunit vaccine
c_description: The cell wall peptidoglycan fraction (PG-F7) extracted from Brucella melitensis was tested as a unique antigen. Efficacy: PG-F7 conferred good dose-dependent immunity in mice. [Ref:7321]
c_preparation: Purified cell wall peptidoglycan fraction with or without oil adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis conjunctival live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was administered as a single dose conjunctival vaccination against Brucella melitensis in sheep. Efficacy: Antibody titers increased significantly at the first month post-vaccination (p < 0.001) but began to decline by the second month; the vaccine was considered safe and effective for protecting sheep from brucellosis. [Ref:7111]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis CU/ZN-SOD Omp31 BP26 multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope subunit vaccine (MEVcob) was designed using reverse vaccinology, combining six CTL epitopes, seven HTL epitopes, and four linear B cell epitopes from CU/ZN-SOD, Omp31, and BP26 proteins, linked with CTB molecular adjuvant and PADRE universal T helper epitope. Efficacy: The vaccine induced statistically significant protection in BALB/c mice challenged with Brucella melitensis 043. [Ref:7236]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct is a 412-amino acid multi-epitope protein including CTL, HTL, and B cell epitopes linked by AAY, GPPGG, and KK linkers, with CTB as molecular adjuvant and PADRE epitope; codon adaptation and computer cloning were performed.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis delta znuA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Nasal vaccination with the ΔznuA B. melitensis strain was used to stimulate immune protection against mucosal Brucella melitensis infection. Efficacy: Vaccination reduced spleen and lung colonization by more than 2500-fold; over 50% of vaccinated mice had no detectable brucellae; complete protection was observed in wild-type and CD4(-/-) mice but not in CD8(-/-) mice. [Ref:7055]
c_preparation: Live attenuated ΔznuA B. melitensis strain administered via nasal route.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Deltaomp25 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Omp25 was examined as a potential vaccine candidate by creating a mutant strain with disruption of the omp25 gene. Efficacy: Vaccination with BM25 resulted in more than a 2 log10 reduction in bacterial load following challenge with virulent B. melitensis (P<0.01). [Ref:1946]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain with omp25 gene disruption (BM25).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis detoxified lipopolysaccharide-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine
c_description: Detoxified lipopolysaccharide (d-LPS) from Brucella melitensis was prepared and conjugated to tetanus toxoid as a carrier protein to enhance immune responses. Efficacy: Mice immunized with d-LPS-TT showed the strongest protective immune responses against B. melitensis 16M challenge. [Ref:7273]
c_preparation: Conjugate of detoxified LPS and tetanus toxoid (d-LPS-TT).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis DnaK and Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: Combination of recombinant DnaK and recombinant Omp31 proteins used as a subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Combination vaccine induced protection statistically similar to that of Rev. 1 vaccine, superior to each component alone. [Ref:7018]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins DnaK and Omp31; no adjuvant mentioned.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis DnaK subunit vaccine
c_description: The dnak gene was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli to produce recombinant DnaK protein used as a subunit vaccine. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with DnaK showed significant protection against Brucella infection compared to controls (p<0.001), though less than protection by Rev. 1 vaccine (p<0.05). [Ref:7018]
c_preparation: Recombinant DnaK protein expressed in E. coli; no adjuvant mentioned.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis FlgK subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. [Ref:6992]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis fraction I subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated vaccination with a soluble antigen (fraction I) of Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Vaccinated monkeys were protected against subsequent challenge with a virulent strain of Brucella melitensis. [Ref:7338]
c_preparation: Purified soluble antigen (fraction I) of Brucella melitensis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis galE live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The GR024 (galE) mutant is an attenuated bioluminescent Brucella melitensis strain with mutation in galE gene. Efficacy: The galE mutant localized chronically in the tail without changes in liver and spleen and protected IRF-1(-/-) and wild-type mice from virulent challenge. [Ref:6917]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain expressing bioluminescence.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis gamma irradiated inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study hypothesized that bacterial metabolism is important for antigenic and adjuvant properties needed for protective immunity; gamma-irradiation was used to inactivate Brucella melitensis while retaining metabolic activity. Efficacy: The irradiated vaccine protected mice against virulent bacterial challenge without residual virulence. [Ref:6945]
c_preparation: Gamma-irradiated Brucella melitensis bacteria that are nondividing but metabolically active.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis GroEL OMP25 OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the impact of GroEL in combination with recombinant outer membrane proteins OMP25 and OMP31 emulsified in chitosan nanoparticles to enhance immune responses against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Univalent vaccines (except rGroEL alone) and divalent combinations induced higher IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-4 compared to controls; individual OMP25 or OMP31 immunization showed more effective cell-mediated immunity; some rGroEL and rOMP31 combinations were more efficient than other divalent vaccines. [Ref:7096]
c_preparation: Recombinant GroEL, OMP25, and OMP31 proteins emulsified in chitosan nanoparticles; tested as univalent and divalent formulations with different concentrations.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis heat-killed 16 M inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated induction of protective immunity in mice against brucellosis by vaccination with a combination of naloxone, alum, and heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M. Efficacy: The group receiving naloxone + alum + heat-killed Brucella melitensis showed significantly increased IFN-γ, IL-4, and IgG levels, the lowest bacterial load, and 100% survival rate in groups vaccinated with adjuvant combinations. [Ref:6978]
c_preparation: Combination of naloxone and alum as adjuvants with heat-killed Brucella melitensis 16 M.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Hia subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. [Ref:6992]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis high hydrophobic antigenic complex subunit vaccine encapsulated in microparticles
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the effect of excipients facilitating encapsulation of a hydrophobic antigenic complex from Brucella ovis on microparticle properties and to assess protective ability against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: The subcellular vaccine induced protection similar to that of the live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:691]
c_preparation: Poly(epsilon-caprolactone) microparticles containing the hydrophobic antigenic complex (HS) were prepared by solvent extraction/evaporation using a total recirculation one-machine system; excipients beta-cyclodextrin and Pluronic F68 were used to enhance antigen loading and preserve bioactivity.
c_antigen: high hydrophobic antigenic complex extracted from Brucella ovis (HS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis HSP and TF subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to assess the immunogenicity of Brucella melitensis HSP and TF proteins. [Ref:6996]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis hsp60 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study indicates that hsp60 is an immunogenic heat shock protein produced by Brucella melitensis, though at lower levels than in B. abortus. This lower production may contribute to the higher virulence of B. melitensis. Hsp60 is proposed as a candidate antigen for subunit vaccine development. [Ref:6933]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis HspA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the potential of recombinant HspA protein from Brucella melitensis as a subunit vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Administration of recombinant HspA resulted in a significant reduction in bacterial load and a high degree of protection against Brucella melitensis challenge compared to control mice (p<0.001). [Ref:7012]
c_preparation: Recombinant HspA protein was cloned in pDEST42 and used as a subunit vaccine.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid mixture vaccine
c_description: Mixture of hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid (OPS+TT) used for immunization. Efficacy: Not explicitly reported; implied less effective than conjugated vaccines. [Ref:7273]
c_preparation: Non-conjugated mixture of hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis hydrolytic O-polysaccharide-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine
c_description: Hydrolytic O-polysaccharide (OPS) from Brucella melitensis was prepared and conjugated to tetanus toxoid as a carrier protein to enhance immune responses. Efficacy: Mice immunized with OPS-TT demonstrated elevated protective immune responses, though less strong than d-LPS-TT. [Ref:7273]
c_preparation: Conjugate of hydrolytic O-polysaccharide and tetanus toxoid (OPS-TT).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis IFITM3 exosome vaccine
c_description: This study investigated the immune function of extracellular IFITM3 protein in the process of Brucella infection, focusing on exosomes secreted by macrophages infected with Brucella melitensis strain M5.
