Efficacy: Immunization with IFITM3-containing exosomes decreased mouse spleen tissue damage and spleen CFU, establishing an anti-Brucella state in mice. [Ref:7188]
c_preparation: Exosomes carrying IFITM3 protein derived from Brucella M5-infected macrophages.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis inactivated vaccine CF
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safer and more effective candidate for brucellosis vaccination by evaluating the efficacy of the Brucella inactivated vaccine CF, addressing the limitations of current live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: CF demonstrated protective efficacy comparable to the S2 vaccine against B. melitensis biovar 3 infection in mice; CF-immunized guinea pigs resisted infection by B. melitensis M28 and B. melitensis biovar 3. [Ref:7271]
c_preparation: Inactivated Brucella melitensis vaccine designated CF; safety and immunogenicity evaluated with various doses and immunization methods.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis killed cells inactivated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine consisted of killed Brucella melitensis cells suspended in incomplete adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccination reduced B. abortus live cells in spleen; tetramisole treatment increased protection 3.5-fold compared to vaccine alone. [Ref:7304]
c_preparation: Killed Brucella melitensis cells formulated with incomplete adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis L7/L12 ribosomal protein vaccine
c_description: The study identified and sequenced the gene encoding the Brucella melitensis L7/L12 ribosomal protein, which is an immunodominant antigen and may explain the activity of ribosomal vaccines. [Ref:7333]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide core mutant vaccine
c_description: The study characterizes the immunomodulatory effects of Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and a modified LPS with a defective core from a wadC gene mutant strain, highlighting the potential of the wadC mutation for vaccine development targeting the Brucella core LPS structure. Efficacy: The wadC mutant LPS (Bm-wadC) efficiently potentiated mouse and human dendritic cell activation and T cell proliferation in vitro and induced high cytokine secretion in vivo, whereas wild-type LPS (Bm-wt) induced limited dendritic cell activation and cytokine response. [Ref:7091]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide Neisseria meningitidis group B outer membrane protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Intranasal immunization of mice with purified Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide as a noncovalent complex with Neisseria meningitidis group B outer membrane protein was performed. Efficacy: Vaccination significantly reduced bacterial dissemination to spleen and liver compared to controls at 8 weeks postchallenge (P < 0.0001 for spleen, P = 0.005 for liver). No effect was observed on lung infection. [Ref:703]
c_preparation: Purified Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide formulated as a noncovalent complex with Neisseria meningitidis group B outer membrane protein.
c_antigen: lipopolysaccharide; group B outer membrane protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with MONTANIDE ISA 61 VG adjuvant
c_description: The study evaluated immunologic responses and protection against experimental challenge in goats vaccinated with LPS combined with ISA 61 VG adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccination with LPS + ISA 61 VG did not confer protection against abortion, uterine, fetal, mammary, or maternal infection compared to controls. [Ref:7290]
c_preparation: LPS from B. melitensis strain 16M formulated with MONTANIDE™ ISA 61 VG adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine with Neisseria meningitidis GBOMP adjuvant
c_description: A mucosal vaccine against brucellosis was developed consisting of Brucella melitensis LPS complexed with Neisseria meningitidis GBOMP as a mucosal adjuvant. Efficacy: The complex vaccine induced higher levels of IgG and IgA antibodies specific for B. melitensis LPS in lung lavages and antibody-secreting cells in lungs, spleen, and cervical nodes compared to LPS alone; serum antibodies cross-reacted with B. abortus LPS. [Ref:7352]
c_adjuvant: yes; outer membrane protein (GBOMP) of Neisseria meningitidis
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated as a complex of Brucella melitensis LPS with the outer membrane protein GBOMP from group B Neisseria meningitidis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis live attenuated vaccine with wbdR acetyl-transferase gene insertion
c_description: The wbdR acetyl-transferase gene was inserted into Brucella melitensis chromosome II, modifying the O-polysaccharide antigenic structure to include N-acetyl-perosamine and removing native epitopes. Efficacy: The modified strains caused chronic infections in mice and induced antibody responses that differ from wild-type, suggesting potential as tagged vaccines. [Ref:7107]
c_preparation: Live Brucella melitensis constructs with chromosomal wbdR gene insertion and wbkC gene deletion, producing altered lipopolysaccharide antigens.
c_antigen: wbdR acetyl-transferase gene; deletion of wbkC formyltransferase gene

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Lpp-OmpA BtaE subunit vaccine
c_description: This study examined the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of the Lpp-OmpA-BtaE fusion protein co-administered with Freund's adjuvant in protecting against Brucella melitensis infection in a murine model. Efficacy: Vaccination with Lpp-OmpA-BtaE plus Freund's adjuvant conferred superior protection compared to Lpp-OmpA plus BtaE alone, significantly reducing bacterial burdens in spleens of infected mice. [Ref:7277]
c_preparation: Fusion protein of lipoprotein outer membrane protein A (Lpp-OmpA) with Brucella trimeric autotransporter E (BtaE) combined with Freund's adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis LPS-assembly protein LptD subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis polysaccharide export protein subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis cell surface protein subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis heme transporter BhuA subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis flagellin FliC subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis 7-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis immunoglobulin-binding protein EIBE subunit vaccine; Brucella melitensis hemagglutinin subunit vaccine
c_description: Identification of eight potential vaccine candidate proteins from the exoproteome and secretome of Brucella melitensis 16 M using reverse vaccinology approach. [Ref:7047]
c_preparation: Prediction of three surface exposed novel antigenic epitopes from the candidate proteins that can induce both B-cell and T-cell immune responses; peptides proposed for development of exclusive peptide vaccines or multi-component vaccines.
c_antigen: LPS-assembly protein LptD; polysaccharide export protein; cell surface protein; heme transporter BhuA; flagellin FliC; 7-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase; immunoglobulin-binding protein EIBE; hemagglutinin

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Lrp/AsnC family protein subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified six proteins of the Lrp/AsnC family from Brucella melitensis genome, cloned and expressed them in E. coli, and purified the recombinant proteins for immunization. Efficacy: All six Lrp/AsnC proteins induced protective immune responses against Brucella melitensis 16M challenge in mice. [Ref:7049]
c_preparation: Recombinant individual Lrp/AsnC family proteins expressed in Escherichia coli and purified.
c_antigen: Lrp/AsnC family proteins (six individual proteins including BMEI0357)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis lumazine synthase subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to clone, express, and purify the BLS gene from Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 to design a subunit vaccine against undulant fever. [Ref:7131]
c_preparation: The BLS gene was amplified, inserted into pTZ57R/T vector, ligated into pET32(a)+ expression vector, and expressed in E. coli BL21 (DE3) induced by IPTG; the recombinant protein was confirmed by SDS-PAGE and western blotting.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis manBA deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked deletion mutants of manBA gene in Brucella melitensis as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: Provided less protection compared to Deltaasp24 mutants against heterologous challenge. [Ref:700]
c_preparation: Live attenuated unmarked deletion mutant of manBA gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope mRNA vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to create a novel mRNA vaccine with multiple epitopes targeting Brucella melitensis using proteomics and immunoinformatic tools. Efficacy: The designed mRNA construct was predicted to be effective and promising as a vaccine. [Ref:7254]
c_preparation: A multi-epitope protein was modeled from selected antigenic proteins and optimized; mRNA was analyzed for structure and stability.
c_antigen: multiple epitopes from seventeen antigenic proteins

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed by selecting 19 T and B cell epitopes from immunogenic antigens identified by 2D gel electrophoresis, MALDI-TOF, and literature; epitopes ligated with linkers and gene synthesized. Efficacy: Recombinant MEL protein induced immune responses equal to Rev. 1 vaccine in secretion of IFNγ, IL-2, and specific IgG; significant spleen cell proliferation compared to PBS control. [Ref:7195]
c_preparation: Recombinant polypeptide expressed in E. coli BL21, purified and mixed with chitin adjuvant for subcutaneous injection.
c_antigen: multi-epitope protein composed of 19 T and B cell epitopes

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope recombinant protein subunit vaccine
c_description: Live attenuated Brucella vaccines are effective but have safety concerns; subunit vaccines are safer alternatives. This study used bioinformatics to predict B and T cell epitopes to develop a novel recombinant multi-epitope antigen for brucellosis vaccination. Efficacy: The recombinant antigen provided protection against Brucella melitensis 16 M infection comparable to vaccine strain M5-90. [Ref:7064]
c_preparation: Recombinant multi-epitope protein antigen

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine was designed using reverse vaccinology from Omp10, Omp25, Omp31, and BtpB proteins to prevent Brucella infection, addressing the difficulty of eliminating Brucella with current medical treatments. Efficacy: Animal experiments demonstrated high immunogenicity of the MEV. [Ref:7205]
c_preparation: The vaccine peptide contains 806 amino acids, linking CTL, HTL, and B cell epitopes with AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers respectively; supplemented at the N-terminal with adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity.
c_antigen: Omp10, Omp25, Omp31, BtpB; 13 CTL epitopes, 17 HTL epitopes, 9 linear B cell epitopes, 2 conformational B cell epitopes

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multi-epitopes vaccine
c_description: The study designed an in-silico multi-epitopes vaccine for Brucella melitensis using computational approaches including subtractive proteomics, reverse vaccinology, and immunoinformatics to identify potential vaccine candidates from the pathogen core proteome. Efficacy: Docking results showed good binding potency with immune receptors; binding free energy calculations indicated stable interactions, suggesting the vaccine construct can effectively engage immune receptors. [Ref:7217]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct comprises 274 amino acids with a molecular weight of 28.14 kDa and an instability index of 27.62; it includes nine antigenic, non-allergic, water-soluble, and non-toxic epitopes derived from ten selected proteins.
c_antigen: catalase; siderophore ABC transporter substrate-binding protein; pyridoxamine 5'-phosphate oxidase; superoxide dismutase; peptidylprolyl isomerase; superoxide dismutase family protein; septation protein A; hypothetical protein; binding-protein-dependent transport systems inner membrane component; 4-hydroxy-2-oxoheptanedioate aldolase; multi-epitopes

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis multitope peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified nine potential antigenic proteins from non-classically secreted proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M using reverse vaccinology; six novel antigenic epitopes eliciting B-cell and T-cell responses were selected to design a multitope vaccine. Efficacy: Not reported (computational prediction only) [Ref:7090]
c_preparation: Epitopes from selected proteins were joined using amino acid linkers EAAAK and GPGPG; cholera toxin subunit B was linked to the N-terminal as an adjuvant; the vaccine candidate was modeled and physicochemically analyzed.
c_antigen: Omp31 immunogenic protein precursor; Omp22 protein precursor; extracellular serine protease; hypothetical membrane-associated protein; iron-regulated outer membrane protein FrpB; LPS-assembly protein LptD; polysaccharide export protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis O-polysaccharide conjugate vaccine
c_description: A conjugate vaccine was synthesized by covalently coupling the O-polysaccharide from Brucella melitensis 16M to bovine serum albumin (BSA). Efficacy: Immunization with 10 micrograms of conjugate conferred significant protection against virulent challenge with B. melitensis H38, similar to the reference vaccine H38. [Ref:6926]
c_preparation: Conjugate of Brucella melitensis O-polysaccharide and bovine serum albumin (BSA).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp10 Omp28 L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: Recombinant Omp10-Omp28-L7/L12 proteins were expressed in Pichia pastoris and used as immunogens to evaluate immune responses. Efficacy: The recombinant protein expressed in Pichia pastoris with TPPPS adjuvant provided the most pronounced immune effect and significantly better protection than negative controls but less protection than the B. melitensis M5 live vaccine. [Ref:7178]
c_adjuvant: yes; Taishan Pinus massoniana pollen polysaccharides (TPPPS)
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins expressed in Pichia pastoris combined with TPPPS adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis omp16 and omp19 mRNA vaccine
c_description: mRNA encoding omp16 and omp19 genes of Brucella melitensis was synthesized by in vitro transcription as a novel vaccine candidate. [Ref:7302]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmids pIVTRup-omp16 and pIVTRup-omp19 were used to synthesize approximately 600 nt mRNA fragments encoding Omp16 and Omp19 proteins.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 human interleukin 2 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study reports the construction of a recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing the Omp16-IL2 fusion protein as an oral Lactococcus-based vaccine, proposed as an alternative to commonly used live attenuated vaccines for future studies against brucellosis. [Ref:7142]
c_preparation: Omp16-IL2 fusion gene cloned into pAMJ2008 expression vector and expressed in Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris MG1363 by electrotransformation; purified recombinant fusion protein produced.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 L7/L12 Omp19 Cu-Zn SOD recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: A new candidate vector vaccine against human brucellosis was developed based on recombinant influenza viral vectors (rIVV) subtype H5N1 expressing Brucella outer membrane proteins Omp16, L7/L12, Omp19, or Cu-Zn SOD proteins. Efficacy: Double intranasal immunization at 10^6 EID50 dose provided 80% protection of guinea pigs from B. melitensis 16M infection, comparable to the commercial B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:7184]
c_preparation: Recombinant influenza viral vectors subtype H5N1 expressing Brucella Omp16, L7/L12, Omp19, or Cu-Zn SOD proteins; administered via conjunctival, intranasal, and sublingual routes at doses of 10^5, 10^6, and 10^7 EID50.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 L7/L12 Omp19 SOD recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Developed recombinant influenza viral vector subtype H5N1 expressing Brucella immunodominant proteins from NS1 open reading frame to create human brucellosis vaccine candidates. Efficacy: All vaccine formulations were safe in mice; vaccine formulations and commercial B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine protected mice from B. melitensis 16M infection with 1.6 to 2.97 log10 unit reduction; tetravalent vaccine formulation showed significant protection in guinea pigs (0.2 ± 0.4 log10 units reduction) comparable to commercial Rev. 1 vaccine (1.2 ± 2.6 log10 units reduction). [Ref:7179]
c_preparation: Created 18 mono-, bi-, and tetravalent vaccine formulations using influenza viral vectors expressing Omp16, Omp19, L7/L12, and SOD proteins; tetravalent formulation Flu-NS1-80-Omp16+Flu-NS1-80-L7/L12+Flu-NS1-80-Omp19+Flu-NS1-80-SOD selected as lead candidate.
c_antigen: Omp16; L7/L12; Omp19; Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis omp16 mRNA vaccine
c_description: mRNA encoding the omp16 gene of Brucella melitensis was synthesized by in vitro transcription as a vaccine candidate. [Ref:7302]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid pIVTRup-omp16 was used to synthesize approximately 600 nt mRNA encoding Omp16 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp16 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Current Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine has many disadvantages prompting development of alternative vaccines and delivery systems. Efficacy: Invasive E. coli vaccine expressing Omp16 induced significant protection against B. melitensis challenge in mice. [Ref:6976]
c_preparation: Escherichia coli DH5α engineered to express inv gene from Yersinia pseudotuberculosis and hly gene from Listeria monocytogenes, carrying plasmid expressing B. melitensis Omp16.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMP19 and L7/L12 subunit vaccine
c_description: A vaccine candidate was developed composed of two recombinant antigens, OMP19 and L7/L12 of Brucella melitensis, encapsulated in a nanoliposomal adjuvant system. Efficacy: The liposome-OMP19&L7/L12 formulation showed the highest reduction of Brucella melitensis in mouse spleens (2.43 and 1.44 log units of protection) after first and second protection assays, outperforming PBS, liposome alone, protein mixture alone, and Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:7287]
c_preparation: The antigens were encapsulated in a nanoliposomal adjuvant system forming monodisperse spherical nanoparticles approximately 123 nm in size with about 71% encapsulation efficacy and 65% antigen release rate.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis omp19 mRNA vaccine
c_description: mRNA encoding the omp19 gene of Brucella melitensis was synthesized by in vitro transcription as a vaccine candidate. [Ref:7302]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid pIVTRup-omp19 was used to synthesize approximately 600 nt mRNA encoding Omp19 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMP19 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a potential recombinant vaccine candidate using the 19 kDa outer membrane protein (OMP19) of Brucella melitensis strain H38, targeting all Brucella infections, especially in humans and pregnant animals. Efficacy: The recombinant OMP19 antigen showed similar immunogenic power to the commercially available recombinant protein in the mouse model. [Ref:7216]
c_preparation: OMP19 gene was amplified and cloned into the pETSUMO vector system to produce purified recombinant OMP19 antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp22 subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-step antigen selection approach was used to identify outer membrane proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M with antigenic determinants for potential vaccine formulation. Efficacy: Not reported; studies to assess immunogenicity and protective efficacy of individual proteins in mice are currently underway. [Ref:6992]
c_preparation: Recombinant expression of selected outer membrane proteins (Omp22, Hia, BtuB, FlgK) was performed for validation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 and Omp31 DNA vaccine
c_description: DNA vaccine encoding both Omp25 and Omp31 genes was constructed in the eukaryotic expression vector pcDNA3.1/Hygro (+) and confirmed by SDS-PAGE and Western blot. Efficacy: Induced significant immunoglobulin G response, T-cell proliferation, and interferon gamma production compared to controls. [Ref:7116]
c_preparation: Recombinant plasmid pcDNA3.1/Hygro (+) encoding both Omp25 and Omp31 genes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis mutant BM 25 lacks the major 25 kDa outer membrane protein Omp25 and was previously found attenuated in the murine model. This study evaluated its pathogenicity and protective capacity in pregnant goats. Efficacy: Vaccination with BM 25 prior to breeding resulted in 100% protection against abortion following challenge with virulent strain 16M, comparable to protection by strain Rev. 1. [Ref:6883]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant BM 25 with deletion of Omp25 protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 live attenuated vaccine; Brucella abortus Omp25 live attenuated vaccine; Brucella ovis Omp25 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Mutants lacking Omp25 are attenuated in animal models of infection and provide levels of protection similar or better than the currently used attenuated vaccine strain Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1. Efficacy: Mutants lacking Omp25 provide protection levels similar or better than Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:6887]
c_preparation: Mutant strains lacking Omp25 gene

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 Omp31 and Mycobacterium tuberculosis MPT70 MPT83 RNA vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to develop a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting Brucella melitensis and Mycobacterium tuberculosis using immunoinformatics approaches, selecting proteins Omp25, Omp31, MPT70, and MPT83 to identify predominant T- and B-cell epitopes. Efficacy: The multi-epitope mRNA vaccine demonstrated increased antigenicity, non-allergenicity, solubility, high stability, and robust binding affinity to TLR4, suggesting potential efficacy. [Ref:7260]
c_preparation: The vaccine was constructed using helper T lymphocyte epitopes, cytotoxic T lymphocyte epitopes, linear B-cell epitopes, and conformational B-cell epitopes; nucleotide sequence optimization achieved a codon adaptation index of 1.0 and average GC content of 54.01%, indicating potential for efficient expression in Escherichia coli.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study involved molecular cloning and expression analysis of the Omp25 gene from Iranian Brucella melitensis to design a subunit vaccine candidate. [Ref:7072]
c_preparation: The Omp25 gene was amplified, cloned into pTZ57R/T vector, and expressed using pET32(a)+ vector in E. coli BL21 (DE3) strain, producing a 42 kDa protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMP28 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the potential of CpG ODN to enhance the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of recombinant OMP28 of Brucella melitensis as a subunit vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The rOMP28+CpG treated mice showed significant protection against B. abortus 544 challenge, but the level of protection was lower than the required level. [Ref:6948]
c_preparation: Recombinant OMP28 protein co-administered with CpG oligonucleotides as an adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp28 vaccine
c_description: The study cloned and characterized a 28-kDa outer membrane protein (Omp28) from Brucella melitensis, recognized by the humoral immune response in human brucellosis, suggesting its potential use as a vaccine antigen. [Ref:7348]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 48-74 peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: A synthetic peptide containing amino acids 48 to 74 of Omp31 was evaluated for immunogenicity and protective efficacy in mice. Efficacy: The peptide induced protection against B. melitensis similar to rOmp31 but less protection against B. ovis. [Ref:6911]
c_preparation: Synthetic peptide administered with incomplete Freund's adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 and OmpA vaccine
c_description: Exosomes secreted by Brucella melitensis M5-infected macrophages (Exo-M5) were extracted and identified to study their role in immune activation and macrophage polarization. Efficacy: Exo-M5 promoted M1 macrophage polarization, induced secretion of M1 cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ), inhibited M2 cytokine (IL-10), reduced intracellular Brucella survival, increased IgG2a antibody release, protected mice from Brucella infection, and reduced spleen parasitaemia. [Ref:7226]
c_preparation: Exosomes carrying Brucella antigen components including Omp31 and OmpA derived from infected macrophages.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 and trigger factor subunit vaccine
c_description: Subunit vaccines were developed using recombinant outer membrane protein Omp31 and trigger factor chaperone protein (TF) of Brucella melitensis, administered alone or in combination, as safer alternatives to live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: The combination of rOmp31 and rTF provided protection against Brucella melitensis infection comparable to the live attenuated vaccine strain Rev. 1; combination showed a slight but not significant increase in protection compared to rTF alone. [Ref:7043]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins rOmp31 and rTF used alone or combined as a cocktail.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMP31 epitopic region subunit vaccine fused to interleukin 2
c_description: The vaccine is a recombinant protein consisting of three repeats of a 27 amino acid immunogenic epitope derived from OMP31 antigen of Brucella melitensis fused to IL-2 as a molecular adjuvant to enhance immune stimulation. Efficacy: Treatments with chimeric proteins significantly reduced splenocyte microbial load compared to controls; 3E-IL2 treatment showed the best protection with lowest agglutination rates in Wright test. [Ref:7144]
c_preparation: Recombinant chimeric protein with molecular adjuvant IL-2; chemical adjuvant incomplete Freund's adjuvant (IFA) was also used in some treatments.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMP31 LptE VirB2 multi-epitope recombinant BCG live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) was designed using reverse vaccinology targeting three immunogenic proteins of Brucella melitensis: OMP31, LptE, and VirB2. Molecular adjuvants cholera toxin B subunit and PADRE were incorporated to enhance immunogenicity, and TAT cell-penetrating peptides were added to improve intracellular delivery. Efficacy: Simulations showed potent immune activation with significant increases in cytotoxic T cells (1050 cells/mm³), memory helper T cells (1150 cells/mm³), and IFN-γ production (2 × 10^6 ng/ml), along with sustained IgG/IgM titers over 350 days (1 × 10^5 cells/mm³). Experimental validation of immunological efficacy is pending. [Ref:7284]
c_adjuvant: yes; cholera toxin B subunit and PADRE
c_preparation: The MEV includes six CTL epitopes, nine HTL epitopes, seven linear B-cell epitopes, and five conformational B-cell epitopes. Structural optimization involved disulfide bond engineering to improve molecular stability. The codon-optimized MEV sequence was cloned in silico into the pMV261 shuttle vector to generate a recombinant BCG construct.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the role of Omp31 in virulence and the potential of the omp31 mutant strain as a vaccine candidate to prevent brucellosis in goats. Efficacy: The omp31 mutant strain showed decreased splenic colonization and no apparent lesions compared to controls; it conferred protection similar to the B. melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine strain against virulent challenge. [Ref:7154]
c_preparation: Live attenuated B. melitensis LVM31 mutant strain with omp31 gene mutation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 Omp25 Omp28 recombinant subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to design a recombinant vaccine containing potential immunogenic epitopes against Brucella melitensis using immunoinformatics approaches. Efficacy: The designed vaccine showed high quality and acceptable physicochemical properties with predicted ability to induce humoral and cellular immune responses against Brucella melitensis. [Ref:7234]
c_preparation: The vaccine was designed as a multi-epitope recombinant subunit vaccine combining epitopes from Omp31, Omp25, and Omp28 antigens joined by flexible linkers; codon optimization for expression in E. coli was performed in silico.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis OMP31 peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: Peptides containing both T-cell and B-cell epitopes of OMP31 were synthesized and used for immunization. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significantly lower bacterial loads in lungs compared to control group after challenge. [Ref:7126]
c_preparation: Peptides administered by nasal route without reported adjuvant.
c_antigen: OMP31 peptides containing T-cell epitope, B-cell epitope, or TB epitopes

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 recombinant vector vaccine (plain E. coli)
c_description: BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant Escherichia coli expressing the omp31 gene of Brucella melitensis, coding for a major outer membrane protein. Efficacy: No significant protection against challenge with smooth Brucella melitensis H38S was observed. [Ref:7361]
c_preparation: Recombinant Escherichia coli expressing the omp31 gene; boosting with a dose ten times lower than the first.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 recombinant vector vaccine (Lactococcus lactis surface display)
c_description: Since Brucella infection mostly occurs through mucosal surfaces, a vaccine delivered via mucosal route can enhance immune response to control brucellosis. Omp31 is a major outer membrane protein and protective antigen of Brucella. Efficacy: Immunized mice showed significant increases in sIgA, serum IgA, IgM, and total IgG antibodies with live vaccine; killed vaccine induced significant increases in serum IgM and total IgG; IgG2a subtype response was higher than IgG1 in both groups. [Ref:7171]
c_preparation: Recombinant Lactococcus lactis displaying Omp31 antigen was constructed by fusing omp31 gene with usp45 signal peptide and M6 cell wall anchor in pNZ7021 expression vector; live and killed forms of recombinant L. lactis were used for oral and intraperitoneal immunization, respectively.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The recombinant 31-kDa outer membrane protein from Brucella melitensis (rOmp31) was evaluated for immunogenicity and protective efficacy in mice. Efficacy: Immunization with rOmp31 conferred protection against B. melitensis and B. ovis infection; protection against B. melitensis was mediated primarily by CD4+ T cells. [Ref:6911]
c_preparation: rOmp31 was administered with incomplete Freund's adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine with aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles
c_description: The study compared aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles as antigen delivery systems using Omp31 protein, a candidate antigen for protection against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: AH/Omp31 nanoparticles induced protection comparable to Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:7124]
c_preparation: Omp31 protein loaded on aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles (AH/Omp31).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine with calcium phosphate nanoparticles
c_description: The study aimed to compare calcium phosphate nanoparticles as antigen delivery systems using Omp31 protein, a candidate antigen for protection against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: CP/Omp31 nanoparticles elicited protection against Brucella melitensis challenge equivalent to the vaccine strain Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 and showed a low increase in protection compared to CS/Omp31 nanoparticles. [Ref:7124]
c_preparation: Omp31 protein loaded on calcium phosphate nanoparticles (CP/Omp31).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 subunit vaccine with chitosan nanoparticles
c_description: The study evaluated chitosan nanoparticles as antigen delivery systems using Omp31 protein, a candidate antigen for protection against Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: CS/Omp31 nanoparticles elicited protection against Brucella melitensis 16M, but less than CP/Omp31 nanoparticles. [Ref:7124]
c_preparation: Omp31 protein loaded on chitosan nanoparticles (CS/Omp31).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis Omp31 vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the role of the major outer membrane protein Omp31 in Brucella melitensis by generating an Omp31 mutant strain to evaluate its importance in outer membrane integrity and intracellular survival. Efficacy: The Omp31 mutant strain showed increased susceptibility to polymyxin B, sodium deoxycholate, and nonimmune serum compared to wild-type and Rev1 vaccine strains; it also exhibited decreased internalization and significantly reduced intracellular survival in both cell lines. [Ref:7080]
c_preparation: An Omp31 gene inactivated mutant strain (LVM31) of Brucella melitensis was constructed by insertion of a kanamycin cassette into the gene cloned in pUC18 plasmid and transformed into the wild-type strain.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: OMVs from Brucella melitensis have been shown to be effective vaccines against B. melitensis challenge in mice. Efficacy: No additive effect on clearance of B. melitensis; however, mice receiving OMVs with antibiotics exhibited no Brucella replication post-treatment compared to antibiotics alone; mice receiving only vaccines did not show significant clearance. [Ref:7003]
c_preparation: OMVs administered twice during antibiotic therapy.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis outer membrane vesicles subunit vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella melitensis have been shown to provide protection similar to the live attenuated strain Rev. 1 vaccine in mice but without the associated risks of live vaccines. Efficacy: Pluronic P85 enhanced the protection provided by OMVs against Brucella melitensis challenge in mice; P85 alone also improved bacterial clearance compared to saline controls [Ref:6985][Ref:7286]
c_preparation: OMVs combined with Pluronic P85 as an adjuvant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis P39 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study analyzed the potential of the Brucella melitensis 16 M periplasmic binding protein (P39) antigen expressed in live Escherichia coli as a vaccine against B. melitensis 16 M infection in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: Vaccination significantly reduced the number of Brucella melitensis strain 16 M bacteria in spleens compared to saline controls (p<0.001). [Ref:6949]
c_preparation: Live Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) pEt15b expressing Brucella P39 protein administered intraperitoneally twice at 4-week intervals.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis pgm gene deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A novel highly attenuated vaccine strain constructed by clean deletion of the phosphoglucomutase (pgm) gene, which is involved in biosynthesis of polysaccharides including O-antigen and cyclic beta glucans. Efficacy: The vaccine confers excellent levels of protection against B. melitensis in mice and cross protection against B. abortus and B. suis. [Ref:7225]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain with pgm gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis phenol insoluble fractions subunit vaccine
c_description: Mouse inoculation with three different phenol-insoluble fractions extracted from Brucella melitensis was performed to study immune protection. Efficacy: Inoculation with fractions accelerated blood clearance of live Brucella and reduced bacterial multiplication in spleen; immune serum conferred good specific protection to non-immunized hosts. [Ref:7324]
c_preparation: Phenol-insoluble fractions 'PI', '4A', and '5' extracted from Brucella melitensis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis PI fraction vaccine
c_description: The PI fraction, a phenol-extracted fraction from Brucella melitensis, has been used for years in the laboratory for vaccination of laboratory and agricultural workers considered at risk. [Ref:7360]
c_preparation: Phenol-extracted fraction (PI); another phenol-extracted and peptidoglycan containing fraction (4A) was also used in vitro.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis plsC gene deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study used transposon sequencing to identify genes essential for Brucella melitensis multiplication in mouse spleen and lungs, selecting genes whose deletion would attenuate the bacteria in the spleen, the main reservoir. Efficacy: The plsC deletion mutant showed protective efficacy similar to the reference Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine but with shorter persistence in the spleen. [Ref:7252]
c_preparation: Deletion mutant of the plsC gene, which is involved in phospholipid biosynthesis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis purD deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study constructed a purD gene deletion mutant in Brucella melitensis M5 strain to investigate the role of de novo purine biosynthesis in virulence and intracellular survival. Efficacy: The purD mutant showed impaired growth, increased sensitivity to detergent, reduced membrane permeability, altered lipid biosynthesis, decreased ability to invade and survive in host cells, and reduced colonization and pathology in mice. [Ref:7292]
c_preparation: A live attenuated strain with deletion of the purD gene, impairing purine biosynthesis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis purE deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A purE mutant (delta purE201) of Brucella melitensis 16M was previously shown to be attenuated in cultured human monocytes and was evaluated here for attenuation in mice. Efficacy: The delta purE201 mutant showed significantly reduced bacterial counts in spleen, liver, and lungs compared to wild-type 16M; it was essentially eliminated from mice by 8 weeks postinfection, whereas 16M persisted at high levels; mice infected with delta purE201 had only mild, transient splenomegaly and no serum interleukin-6 production. [Ref:1799]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M with purE gene deletion (delta purE201).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis purE deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Young goats were inoculated subcutaneously with the purE deletion mutant to evaluate host responses. Efficacy: The purE mutant was cleared from visceral tissues by PID 84, with no bacteria detected in mammary lymph nodes or spleen at necropsy; it produced immune responses and less severe pathologic changes compared to the virulent parental strain. [Ref:7347]
c_preparation: Genetic deletion mutant (deltapurE201) of Brucella melitensis strain 16M.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis rBtuB Hia FlgK subunit vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the goat Th1/Th2 immune response to a cocktail of three Brucella melitensis peptides (rBtuB-Hia-FlgK) previously shown to induce antigen-specific immune responses in rodent models. Efficacy: The peptide cocktail induced an increase in CD4+/CD8+ T cells starting at day 15 and persisting to day 80. IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-2 mRNA expression were induced by day 15, with IFN-γ levels maintained at day 80. Although IFN-γ production was lower than that induced by Rev-1 at day 15, this may be due to sampling timing. [Ref:7215]
c_preparation: A cocktail of three peptides (rBtuB, Hia, FlgK) from Brucella melitensis was used; adjuvant was included but not specified.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis riboflavin synthase alpha chain subunit vaccine
c_description: The study identified immunogenic proteins from Brucella melitensis 16 M soluble proteins using immunoproteomic assay to screen candidate antigens for subunit vaccine development. Riboflavin synthase alpha chain (RS-α) was identified as a novel vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Mice vaccinated with recombinant RS-α showed partial protection against Brucella melitensis infection. [Ref:6969]
c_preparation: Recombinant RS-α protein expressed in Escherichia coli as a His-tag fusion protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine hydrolase subunit vaccine
c_description: Due to drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines, screening of Brucella-protective antigens as subunit vaccine candidates was pursued; immunoproteomic assay identified immunogenic soluble proteins of Brucella melitensis 16M, including AdoHcyase. Efficacy: Recombinant AdoHcyase induced a high level of protection against B. melitensis 16M challenge in mice. [Ref:6960]
c_preparation: Recombinant AdoHcyase protein expressed in Escherichia coli.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis SP41 DNA vaccine
c_description: A plasmid construct pCISP41 was established for expression of SP41 protein in mammalian cells to evaluate its role as a DNA vaccine against Brucella spp. Efficacy: DNA-SP41 vaccination induced specific IgG and T-cell responses but provided lower protection against B. melitensis 16M challenge in mice compared to the attenuated B. melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine [Ref:6993]
c_preparation: DNA plasmid pCISP41 encoding SP41 protein

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 16 M delta vjbR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Developed as a safer live attenuated vaccine candidate for human and animal use with demonstrated safety and protective efficacy in multiple immunocompetent animal models. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced colonization in multiple organs and reduced pathological changes after challenge with wild-type Brucella melitensis 16M. [Ref:6970]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16 M with vjbR gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 16M delta mucR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The mucR mutant (BMEI 1364) was identified and characterized as a vaccine candidate for brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccinated animals demonstrated a statistically significant degree of protection against both intraperitoneal and aerosol challenge. [Ref:2071]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant administered intraperitoneally at a dose of 10^5 CFU.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 16M delta vjbR live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study investigates the safety of the Brucella melitensis 16MΔvjbR strain vaccine candidate in young goats over a 15-month period including vaccination, impregnation, delivery, and lactation. Efficacy: Not reported (the study focused on safety, not efficacy). [Ref:7180]
c_preparation: A single subcutaneous dose containing 1x10^9 CFU of B. melitensis 16MΔvjbR was delivered either encapsulated in alginate microcapsules or non-encapsulated.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 16M hfq mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was constructed to overcome drawbacks of current vaccines Rev. 1 and M5-90, including residual virulence and inability to differentiate infection from vaccination. Efficacy: Reduced survival of the mutant strain in macrophages and mice; strong protective immunity against virulent Brucella melitensis 16M challenge in BALB/c mice. [Ref:6994]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain 16M with hfq gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 16M purE deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A defined purine-auxotrophic mutant of Brucella melitensis 16M was constructed by chromosomal gene replacement deleting part of purE and purK genes. Efficacy: The purE deletion mutant failed to grow in human monocyte-derived macrophages, whereas wild-type and complemented strains grew by nearly two logs, indicating attenuation. [Ref:706]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with purE gene deletion requiring exogenous purines for growth.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 16M vjbR deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vjbR gene, a quorum sensing regulator involved in Brucella intracellular survival, was targeted to develop a vaccine candidate that allows differentiation between infection and vaccination. Efficacy: Vaccination with 16MΔvjbR conferred significant protective immunity against Brucella melitensis strain 16M challenge, equivalent to the licensed vaccine Rev. 1. [Ref:1910]
c_preparation: A vjbR mutant of Brucella melitensis strain 16M was constructed by replacing the vjbR gene with a kanamycin resistance gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 201 vaccine
c_description: A purEK deletion mutant, delta purE201 (strain 201), was used as a live attenuated vaccine candidate in juvenile goats. [Ref:7355]
c_preparation: Live bacteria (delta purE201 mutant strain)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain 53 H 38 inactivated vaccine
c_description: Mice were immunized subcutaneously with a heat-inactivated Brucella melitensis strain 53 H 38 vaccine incorporated into a water-in-oil emulsion. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed a decrease in challenge bacteria in the spleen during the first two days post-challenge, followed by an increase that remained lower than in unvaccinated controls; spleen weights were lower in vaccinated animals. [Ref:7340]
c_preparation: Heat-inactivated Brucella melitensis strain 53 H 38 incorporated into a water-in-oil emulsion adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain B115 vaccine
c_description: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 is used as vaccine for prophylaxis in sheep and goats but induces antibodies to O-polysaccharide (O-PS) complicating differentiation of vaccinated and infected animals; B115 is a natural, attenuated, rough strain lacking surface O-PS and proposed as alternative vaccine. Efficacy: Vaccination with B115 conferred significant protective immunity against B. melitensis 16M and B. ovis, equivalent to that of Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:6932]
c_preparation: Live, attenuated rough strain B115 with O-PS present intracellularly but not exposed on surface.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain G16 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: This study developed the rough-type attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant G16 as a vaccine candidate with DIVA potential. Efficacy: G16 showed immune protection levels matching the reference vaccine M5-90Δ26 with attenuated virulence and no viable bacteria recovered from spleens at 4 weeks post-inoculation. [Ref:7279]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain G16 with semi-rough phenotype retaining partial O-antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain G7 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: This study developed the rough-type attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant G7 as a vaccine candidate with DIVA potential. Efficacy: G7 showed immune protection levels matching the reference vaccine M5-90Δ26 with attenuated virulence and no viable bacteria recovered from spleens at 4 weeks post-inoculation. [Ref:7279]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain G7 with complete rough phenotype.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain G8 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: This study developed the rough-type attenuated Brucella melitensis mutant G8 as a vaccine candidate with DIVA potential. Efficacy: G8 showed slightly lower immune protection efficacy compared to reference vaccine M5-90Δ26 with attenuated virulence and no viable bacteria recovered from spleens at 4 weeks post-inoculation. [Ref:7279]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain G8 with complete rough phenotype.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain H-38 inactivated vaccine
c_description: Mice were immunized 36 days before pregnancy with the vaccine. Efficacy: Immunized mice were protected against placental colonization by Brucella abortus challenge. [Ref:7315]
c_preparation: Killed (inactivated) vaccine of Brucella melitensis strain H-38.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5 purE purK gene-deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A two-gene (purE and purK) deletion mutant was constructed in Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5 using homologous recombination to reduce cytotoxicity while maintaining protective efficacy. Efficacy: The mutant vaccine conferred protection against infection with virulent wild-type Brucella melitensis strain 16M comparable to parental strain M5. [Ref:7264]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5 with purE and purK gene deletions.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5 vaccine
c_description: The study investigates microparticles (MPs) released from macrophages infected with the attenuated Brucella melitensis strain M5, exploring their role in enhancing host defense and adaptive immunity against Brucella. Efficacy: MPs promoted bacterial clearance and restricted intracellular survival; elicited potent Th1-polarized immunity with elevated IgG2a and IFN-γ; activated NF-κB pathway in dendritic cells enhancing IL-12 and TNF-α secretion; primed cytotoxic T lymphocytes for specific lysis of Brucella-infected targets. [Ref:7296]
c_preparation: Microparticles derived from macrophages infected with Brucella melitensis strain M5.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 delta irr live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study constructed the M5-90Δirr mutant of Brucella melitensis to investigate the role of the irr gene in virulence and growth, suggesting its potential as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: M5-90Δirr showed attenuated adhesion and invasion but enhanced intracellular replication and resistance to hydrogen peroxide; growth was stronger under iron-limiting conditions; no significant difference in spleen bacterial load compared to parental strain at 7 and 15 days postinfection; splenic index was lower than parental strain, indicating attenuation. [Ref:7157]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant with deletion of the irr gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 delta rirA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study constructed the M5-90ΔrirA mutant of Brucella melitensis to investigate the role of the rirA gene in virulence and growth. Efficacy: M5-90ΔrirA showed attenuated adhesion and invasion but enhanced intracellular replication and resistance to hydrogen peroxide; bacterial load in spleen was significantly reduced at 15 days postinfection compared to parental strain. [Ref:7157]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant with deletion of the rirA gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: B. melitensis strain M5-90 is a live attenuated vaccine cultured from B. melitensis strain M28 and has been used as an effective tool in the control of brucellosis in goats and sheep in China. Efficacy: Not directly reported; study provides molecular insights into attenuation mechanisms that may facilitate generation of new attenuated vaccine strains with enhanced efficacy [Ref:6971]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain derived from B. melitensis strain M28

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 manB mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate M5-90ΔmanB was generated to overcome drawbacks of current vaccines such as residual virulence and inability to differentiate infection from vaccination. Efficacy: M5-90ΔmanB showed significantly reduced survival in macrophages and mice and conferred strong protective immunity against virulent Brucella melitensis 16M challenge in BALB/c mice. [Ref:7089]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis M5-90 strain with manB gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 phosphoglucomutase mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 pgm mutant (M5-90Δpgm) was constructed to overcome drawbacks of residual virulence and serological differentiation issues of existing live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: M5-90Δpgm showed significantly reduced survival in cells and mice and induced high protective immunity in BALB/c mice against wild-type challenge. [Ref:7062]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain with deletion of phosphoglucomutase gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5-90 was developed in China during the 1970s-1980s by attenuation from virulent M28 strain. Efficacy: M5-90 was completely cleared from mice within 15 weeks; immunization with 10^5 CFU conferred significant protection against virulent B. melitensis M28 and B. abortus 544 challenges at 45 and 150 days post-vaccination; in guinea pigs, 3×10^8 CFU dose provided 100% protection against M28 and 90% protection against 544 challenges. [Ref:7293]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain M5-90 administered subcutaneously at doses ranging from 10^5 to 3×10^8 CFU.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 vjbR deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The M5-90ΔvjbR mutant was constructed from the Brucella melitensis M5-90 vaccine strain to overcome safety issues and enable differentiation of infected from vaccinated animals. Efficacy: M5-90ΔvjbR showed reduced survival in macrophages and mice, induced high protective immunity in mice, and stimulated specific IgG responses and cytokine production in both mice and sheep. [Ref:7112]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis M5-90 strain with vjbR gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain M5-90 wboA deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A wboA mutant was derived from Brucella melitensis vaccine strain M5-90 to address drawbacks of current vaccines including inability to serologically differentiate vaccinated from infected animals. Efficacy: The M5-90ΔwboA strain showed reduced survival in macrophages and mice, induced protective immunity comparable to parental M5-90 strain in mice, and elicited specific IgG and cytokine responses; in sheep, it induced IFN-γ secretion and did not cause positive results in standard serological tests. [Ref:7030]
c_preparation: Live attenuated wboA deletion mutant of B. melitensis strain M5-90.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain NI-NB6 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed as a rough-mutant strain with wboA gene deletion from Brucella melitensis NI parent strain to evaluate effects of genetic background on virulence, pathogenicity, and protective immunity. Efficacy: Showed longer survival time in mice (11 weeks) but offered less protection against challenge compared to some other mutants. [Ref:6988]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 bp26 and omp31 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The CGV2631 mutant, deleted in both bp26 and omp31 genes, was evaluated as a vaccine candidate against Brucella ovis infection in sheep. Efficacy: CGV2631 conferred significant protection against Brucella ovis but protection was significantly lower than that conferred by CGV26 and Rev. 1 vaccines. [Ref:6934]
c_preparation: Live attenuated deletion mutant of Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with bp26 and omp31 genes deleted; administered subcutaneously or conjunctivally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 bp26 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The CGV26 mutant, deleted in the bp26 gene, was tested as a vaccine candidate alternative to the Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine for protection against Brucella ovis infection in sheep. Efficacy: CGV26 conferred significant protection against Brucella ovis, similar to that of Rev. 1 vaccine and significantly higher than the CGV2631 mutant. [Ref:6934]
c_preparation: Live attenuated deletion mutant of Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with bp26 gene deleted; administered subcutaneously or conjunctivally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 delta fba delta tal live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study proposes that deleting the genes encoding fructose-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba) and transaldolase (Tal) in the Brucella melitensis live-attenuated Rev. 1 vaccine strain blocks erythritol incorporation into central carbon metabolism, potentially reducing placental proliferation and adverse reproductive effects. Efficacy: The Rev1ΔfbaΔtal mutant provided comparable protection to the parental Rev. 1 vaccine in mice. [Ref:7259]
c_preparation: A double mutant of the Rev. 1 strain with deletions in fba and tal genes, unable to metabolize erythritol.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 delta wzm live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate Rev1Δwzm was developed as a derivative of B. melitensis strain Rev. 1 with a wzm gene deletion, aiming to improve safety and efficacy compared to the conventional Rev. 1 vaccine, especially for use in both young and adult sheep. Efficacy: Rev1Δwzm protected rams against Brucella ovis infection 25 weeks after vaccination, demonstrating effective protection in the target host. [Ref:7246]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with wzm gene deletion; green fluorescent protein tagging was used to identify vaccinated sheep.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 inactivated vaccine
c_description: The inactivated antigen was prepared and used to immunize guinea pigs to study immunity and macrophage migration inhibition. Efficacy: An association between macrophage migration inhibition and resistance to infection was demonstrated [Ref:7339]
c_preparation: Soluble protein antigen prepared from Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1, inactivated
c_antigen: soluble protein antigen from Brucella melitensis Rev I

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 wzm deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study constructed wzm/wzt single- and double-deletion mutants using the attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 as the parental strain to investigate the biological implications of the Wzm/Wzt system and its potential as a vaccine. Efficacy: Rev1Δwzm mutant was highly attenuated yet immunogenic and effective as a vaccine against Brucella melitensis and Brucella ovis in mice; it showed low persistence but maintained efficacy. [Ref:7206]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 with wzm gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain RM57 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A rough mutant RM57 was artificially induced from a Brucella melitensis isolate M1981 to overcome disadvantages of traditional live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: RM57 was attenuated and conferred good protection against virulent Brucella melitensis challenge, especially in the guinea pig model. [Ref:7082]
c_preparation: Rough mutant strain RM57 with altered LPS; no significant change in LPS gene expression but increased sensitivity to polymyxin B indicating altered outer membrane integrity.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain RM57 vaccine
c_description: The rough-type Brucella melitensis mutant strain RM57 was artificially induced from the parent strain M1981 and showed protective effects in guinea pigs, indicating it is a good vaccine candidate. Efficacy: RM57 showed reduced virulence in macrophage and mice infection models and protective effects in guinea pigs. [Ref:7155]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain streptomycin non dependent live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Whole organism vaccine
c_description: The vaccine strain was isolated and its properties and behavior studied to evaluate its ability to immunize goats against brucella infection and prevent abortion. Efficacy: Demonstrated immunization of goats against brucella infection and protection against abortion; efficacy differed between heat-killed and living cell vaccines. [Ref:6892]
c_preparation: Both heat-killed and living cells of the strain were used as vaccine formulations.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain WRR51 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Two defined nonreverting rough mutants were derived from virulent Brucella melitensis strain 16M as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: WRR51 showed better survival in hMDMs compared to WRRP1 and less attenuation in mice compared to dual mutant WRRP1. [Ref:6951]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with wboA deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain WRRP1 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Two defined nonreverting rough mutants were derived from virulent Brucella melitensis strain 16M as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: WRRP1 exhibited reduced survival in hMDMs and persisted for 1 week or less in mice, showing more severe attenuation than single mutants. [Ref:6951]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant with dual deletions in wboA and purEK.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain WRRP1 live attenuated vaccine expressing wboA and Bacillus anthracis protective antigen
c_description: The study investigated simultaneous expression of a homologous antigen (wboA gene encoding mannosyltransferase for LPS O-antigen biosynthesis) and a heterologous antigen (Bacillus anthracis pag gene encoding protective antigen) in an attenuated rough Brucella melitensis strain. Efficacy: Strain WRSPA induced protection in BALB/c mice against B. melitensis 16M challenge but failed to protect A/J mice against B. anthracis Sterne strain challenge. [Ref:6943]
c_preparation: The wboA and pag genes were cloned into plasmid pBBR4MCS and introduced into O-antigen deficient B. melitensis strain WRRP1 to produce strain WRSPA, which expressed O-antigen and protective antigen products.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis strain znBM-mC live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A novel live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain znBM-mC was developed and characterized for immunity. Efficacy: Vaccination conferred nearly complete protection in lungs and spleens from Brucella colonization; full protection observed in CD4-/-, CD8-/-, and wild-type mice; partial protection in IL-17-/- mice (lungs protected, spleen not). [Ref:7209]
c_preparation: Administered via an oral prime followed by an intranasal boost.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis streptomycin dependent mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study investigates immunity induced by a streptomycin-dependent mutant of Brucella melitensis. [Ref:6891]
c_preparation: Live attenuated streptomycin-dependent mutant strain of Brucella melitensis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis streptomycin-dependent mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_type: Whole organism vaccine + Live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study investigated immunization against Brucella infection using viable and nonviable suspensions of a streptomycin-dependent mutant of Brucella melitensis. [Ref:6894]
c_preparation: Viable (live) and nonviable (inactivated) suspensions of the streptomycin-dependent mutant were used.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis subunit vaccine using outer membrane proteins
c_description: Proteins extracted by hot saline or released into outer membrane blebs from field strains of Brucella melitensis were analyzed and found to be antigenically related to those of B. ovis. Efficacy: Not directly reported; antigenic similarity and conservation suggest potential for subcellular vaccine development. [Ref:7048]
c_preparation: Subcellular proteins present in hot saline extracts and outer membrane blebs, similar in profile to B. ovis proteins.
c_antigen: proteins of 43 kDa; group A (25.5 to 32.0 kDa); group B (21.5 to 22.5 kDa); group C (18.0 to 19.5 kDa); group D (13.0 to 15.5 kDa)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis T cell epitope virus-like particle subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a new-generation vaccine by presenting selected Brucella melitensis T cell epitopes on the surface of Orbivirus core-like particles (CLPs) transiently expressed in Nicotiana benthamiana plants. Efficacy: One of the three chimeric CLPs induced protection against virulent Brucella strain challenge equivalent to the commercial Rev. 1 vaccine; all three were safe at specific antigen doses. [Ref:7248]
c_preparation: Five chimeric CLPs were assembled in plants, each presenting a different T cell epitope; three highest-yielding CLPs were selected for further study.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis TF BP26 Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study addresses the need for a protective subunit vaccine against Brucella melitensis due to problems with the live attenuated Rev. 1 vaccine used in ovine brucellosis prophylaxis. Efficacy: Not reported (no in vivo or in vitro efficacy data presented) [Ref:7008]
c_preparation: A synthetic chimeric gene encoding fragments of TF, BP26 (93-111), and Omp31 (48-74) proteins was designed and modeled in silico to predict the 3D structure.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor Bp26 Omp31 subunit vaccine with aluminum hydroxide adjuvant
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate immune responses induced by a chimeric protein consisting of trigger factor, Bp26, and Omp31 loaded on aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles as an adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice with AH/TBO nanoparticles showed a higher reduction of bacterial culture after challenge compared to Se/TBO nanoparticles and TBO alone. [Ref:7235]
c_preparation: Recombinant chimeric protein (TBO) loaded onto aluminum hydroxide nanoparticles (~60 nm size) administered subcutaneously.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor Bp26 Omp31 subunit vaccine with selenium nanoparticle adjuvant
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate immune responses induced by a chimeric protein consisting of trigger factor, Bp26, and Omp31 loaded on selenium nanoparticles as an adjuvant. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice with Se/TBO nanoparticles showed reduction of bacterial culture after challenge, but less than AH/TBO nanoparticles. [Ref:7235]
c_preparation: Recombinant chimeric protein (TBO) loaded onto selenium nanoparticles (~150 nm size) administered subcutaneously.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor DNA vaccine
c_description: The Brucella melitensis 16M genome was screened for immunogenic proteins; trigger factor was identified as a protective antigen. Efficacy: trigger factor DNA vaccine conferred protection against wild-type B. melitensis 16M challenge; combined with bp26, protection was significantly enhanced. [Ref:6909]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant plasmid encoding trigger factor used for intramuscular DNA immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis trigger factor Omp31 BP26 fusion subunit vaccine
c_description: The study focuses on a chimeric gene encoding fragments of trigger factor, Omp31, and BP26 from Brucella melitensis as a potential subunit vaccine candidate due to concerns about live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: Antibodies against rTOB were detected in 76.5% of sera from infected patients; vaccinated rabbit sera strongly reacted with rTOB. [Ref:7034]
c_preparation: Recombinant fusion protein (rTOB) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21-DE3 and purified by Ni-NTA agarose column.
c_antigen: trigger factor (TF), Omp31(48-74), BP26(87-111) fusion protein (TOB)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis UGPase deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study identifies UGPase as a critical determinant of Brucella virulence and immunogenicity, demonstrating that deletion of UGPase disrupts LPS synthesis, leading to a rough phenotype and reduced virulence. Efficacy: The UGPase deletion mutant showed impaired ability to infect host cells, diminished pathogenicity in mice, altered LPS structure with reduced binding to Brucella-positive serum, and induced a protective pro-inflammatory cytokine profile. [Ref:7276]
c_preparation: A Brucella melitensis 16M strain with UGPase gene deletion (16M-ΔUGPase) was used as the vaccine candidate.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis virB2 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Constructed unmarked deletion mutants of virB2 gene in Brucella melitensis as vaccine candidates. Efficacy: Provided less protection compared to Deltaasp24 mutants against heterologous challenge. [Ref:700]
c_preparation: Live attenuated unmarked deletion mutant of virB2 gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis virB2 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine candidate BMDeltavirB2 was evaluated in pregnant goats, the natural host species for Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: BMDeltavirB2 was considered safe as it did not cause abortion or colonize fetal tissues and was protective against abortion and infection in the majority of pregnant goats, though less efficacious than BMDeltaasp24. [Ref:6918]
c_preparation: Unmarked deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine strain BMDeltavirB2.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis virB4 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The GR019 (virB4) mutant is an attenuated bioluminescent Brucella melitensis strain with mutation in virB4 gene. Efficacy: The GR019 mutant was attenuated in IRF-1(-/-) mice and cultured macrophages; vaccination conferred protection against virulent challenge. [Ref:6917]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strain expressing bioluminescence.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis vtlR mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vtlR mutant strain of Brucella melitensis M5 was constructed and shown to be essential for virulence, with deletion impairing bacterial growth on certain sugars and increasing sensitivity to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Efficacy: The vtlR mutant strain showed reduced intracellular survival and triggered reactive oxygen species production; importantly, it elicited protective immunity in mice. [Ref:7285]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vtlR deletion mutant strain of Brucella melitensis M5

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis WbkC subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope vaccine was designed using immunoinformatics methods targeting the WbkC protein, a methyltransferase involved in O-antigen biosynthesis of Brucella lipopolysaccharide, known to stimulate strong immune responses in mice. Efficacy: Vaccination with rWbkC significantly reduced bacterial loads in spleen and liver compared to PBS control (p < 0.001); rWbkC showed superior clearance of bacterial burden in liver compared to WbkC protein alone (p < 0.01). [Ref:7305]
c_preparation: Immunodominant linear B lymphocyte, cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and helper T lymphocyte epitopes of WbkC were linked with short connectors to construct the recombinant protein rWbkC; bioinformatics predicted high antigenicity, solubility, and no allergenicity or toxicity; molecular docking showed stable binding to TLR2/4.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis znBM-lacZ live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Two Brucella melitensis mutants, znBM-lacZ (znBMZ) and znBM-mCherry (znBM-mC), were developed to improve brucellosis vaccination and tested for systemic immunity against virulent B. melitensis challenge. Efficacy: znBMZ vaccination reduced splenic brucellae colonization by approximately 25,000-fold compared to PBS controls, outperforming B. abortus S19 vaccine which reduced colonization by 700-fold. [Ref:7239]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutants administered once by intraperitoneal route.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella melitensis znuA deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a live attenuated Brucella melitensis strain with deletion of the znuA gene involved in zinc transport, developed to provide protection against inhalational infection. Efficacy: Single oral vaccination rapidly cleared from mice within 2 weeks; effectively protected mice against nasal challenge with wild-type B. melitensis 16M; 83% of vaccinated mice had no detectable brucellae in spleens; enhanced clearance from lungs; partial protection observed in IFN-γ-deficient mice. [Ref:6968]
c_preparation: Live attenuated ΔznuA B. melitensis administered orally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope fusion subunit vaccine
c_description: The study developed a recombinant antigen by fusing the human Fc domain with Brucella's multi-epitope protein to target FcRn for mucosal vaccine delivery. Efficacy: Oral delivery elicited enhanced systemic immunity with elevated serum IgG titers, increased CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratios, significant mucosal IgA upregulation, long-term immune memory lasting six months, and markedly reduced Brucella colonization in visceral organs after challenge. [Ref:7274]
c_preparation: The vaccine was delivered orally via chitosan nanoparticles.
c_antigen: multi-epitope protein (MEV) fused with human Fc domain

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope peptide subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope peptide vaccine was designed in silico targeting five immunogenic Brucella antigens (Omp31, BP26, BLS, DnaK, L7-L12) fused with helper epitopes from Tetanus toxin fragment C to induce CD4+ helper T cell responses. Efficacy: Predicted to strongly induce T cell and B cell mediated immune responses based on immunoinformatics analysis. [Ref:7084]
c_preparation: Selected epitopes were linked by GPGPG linkers; cholera toxin B was linked to the N-terminal as an adjuvant using an EAAAK linker; the final construct was a 377 amino acid chimeric protein predicted to be soluble, stable, non-allergenic, and 40.59 kDa in size.
c_antigen: Omp31, BP26, BLS, DnaK, L7-L12, Tetanus toxin fragment C (TTFrC)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope subunit vaccine (seven-epitope, four-species design)
c_description: A multi-epitope peptide vaccine was designed using computational techniques selecting seven epitopes from four main Brucella species infecting humans, aiming to induce cellular and humoral immune responses without allergenic properties. Efficacy: The designed vaccine showed high potential to induce immune responses, especially cellular immunity, with appropriate physicochemical properties and predicted high expression potential in a prokaryotic system. [Ref:7222]
c_preparation: The vaccine structure included selected epitopes combined with suitable adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity; physicochemical and immunological properties were evaluated; two- and three-dimensional structures were predicted; docking with toll-like receptor 4 was performed; in silico cloning, codon optimization, and mRNA stability analyses were conducted for expression in Escherichia coli.
c_antigen: seven epitopes from four main Brucella species that infect humans

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multi-epitope subunit vaccine associated with LPS loaded chitosan nanoparticle
c_description: The study evaluated multi-epitope antigens associated with LPS loaded chitosan (LLC) or mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle (MCN) as adjuvants and delivery systems to enhance immune responses against Brucella infection. Efficacy: Vaccine candidates containing mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles provided a high percentage of protection against Brucella melitensis and Brucella abortus infection. [Ref:7214]
c_adjuvant: yes; mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle; LPS loaded chitosan
c_preparation: Multi-epitope antigens were formulated with either LPS loaded chitosan nanoparticles or mannosylated chitosan nanoparticles.

c_vaccine_name:
Brucella multi-epitope subunit vaccine associated with mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle
===
c_adjuvant: yes; mannosylated chitosan nanoparticle; LPS loaded chitosan

c_vaccine_name: Brucella multivalent DNA vaccine
c_description: Attenuated live Brucella strains cause side effects and are unsuitable for humans; a safer vaccine was developed by constructing plasmid DNA expressing six Brucella proteins. Efficacy: The single low-dose injection exerted a reliable protective effect against subsequent Brucella challenge. [Ref:7266]
c_preparation: Plasmid DNA complexes with linear polyethylenimine to enhance DNA delivery.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella neotomae 26 kDa periplasmic protein gamma irradiated live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Recombinant B. neotomae overexpressing a 26 kDa periplasmic protein was evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant resistance against challenge with virulent Brucella species. [Ref:6958]
c_preparation: Recombinant B. neotomae rendered non-replicative by gamma-radiation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella neotomae gamma irradiated live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate Brucella neotomae, a bacterium not known to cause disease, as a vaccine platform for human brucellosis. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant resistance against challenge with virulent B. abortus, B. melitensis, and B. suis. [Ref:6958]
c_preparation: B. neotomae rendered non-replicative by gamma-radiation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella neotomae superoxide dismutase gamma irradiated live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Recombinant B. neotomae overexpressing superoxide dismutase was evaluated as a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant resistance against challenge with virulent Brucella species. [Ref:6958]
c_preparation: Recombinant B. neotomae rendered non-replicative by gamma-radiation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella neotomae wboA deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A rough, live-attenuated Brucella neotomae strain was generated by deleting the wboA gene encoding a glycosyltransferase, resulting in loss of the O-side chain in lipopolysaccharide (LPS) allowing serological differentiation from field-infected animals. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significantly higher protection against virulent Brucella suis 1330 challenge compared to controls; the rough mutant was cleared from mice within 6 weeks even at high dose (2 x 10^8 CFU). [Ref:7147]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain lacking O-side chain due to wboA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella O-polysaccharide C epitope vaccine
c_description: The study revisited the structural identity of the C epitope of Brucella O-polysaccharide, revealing a unique capping perosamine tetrasaccharide with specific interresidue linkages essential for the epitope. [Ref:7037]
c_preparation: Synthetic oligosaccharide glycoconjugates were used to demonstrate the structural requirements of the epitope.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella O-polysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study developed a high-performance bioconjugate nanovaccine by introducing a self-assembly nanoparticle platform and an O-linked glycosylation system into Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O:9, which has an O-polysaccharide composed of the same unit as Brucella. Efficacy: The nanovaccine provided cross-protection against B. abortus, B. melitensis, and B. suis lethal dose challenges and improved clearance of B. melitensis in non-lethal infection. [Ref:7233]
c_preparation: A self-assembled bioconjugate nanovaccine coupling polysaccharide antigens with nano carriers was prepared and confirmed stable.
c_antigen: O-polysaccharide from Yersinia enterocolitica serotype O:9

c_vaccine_name: Brucella O-specific polysaccharide conjugate ferritin nanoparticle vaccine
c_description: The study developed a bioconjugate nanovaccine by enzymatically coupling Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 O-specific polysaccharide, a structural analogue of Brucella antigens, to a self-assembled ferritin nanoparticle, creating a stable and monodisperse nanoparticle platform for targeted antigen delivery. Efficacy: The vaccine induced a robust immune response that provided strong protection against Brucella infection in mice. [Ref:7283]
