c_preparation: A ferritin nanoparticle platform conjugated with Yersinia enterocolitica O:9 O-specific polysaccharide via bacterial glycosylation-driven synthetic strategy, forming a bioconjugate nanovaccine (Fn-OPS) with stability at room temperature and confirmed in vivo safety.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp16 subunit vaccine
c_description: U-Omp16 from Brucella spp. was delivered by the nasal route as an adjuvant to induce immune responses. Efficacy: U-Omp16 increased antigen presence in lung tissues, induced systemic IgG and Th1 responses to ovalbumin, and ameliorated hypersensitivity to cow's milk protein by reducing clinical signs and anti-CMP IgE antibodies. [Ref:6998]
c_preparation: Unlipidated outer membrane protein Omp16 (U-Omp16) administered intranasally, co-administered with ovalbumin as a model antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP16 vaccine
c_description: OMP16 is a key Brucella virulence factor essential for bacterial survival and functions as a protective antigen capable of activating host immunity. The study focuses on monoclonal antibodies targeting OMP16 to identify protective epitopes for vaccine development. Efficacy: Both monoclonal antibodies H4 and E6 reduced bacterial loads and mitigated splenic and hepatic pathology in murine challenge studies. E6 additionally triggered complement-dependent bacteriolysis. [Ref:7291]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp19 live attenuated vaccine delivered by Salmonella recombinant vector
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Oral administration of live attenuated Salmonella secreting Brucella Omp19 antigen with antacid buffers to neutralize stomach acidity and improve vaccine viability. Efficacy: Significant enhancement of antigen-specific protective immune responses against virulent Brucella challenge with antacid co-administration. [Ref:7182]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella vector secreting Brucella Omp19 antigen co-administered orally with sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based gastric antacid buffers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp19 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify multi-epitope vaccine candidates based on the outer membrane protein Omp19 of Brucella, which is widely expressed, highly conserved, and immunogenic. [Ref:7220]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP19 OMP16 OMP25 L7/L12 multiepitope subunit vaccine
c_description: The study developed a novel IgG-Fc-fused multiepitope vaccine (MEV-Fc) based on immunodominant epitopes of Brucella antigens OMP19, OMP16, OMP25, and L7/L12, identified using an epitope- and structure-based vaccinology platform. Efficacy: MEV-Fc exerted a significant protective effect against Brucella infection compared to the PBS control group. [Ref:7270]
c_preparation: MEV-Fc was expressed and purified via an Escherichia coli expression system.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP19 SODC recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aims to develop a new human brucellosis vaccine using recombinant capripoxvirus vectors expressing Brucella antigens. [Ref:7282]
c_preparation: Recombinant capripoxvirus SPPV (TK-) expressing OMP19 and SODC antigens cultivated in Vero cells using BelloStage™-3000 bioreactor with BioNOC II® macrocarriers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp22 Omp19 Omp28 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: This study designed a safe and effective multi-epitope vaccine based on dominant T and B cell epitopes of Brucella outer membrane proteins Omp22, Omp19, and Omp28 using bioinformatics methods. [Ref:7190]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct combined T/B dominant epitopes of Omp22, Omp19, and Omp28 linked by HEYGAALEREAG and GGGS linkers, with carrier sequences linked at the N- and C-termini via EAAAK linkers; the tertiary structure and physicochemical properties were analyzed in silico.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify multi-epitope vaccine candidates based on the outer membrane protein Omp25 of Brucella, which is widely expressed, highly conserved, and immunogenic. [Ref:7220]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP25 recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aims to develop a new human brucellosis vaccine using recombinant capripoxvirus vectors expressing Brucella antigens. [Ref:7282]
c_preparation: Recombinant capripoxvirus SPPV (TK-) expressing OMP25 antigen cultivated in Vero cells using BelloStage™-3000 bioreactor with BioNOC II® macrocarriers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study selected two important vaccine candidate proteins for brucellosis, rOmp25 and rEipB, as models to evaluate recombinant protein production for vaccine purposes. [Ref:7238]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins produced in Escherichia coli BL21 expression system.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25 vaccine
c_description: The study identifies Omp25 as a key factor promoting Brucella intracellular survival and proliferation by activating the host unfolded protein response (UPR). Omp25 is highlighted as a potential target for therapeutic interventions and next-generation attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: The omp25-deleted strains showed impaired intracellular replication and reduced UPR activation, resulting in attenuated induction of inflammatory genes. Mice infected with the omp25 mutant strain exhibited lower bacterial burdens and milder tissue pathology compared with wild-type infected mice. [Ref:7300]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp25c subunit vaccine
c_description: The study discusses the potential interest of Omp25c and Omp31b as subcellular vaccines based on their occurrence in Brucella strains and antigenic relatedness with other family proteins. [Ref:6938]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP2a OMP2b OMP1 OMP25 OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study designed a multi-epitope vaccine targeting conserved regions of Brucella outer membrane proteins OMP2a, OMP2b, OMP1, OMP25, and OMP31 using immunoinformatics approaches, aiming to overcome drawbacks of live attenuated vaccines. Efficacy: The vaccine construct demonstrated antigenicity, non-allergenicity, and stable binding to TLR2 and TLR4 receptors in silico, with immune simulations indicating potential to induce immune responses; however, efficacy requires validation in laboratory and animal models. [Ref:7294]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct consists of selected HTL, CTL, and B-cell epitopes connected by flexible linkers (GGSSGG), fused at the N-terminus to Cholera Toxin B subunit as an adjuvant, and includes a His-tag at the C-terminus for purification; the tertiary structure was modeled and refined in silico.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b Omp31 CTLA-4 variable region fusion vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to improve safety and immune protection of Brucella vaccines by designing a fusion vaccine using bioinformatics approaches, linking Omp2b and Omp31 proteins and fusing the CTLA-4 variable region to the N-terminal of the epitope sequence. Efficacy: The designed fusion vaccine showed high potency against Brucella based on bioinformatics analyses. [Ref:7228]
c_preparation: A fusion protein vaccine was designed by sequentially linking Omp2b and Omp31 proteins and fusing the CTLA-4 variable region at the N-terminal; molecular docking showed strong affinity with B7-1 and B7-2.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b protein vaccine
c_description: This study analyzed the physicochemical properties, structural characteristics, and dominant epitopes of Brucella outer membrane protein 2b (Omp2b) to provide a theoretical basis for constructing a multivalent epitope vaccine. [Ref:7167]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp2b subunit vaccine; Brucella Omp2b DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated immunogenicity and protective efficacy of Brucella outer membrane protein 2b (Omp2b) using three immunization strategies: protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/protein in BALB/c mice. Efficacy: DNA/protein regimen conferred higher protection levels against B. melitensis and B. abortus challenge compared to protein or DNA alone. [Ref:7075]
c_preparation: Three vaccine regimens: protein/protein, DNA/DNA, and DNA/protein using Omp2b antigen.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella OMP31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to design vaccines and drugs for brucellosis using protein modeling, epitope prediction, and molecular docking of the target proteins BvrR, OMP25, and OMP31. [Ref:7245]
c_preparation: Tertiary structure models of the three target proteins were constructed and analyzed for epitopes including B cell, cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and T helper lymphocyte epitopes; no specific formulation was reported.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella Omp31b subunit vaccine
c_description: The study discusses the potential interest of Omp25c and Omp31b as subcellular vaccines based on their occurrence in Brucella strains and antigenic relatedness with other family proteins. [Ref:6938]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Existing Brucella vaccines are attenuated and can cause vaccine-associated brucellosis; subunit vaccines are safer but poorly immunogenic; LDH was added as an adjuvant to enhance immune response. Efficacy: LDH subunit vaccine induced higher specific antibody levels and Th1-type immune responses compared to Freund's adjuvant; mice had significantly lower splenic bacterial loads; LDH-OMV vaccine provided higher protection against Brucella infection. [Ref:7224]
c_preparation: LDH combined with Brucella outer-membrane vesicles and OMV-associated proteins to form a subunit vaccine.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis antigenic complex HS vaccine
c_description: Microparticles containing an antigenic complex from Brucella ovis (HS) were prepared by double emulsion solvent evaporation using two different polyesters for vaccine purposes against brucellosis. Efficacy: Not directly reported; however, HS-PEC microparticles showed antigen release in boosters and enhanced phagocytosis, suggesting potential effectiveness. [Ref:6882]
c_preparation: Antigenic complex HS encapsulated in polyester microparticles made from poly-lactide-co-glycolide acid (75:25; RG 756) or poly-epsilon-caprolactone (PEC), forming smooth spherical sub-5 micrometer particles with ~30% antigen encapsulation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis antigenic complex vaccine
c_description: This study developed a novel formulation strategy for delivering the Brucella ovis antigenic extract (HS) into ovine mucosal surfaces. [Ref:6944]
c_preparation: HS was entrapped in conventional and mannosylated poly(anhydride) nanoparticles prepared by solvent displacement method; nanoparticles were gamma-irradiated at 10 kGy or 25 kGy for sterilization suitable for ophthalmic administration.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis attenuated ΔabcBA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is an attenuated live vaccine model with deletion of abcBA genes. Efficacy: β-glucan training did not enhance the efficacy of this attenuated vaccine; trained innate immunity exerted a detrimental influence on its efficacy. [Ref:7298]
c_preparation: Live attenuated vaccine based on Brucella ovis ΔabcBA mutant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis BLSOmp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: This study tested a new delivery system for mucosal immunization with BLSOmp31 in a murine model to improve efficacy over previous formulations. Efficacy: BLSOmp31/CpG-ODN/Coa-ASC16 administered subcutaneously conferred significant protection against B. ovis challenge; ocular administration showed a similar degree of protection (3.66 and 3.60 logs of protection, respectively). [Ref:7185]
c_preparation: BLSOmp31 formulated with class B CpG-ODN in a nanostructure called Coa-ASC16; compared with BLSOmp31 alone, BLSOmp31 with CpG-ODN, and BLSOmp31 emulsified in Incomplete Freund Adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis delta abcBA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: This study aimed to evaluate protection induced by the vaccine candidate B. ovis ΔabcBA against experimental challenge with wild type B. ovis in rams. Efficacy: Immunization, particularly with encapsulated B. ovis ΔabcBA, prevented infection, secretion of wild type B. ovis in semen and urine, shedding of neutrophils in semen, and development of clinical changes, gross and microscopic lesions induced by wild type B. ovis. [Ref:7041]
c_preparation: B. ovis ΔabcBA strain encapsulated with sterile alginate or non encapsulated vaccine strain.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis Deltaomp25 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Omp25 was examined as a potential vaccine candidate by creating a mutant strain with disruption of the omp25 gene. Efficacy: Vaccination with BO25 resulted in clearance of the challenge strain and provided 2.5 log10 greater protection against virulent B. ovis than vaccine strain Rev. 1. [Ref:1946]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella ovis strain with omp25 gene disruption (BO25).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis gamma irradiated live attenuated vaccine with Montanide ISA 61 adjuvant
c_description: The study evaluated reactogenicity, antibody responses, and protection of γ-irradiated Brucella ovis antigen formulated with Montanide ISA 61 adjuvant. Efficacy: Montanide ISA 61 formulation induced milder reactogenicity compared to alginate/chitosan and elicited higher levels of IgG2b, an important marker of cellular immune response; protection data not explicitly detailed. [Ref:7242]
c_preparation: γ-irradiated Brucella ovis antigen formulated with Montanide ISA 61 emulsion adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis gamma-irradiated inactivated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is an inactivated formulation prepared by gamma irradiation of Brucella ovis. Efficacy: β-glucan training markedly reduced bacterial colonization in mice vaccinated with this inactivated vaccine. [Ref:7298]
c_preparation: Gamma-irradiated inactivated vaccine.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hdeA deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study also evaluated a hdeA deletion mutant and a double mucR and hdeA deletion mutant of Brucella ovis PA. Efficacy: Deletion of hdeA alone did not modify evaluated properties; however, the double mutant showed attenuation and persistence similar to mucR single mutant, supporting evaluation as attenuated vaccine candidates. [Ref:7201]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella ovis PA strain with hdeA gene deletion; also combined with mucR deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hot saline antigenic extract subunit vaccine bearing poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles
c_description: A hot saline antigenic extract from Brucella ovis was encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles to create a vaccine candidate. Efficacy: Subcutaneous or oral administration of HS-PEC protected mice against B. ovis infection with protection similar to the Rev. 1 vaccine; subcutaneous vaccination with HS-PEC was as effective as Rev. 1 in protecting against B. abortus infection; free HS or empty PEC microparticles did not confer protection. [Ref:6879]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of the hot saline antigenic extract encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles (HS-PEC).
c_antigen: hot saline antigenic extract (HS) from Brucella ovis

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hot saline complex subunit vaccine encapsulated in mannosylated nanoparticles
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the protection offered by the hot saline complex extracted from Brucella ovis encapsulated in mannosylated nanoparticles when administered conjunctivally. Efficacy: Vaccinated animals showed a 3-log reduction in spleen colony forming units compared to unvaccinated controls; protection was significantly higher than that observed with the commercial Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine administered subcutaneously. [Ref:6980]
c_preparation: The vaccine consisted of hot saline complex antigen encapsulated in mannosylated nanoparticles of approximately 300 nm size, with antigen loading close to 30 μg per mg nanoparticle; the encapsulated antigen maintained protein profile, structural integrity, and antigenicity.
c_antigen: hot saline complex extracted from Brucella ovis (HS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis hot saline extract subunit vaccine
c_description: Vaccination with hot saline extract (HS) conferred good protection against Brucella ovis infection, with protection greatly enhanced by incorporation of QS-21 or other adjuvants. Efficacy: HS-QS-21 vaccine afforded protection against B. ovis challenge as good as that developed after primary infection and as good as or better than that provided by attenuated Brucella melitensis strain Rev. 1 vaccine. [Ref:7341]
c_preparation: Subcellular vaccine consisting of hot saline extract proteins; adjuvanted formulations included QS-21 or other adjuvants.
c_antigen: protein moieties of hot saline extract

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis Hot Saline extract vaccine
c_description: The antigenic extract Hot Saline from Brucella ovis was microencapsulated by spray-drying with different polyesters to develop microparticles smaller than 5 micrometers as a vaccine delivery system. Efficacy: Not reported (no in vivo efficacy data provided) [Ref:6886]
c_preparation: Microparticles prepared by spray-drying using poly-lactide-co-glycolide RG502H (PLGA) and blends with poly-epsilon-caprolactone (PEC) with varying ratios; formulations with higher PEC showed better macrophage uptake and less acidification.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis inactivated saline in oil vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was administered to adult ewes and rams by intraperitoneal and subcutaneous routes to study local tissue reactions. [Ref:6906]
c_preparation: Inactivated Brucella ovis formulated as a saline-in-oil emulsion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis inactivated saline in-oil vaccine
c_description: The study compared four vaccination methods using the inactivated Brucella ovis saline in-oil vaccine in rams. Efficacy: Two spaced doses given subcutaneously induced a more consistent, persistent, and higher magnitude serological response than a single dose or intraperitoneal administration. [Ref:6905]
c_preparation: Inactivated Brucella ovis vaccine formulated in saline in-oil adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis inactivated vaccine
c_description: An aluminum hydroxide adsorbed bacterin administered as two injections spaced 3-6 weeks apart conferred significant and acceptable immunity. Efficacy: Conferred a significant and acceptable level of immunity. [Ref:6875]
c_preparation: Aluminum hydroxide adsorbed bacterin administered as two injections spaced 3-6 weeks apart.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis inactivated vaccine with hydroxide adjuvant
c_description: Two killed vaccines were produced using four strains of Brucella ovis, differing by the adjuvant used (hydroxide or oil). Vaccination was applied twice at an interval of 20 days to rams under experimental and field conditions. Efficacy: Rams treated with the hydroxide adjuvant vaccine developed immunity; postvaccinal antibodies disappeared after three months. [Ref:7322]
c_preparation: Killed (inactivated) vaccine formulated with hydroxide adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis inactivated vaccine with oil adjuvant
c_description: Two killed vaccines were produced using four strains of Brucella ovis, differing by the adjuvant used (hydroxide or oil). Vaccination was applied twice at an interval of 20 days to rams under experimental and field conditions. Efficacy: Rams treated with the oil adjuvant vaccine built up solid immunity. [Ref:7322]
c_preparation: Killed (inactivated) vaccine formulated with oil adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis live attenuated vaccine wbkC deletion wbdR tagged
c_description: The vaccine is a modified Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 strain deleted in wbkC (lipopolysaccharide formyl-transferase) and carrying wbdR (E. coli acetyl-transferase) to induce an antibody response distinguishable from wild-type strains and to avoid interference with B. melitensis serodiagnosis. Efficacy: The modified Rev. 1 vaccine was comparatively attenuated and provided protection against Brucella ovis infection in mice. [Ref:7146]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 strain with wbkC gene deletion and wbdR gene insertion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis mucR deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study constructed and characterized a mucR deletion mutant of virulent Brucella ovis PA, which affects surface properties and virulence. Efficacy: The mucR deletion mutants showed virulence attenuation but established persistent splenic infection in mice, suggesting potential as specific attenuated vaccines against Brucella ovis. [Ref:7201]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Brucella ovis PA strain with mucR gene deletion; also studied a double mutant with hdeA deletion.
c_antigen: mucR deletion mutant; hdeA deletion mutant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis Omp16 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify protective outer membrane proteins (OMPs) of Brucella ovis as vaccine candidates by testing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against these antigens for protection in mice. Efficacy: Monoclonal antibodies to Omp16, Omp19, and Omp31 provided significant protection against B. ovis challenge, reducing spleen infection and preventing splenomegaly; mAbs to Omp31 maintained protection even in mixtures with nonprotective mAbs. [Ref:6871]
c_preparation: Monoclonal antibodies against individual or combinations of OMPs and rough lipopolysaccharide (R-LPS) were used for passive immunization; a mouse serum raised against B. ovis hot-saline extract containing antibodies to both OMPs and R-LPS was used as a positive control.
c_antigen: Omp16; Omp19; Omp31; Omp10; Omp25; Omp2b; Omp1; rough lipopolysaccharide (R-LPS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis omp22 deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Two previously characterized B. ovis attenuated mutants including Δomp22 were evaluated as homologous vaccines for specific prophylaxis of B. ovis infection. Efficacy: Protective efficacy against B. ovis similar to that observed with B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine. [Ref:7009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis omp25d deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Two previously characterized B. ovis attenuated mutants including Δomp25d were evaluated as homologous vaccines for specific prophylaxis of B. ovis infection. Efficacy: Protective efficacy against B. ovis similar to that observed with B. melitensis Rev 1 vaccine. [Ref:7009]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis outer membrane complex microparticle vaccine
c_description: A safer vaccine alternative to Brucella melitensis Rev. 1 was developed using an outer membrane complex from Brucella ovis encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles. Efficacy: Vaccination with 800 microg HS-PEC microparticles induced adequate serological response and conferred protection against Brucella ovis challenge similar to that of the live attenuated Rev. 1 vaccine; lower dose (80 microg) was less effective; revaccination increased serological response but not protection. [Ref:6912]
c_preparation: Outer membrane complex antigen from Brucella ovis encapsulated in poly-epsilon-caprolactone microparticles prepared by a double emulsion solvent evaporation method (TROMS), with antigen loading about 13 microg HS per mg microparticles.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis outer membrane protein and rough lipopolysaccharide subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to identify protective antigens of Brucella ovis to develop a safe, specific subcellular vaccine for ram epididymitis. Efficacy: Mixtures of MAbs against specific OMPs and anti-R-LPS MAb alone conferred significant protection compared to controls; combination of OMP MAbs with anti-R-LPS MAb was strongly protective. [Ref:7326]
c_preparation: Monoclonal antibodies directed against multiple outer membrane proteins and rough lipopolysaccharide were tested individually and in combination.
c_antigen: outer-membrane proteins (16.5-, 25-27-, 31-34- and 36-38-kDa OMPs); rough lipopolysaccharide (R-LPS)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis Ovis antigen vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to optimize radiolabeling of mannosylated Gantrez nanoparticles loaded with Brucella ovis antigen for ocular vaccination and to study their biodistribution in mice. Efficacy: Not directly reported; the formulation showed biodistribution in nasal mucosa and gastrointestinal tract, suggesting effective antigen delivery. [Ref:6990]
c_preparation: Mannosylated Gantrez nanoparticles loaded with Brucella ovis antigen (Man-NP-HS) prepared by solvent displacement, purified, lyophilized, and radiolabeled with technetium-99m.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis pyruvate phosphate dikinase deletion live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study reports the generation of a pyruvate phosphate dikinase (PpdK) deletion mutant in Brucella ovis PA strains (both CO2-dependent and CO2-independent) as a potential vaccine candidate. Efficacy: The PpdK mutant showed impaired growth in vitro, inability to multiply in infected cells, and an unusual attenuation pattern in mice with initial higher spleen colonization followed by marked decrease, indicating attenuation and potential as a vaccine candidate. [Ref:7175]
c_preparation: Live attenuated mutant strains with deletion of the PpdK gene impairing growth and virulence.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis strain delta abcBA live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the Brucella ovis ΔabcBA strain as a vaccine candidate in mice to assess protection against wild-type B. ovis challenge. Efficacy: Single or multiple immunizations with non-encapsulated strain provided mild protection with reduced liver bacterial loads but not spleen; encapsulated vaccine significantly improved protection in both mouse strains and prevented lesions in spleen and liver. [Ref:7032]
c_preparation: The vaccine was formulated as an encapsulated live attenuated ΔabcBA strain; both single and multiple doses were tested, with encapsulation significantly improving protection.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis strain H38 delta wbkF delta wadB live attenuated vaccine; Brucella ovis strain H38 delta wbkF delta wadC live attenuated vaccine
c_description: Mutants of H38ΔwbkF vaccine with additional deletions in wadB or wadC genes, altering sugars of the rough LPS core tetrasaccharide branch, were constructed to minimize serological interference. Efficacy: These core-defective mutants were over-attenuated and failed to protect mice against infection. [Ref:7301]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutants with deletions in wbkF plus wadB or wadC genes; administered subcutaneously in mice.
c_antigen: wbkF deletion; wadB deletion; wadC deletion

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis strain H38 delta wbkF live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The vaccine is a rough mutant of Brucella melitensis strain H38 with deletion of wbkF gene, previously shown to protect rams against B. ovis infection without interfering in S-LPS-based serological tests. Efficacy: H38ΔwbkF vaccine protected rams against B. ovis infection similarly to B. melitensis Rev. 1 vaccine; core-defective mutants (wadB and wadC deletions) were over-attenuated and failed to protect mice; conjunctival administration preserved efficacy in rams. [Ref:7301]
c_preparation: Live attenuated rough mutant strain H38ΔwbkF administered by subcutaneous or conjunctival routes; conjunctival administration explored to reduce serological interference.
c_antigen: wbkF deletion; wadB deletion; wadC deletion (mutants studied)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis vitamin E adjuvant vaccine
c_description: Rams vaccinated at 6-8 months of age with a water-in-oil Brucella ovis-vitamin E adjuvant vaccine. Efficacy: Rams vaccinated with the vitamin E adjuvant vaccine had significantly higher serum antibody levels than those vaccinated with commercial B. ovis bacterin or B. melitensis Rev. 1; higher antibody levels persisted two years post-vaccination. [Ref:6954]
c_preparation: Water-in-oil emulsion with vitamin E as adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis wadB mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The wadB mutant of Brucella ovis was generated by mutating the wadB gene, which encodes an LPS core glycosyltransferase, resulting in defects in LPS structure and outer membrane topology. Efficacy: The wadB mutant was attenuated in mice and protected them against B. ovis challenge. [Ref:7013]
c_preparation: Live attenuated wadB mutant strain of Brucella ovis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella ovis wadC mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The wadC mutant of Brucella ovis was generated by mutating the wadC gene, which encodes an LPS core glycosyltransferase, resulting in defects in LPS structure and outer membrane topology. Efficacy: The wadC mutant was attenuated in mice and protected them against B. ovis challenge. [Ref:7013]
c_preparation: Live attenuated wadC mutant strain of Brucella ovis.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella P39 DNA vaccine
c_description: Eukaryotic expression vector pCIP39 encoding P39 constructed and verified for protein expression in COS-7 cells. Efficacy: Induced higher antibody responses than bacterioferritin vaccine; elicited a strong and long-lived memory immune response lasting at least 3 months; induced a typical T-helper 1-dominated immune response; induced moderate protection against B. abortus 544 challenge. [Ref:2291]
c_preparation: Intramuscular injection of plasmid DNA vector pCIP39, administered three times at 3-week intervals.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella pgm mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The pgm mutant of Brucella was constructed and studied for its biological function and effects on human trophoblast cells. Efficacy: The pgm mutant showed reduced adhesion and infection of human trophoblast cells compared to Brucella vaccine strain M5-90; sera of mice immunized with the pgm mutant were negative by agglutination tests. [Ref:6986]
c_preparation: Live pgm mutant strain of Brucella.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella phosphoglucomutase subunit vaccine
c_description: Purified PGM protein was used to infect human trophoblast cells to study its effects. [Ref:6986]
c_preparation: Purified PGM protein.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella protective antigen subunit vaccine
c_description: The study investigated the protective function of cells at the local inflammatory focus caused by administration of live Brucella culture to guinea pigs immunized with the protective antigen at optimal and increased doses. Efficacy: Optimal dose of protective antigen enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of Brucella; increased dose suppressed macrophage ingestive and digestive functions. [Ref:7362]
c_preparation: Protective antigen administered at optimal (0.6 mg) and increased (2 mg) doses; residual lipopolysaccharide (endotoxin) present in the antigen preparation.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella recombinant vector vaccine using Escherichia coli
c_description: The study evaluates a live, non-pathogenic Escherichia coli genetically engineered to mimic Brucella infection pathways and present antigens to induce cytolytic T cell responses as a vaccine delivery system. Efficacy: The E. coli vaccine vector infected all tested cells and efficiently delivered therapeutics; elicited a Th1 cytokine profile in primary and secondary immune responses; induced specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) when delivering Brucella antigen. [Ref:6937]
c_preparation: Escherichia coli modified to express Yersinia invasin and Listeria listeriolysin O (LLO) to enable infectivity and antigen release; engineered to express GFP or Brucella antigens.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella rOMP25 subunit vaccine
c_description: Subunit vaccines are considered as an efficient strategy against Brucellosis but are usually less immunogenic than live or killed vaccines; the study aimed to find a proper adjuvant to enhance immune response. Efficacy: CS adjuvant stimulated higher IFN-γ immunity and higher total antibody titers; rOMP25 formulated with CS, IFA, and IFA-CS induced higher IgG2a titers; cell proliferation was promoted after immunization with CS; TNF-α levels were not significantly different except for single IFA treatment. [Ref:7132]
c_adjuvant: yes; Aluminum Hydroxide; Incomplete Freund; Chitosan Nanoparticle
c_preparation: Recombinant OMP25 protein formulated with different adjuvants including Aluminum Hydroxide (AH), Incomplete Freund (IFA), Chitosan Nanoparticle (CS), and combinations of CS with AH or IFA.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella rough strain live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate the safety of the rough strain vaccine against brucellosis in pregnant cattle, addressing the lack of prophylactic strategies for pregnant heifers and cows in many countries. Efficacy: Vaccination with the rough strain had no adverse effect on pregnancy outcomes or calf viability at any gestational period. [Ref:7086]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella SodC and Omp19 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study investigated an oral live vaccine candidate using an attenuated Salmonella typhimurium strain secreting Brucella antigens SodC and Omp19, with the addition of sodium bicarbonate antacid to enhance vaccine efficacy. Efficacy: Addition of sodium bicarbonate significantly increased anti-Brucella-specific systemic IgG levels, lymphocyte proliferation, CD4+ T cell responses, and enhanced Salmonella colonization in the intestine, indicating improved protective immune response compared to vaccine without sodium bicarbonate. [Ref:7145]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella typhimurium strain JOL1800 secreting Brucella SodC and Omp19 antigens; sodium bicarbonate (1.3% w/v) administered orally 30 minutes before and immediately after immunization as an antacid buffer.
c_antigen: Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase (SodC); outer membrane protein 19 (Omp19)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella SodC and Omp19 live attenuated vaccine delivered by Salmonella recombinant vector
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study investigated oral administration of a live attenuated Salmonella vaccine secreting Brucella antigens SodC and Omp19, combined with antacid formulations to neutralize stomach acidity and improve vaccine viability. Efficacy: Co-administration with either sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based antacid buffers significantly enhanced antigen-specific protective immune responses against virulent Brucella challenge; magnesium hydroxide buffer improved Salmonella survival and was safer. [Ref:7182]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella vector secreting Brucella SodC and Omp19 antigens co-administered orally with sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based gastric antacid buffers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella SodC live attenuated vaccine delivered by Salmonella recombinant vector
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: Oral administration of live attenuated Salmonella secreting Brucella SodC antigen with antacid buffers to neutralize stomach acidity and improve vaccine viability. Efficacy: Significant enhancement of antigen-specific protective immune responses against virulent Brucella challenge with antacid co-administration. [Ref:7182]
c_preparation: Live attenuated Salmonella vector secreting Brucella SodC antigen co-administered orally with sodium bicarbonate- or magnesium hydroxide-based gastric antacid buffers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella sodC omp19 BLS PrpA LPS subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safe and effective anti-Brucella subunit vaccine for mucosal protection against respiratory exposure. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant reduction of Brucella recovery in lungs and spleen compared to PBS control after nasal challenge. [Ref:7118]
c_preparation: A chitosan-based nasal vaccine formulated with Brucella immunogens sodC, omp19, BLS, PrpA plus Brucella LPS.
c_antigen: sodC, omp19, BLS, PrpA; Brucella LPS

c_vaccine_name: Brucella sodC omp19 BLS PrpA subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to develop a safe and effective anti-Brucella subunit vaccine for mucosal protection against respiratory exposure. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed significant reduction of Brucella recovery in lungs and spleen compared to PBS control after nasal challenge. [Ref:7118]
c_preparation: A chitosan-based nasal vaccine formulated with Brucella immunogens sodC, omp19, BLS, and PrpA; tested with or without Brucella LPS.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella soluble proteins subunit vaccine
c_description: Immunization with soluble Brucella proteins (SBP) was used to study T cell responses compared to live Brucella infection. Efficacy: IL-4-producing CD4+ T cells from SBP-immunized mice failed to mediate resistance against challenge infection, unlike IFN-gamma-producing CD4+ T cells from infected mice which conferred protection. [Ref:7329]
c_preparation: Soluble protein antigen extracts from Brucella were used for immunization.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella split conjugated inactivated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to obtain a vaccine against animal brucellosis with high immunogenic properties by evaluating the effectiveness of a split-conjugated vaccine combined with immunomodulators fosprenil and polypeptide C. Efficacy: The split-conjugated vaccine combined with fosprenil induced higher antibody titers that persisted longer compared to the vaccine combined with polypeptide C or vaccine alone. [Ref:7168]
c_preparation: The dry split-conjugated vaccine was dissolved in saline; fosprenil was administered intramuscularly; polypeptide C was mixed with the vaccine for subcutaneous injection in one group; another group received vaccine diluted with isotonic sodium chloride solution.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella spp. KETc1 subunit vaccine
c_description: Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS) was evaluated as a novel antigen delivery system and mucosal adjuvant for oral immunization using the KETc1 peptide, an anti-cysticercosis vaccine component. Efficacy: Protection up to 98% was induced by the BLS-KETc1 chimera; BLS as adjuvant with KETc1 induced 79% protection, comparable to cholera toxin (74%); KETc1 and BLS administered separately also reduced parasite load. [Ref:6919]
c_preparation: KETc1 peptide was administered orally either as a chimera fused to BLS or with BLS as an adjuvant; KETc1 and BLS were also administered separately.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella spp. lumazine synthase VP8d subunit vaccine
c_description: The study assessed the lumazine synthase from Brucella spp. (BLS) fused to the VP8d domain of bovine rotavirus as a scaffold for recombinant vaccine development in plants. Efficacy: Soluble protein extracts induced specific neutralizing IgY antibodies in the laying hen model. [Ref:7056]
c_preparation: The fusion protein BLSVP8d was expressed in tobacco chloroplasts, producing a highly expressed, soluble, and stable protein representing 40% of total soluble protein; lyophilized leaves containing the antigen were also tested.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella spp. multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine was designed using reverse vaccinology and bioinformatics targeting the CcmA, ccmC, and BepC membrane proteins to provide protection against human Brucella infection. Efficacy: Immunoinformatics simulations predicted effective increase in antibody levels, T cell counts, and proinflammatory cytokines. [Ref:7281]
c_adjuvant: yes; HMGN1 (high mobility group nucleosome binding protein 1)
c_preparation: The vaccine consists of 11 CTL, 9 HTL, 2 conformational B cell, and 9 linear B cell epitopes linked by GGGS, GPGPG, and KK linkers; includes HMGN1 as an adjuvant and PADRE universal HTL epitope to enhance immunogenicity; codon optimized for E. coli expression.
c_antigen: CcmA; ccmC; BepC membrane proteins; PADRE epitope

c_vaccine_name: Brucella strain 2 Ag85A live attenuated vaccine
c_description: This study used Antigen 85A (Ag85A) as a carrier fused with the Brucella S2 vaccine to reduce toxicity and enhance protective effect. Efficacy: The S2-Ag85A vaccine effectively reduced toxicity residue of the S2 vaccine and enhanced protective ability against Brucella infection in mice. [Ref:7213]
c_preparation: Oral live attenuated vaccine combining Brucella S2 strain with Ag85A as a carrier.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella strain BA0711 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to elucidate the genetic basis of virulence attenuation in the Brucella attenuated vaccine strain BA0711 by whole-genome sequencing and comparison with the Brucella wild-type strain M28. Efficacy: The vaccine strain BA0711 maintains strong host adaptability, viability, and immunogenicity despite genetic mutations and deletions. [Ref:7299]

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis Ag85 DNA vaccine
c_description: The oral S2-Ag85 vaccine has been shown to protect the human body and effectively improve the titration of the vaccine by acting on intestinal mucosa cells and enhancing their immunogenicity. Efficacy: The S2-Ag85A vaccine was effective in activating dsDNA and RNA transduction pathways in intestinal cells and improving intestinal antigen presentation in mice. [Ref:7204]
c_preparation: Recombinant S2-Ag85 DNA vaccine administered orally.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis BepC multi-epitope subunit vaccine
c_description: Designed a novel chimeric multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) construct based on immunoinformatic prediction of antigenic proteins from the whole proteome of Brucella suis using subtractive genomics and reverse vaccinology approaches. Efficacy: Computational analyses suggest the MEV is highly antigenic, non-toxic, non-allergenic, flexible, stable, and soluble, with strong predicted interactions with TLR4 and HLAs, supporting its potential efficacy against Brucella suis infections. [Ref:7210]
c_preparation: The MEV construct of 324 amino acids was created by linking six MHC I, ten MHC II, and four B-cell epitopes with appropriate linkers and combined with the TLR4 agonist HBHA protein as an adjuvant to boost immune response.
c_antigen: Multidrug efflux Resistance-nodulation-division (RND) transporter outer membrane subunit (gene BepC); T-cell and B-cell epitopes (six MHC I, ten MHC II, four B-cell epitopes)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis BtaF subunit vaccine
c_description: The BtaF passenger domain was engineered and expressed as a soluble trimeric protein for nasal vaccination. Efficacy: Nasal vaccination with BtaF+c-di-AMP did not protect against respiratory B. suis challenge but conferred significant protection against intragastric challenge, reducing splenic bacterial load by 3.28 log CFU. [Ref:7137]
c_preparation: Nasal immunization with recombinant BtaF protein plus the mucosal adjuvant c-di-AMP.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis ctpA deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A CtpA-deficient Brucella suis strain (1330DeltactpA) was generated by allelic exchange to study the role of the carboxyl-terminal processing protease in bacterial morphology and persistence. Efficacy: Vaccination with the ctpA-deficient strain conferred 4 to 5 log(10) CFU protection against challenge with virulent B. abortus strain 2308 or B. suis strain 1330 but no protection against B. melitensis strain 16 M. [Ref:6907]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain with ctpA gene deletion.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis delta mapB outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Brucella suis ΔmapB outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) were characterized and evaluated as an acellular vaccine candidate to protect against systemic and mucosal B. suis infection, addressing the lack of available vaccines for swine brucellosis. Efficacy: Immunization with ΔmapB OMVs induced higher antigen-specific IgG titers than wild-type OMVs; antibodies reduced bacterial adherence and invasion and enhanced phagocytosis; ΔmapB OMVs induced stronger Th1 cellular responses; both OMVs conferred protection against intratracheal challenge, but ΔmapB OMVs provided superior protection against intraperitoneal infection. [Ref:7267]
c_preparation: OMVs were isolated from B. suis ΔmapB mutant strain using ultracentrifugation and characterized by electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, SDS-PAGE, and proteomics; no adjuvant was reported.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis delta pgm live attenuated vaccine
c_description: A novel vaccine strain was constructed by deleting the phosphoglucomutase (pgm) gene, which is involved in polysaccharide biosynthesis. This strain lacks complete lipopolysaccharide, cannot synthesize cyclic beta glucans, and is sensitive to detergents and Polymyxin B. Efficacy: The Delta-pgm strain was completely avirulent in mice and conferred excellent protection against challenge with virulent Brucella suis. [Ref:7060]
c_preparation: Live attenuated strain with clean deletion of the pgm gene.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis live attenuated vaccine expressing multimeric GnRH
c_description: This study reports the development of a live-attenuated Brucella suis vaccine strain that is auxotrophic for leucine and capable of expressing heterologous antigens, specifically multimeric GnRH, aimed at controlling feral swine populations and brucellosis. Efficacy: The attenuated vaccine strain provided significant protection against Brucella suis challenge in mice. [Ref:7121]
c_preparation: The vaccine strain is leucine auxotrophic, allowing over-expression of heterologous antigens without antibiotic resistance markers.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis OmaA-deficient live attenuated vaccine
c_description: An OmaA-deficient strain of Brucella suis strain 1330 was generated by disrupting the DNA region encoding the passenger alpha-domain of the OmaA protein. The full-length OmaA gene was cloned and used to complement the deficient strain. Efficacy: Vaccination with the OmaA-deficient strain provided 3.0-3.9 log10 colony forming units protection against challenge with B. suis strain 1330 in BALB/c mice. [Ref:6904]
c_preparation: Live attenuated OmaA-deficient Brucella suis strain 1330

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis outer membrane vesicle vaccine; Brucella ovis outer membrane vesicle vaccine; Brucella canis outer membrane vesicle vaccine; Brucella neotomae outer membrane vesicle vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from Brucella suis, B. ovis, B. canis, and B. neotomae were purified and analyzed to determine their proteomic composition and antigenic proteins. [Ref:7181]
c_preparation: OMVs purified from the outer membrane of the four Brucella species; proteomic analysis by SDS-PAGE, transmission electron microscopy, and liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry; antigenic proteins detected by western blot with anti-Brucella sera.
c_antigen: Omp16; Omp25; Omp31; SodC; Omp2a; BhuA

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis polysaccharide protein subunit vaccine
c_description: A subunit vaccine candidate was produced from Brucella suis 145 (biovar 4) expressing both the A antigen of Brucella abortus and the M antigen of Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: Vaccinated mice showed statistically significant reduction in bacterial colonization compared to unvaccinated controls; as little as 1 ng protected mice against B. suis 145 infection; a single 1 μg injection protected mice for at least 14 months. [Ref:7019]
c_preparation: The preparation consisted mostly of polysaccharide (>90% wt/wt; both cell-associated PS and exo-PS combined) and a small amount of protein (1 to 3%) with no apparent nucleic acids; the vaccine was thermostable due to heat treatment (boiling-water bath, autoclaving) and contained no added adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis strain 2 bacterial ghosts vaccine
c_description: The vaccine was generated by cloning the lysis gene E and temperature-sensitive regulator cassette into a shuttle plasmid, which was introduced into attenuated Brucella suis live vaccine S2 bacteria to produce bacterial ghosts by inducing lysis gene E expression. Efficacy: The bacterial ghosts demonstrated protection levels against Brucella melitensis 16M challenge similar to the attenuated Brucella suis live vaccine S2. [Ref:7035]
c_preparation: Bacterial ghosts produced from Brucella suis strain 2 live vaccine S2 by induction of lysis gene E expression.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis strain 2 live attenuated vaccine adjuvanted with Ag85a
c_description: A live-attenuated Brucella suis strain 2 vaccine (S2) was developed and adjuvanted with Ag85a to enhance immune responses and provide a candidate vaccine for preventing Brucella pathogens from livestock, potentially reducing dosage and toxicity compared to S2 alone. Efficacy: Ag85a-S2 triggered a stronger cellular immune response compared to S2 alone, with enhanced induction of interferon and other cytokines dependent on the cGAS-STING pathway. [Ref:7211]
c_preparation: Live-attenuated Brucella suis strain 2 vaccine combined with Ag85a as an adjuvant

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis strain 353-1 live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the safety, immunogenicity, and clearance of the natural rough mutant of Brucella suis strain 353-1 as a vaccine in domestic swine. Efficacy: The vaccine strain was nonpathogenic, cleared from most vaccinates by 10-12 weeks, did not cause significant tissue lesions, was phenotypically stable, and was not shed to sentinel animals. [Ref:6995]
c_preparation: Live natural rough mutant strain 353-1 administered by conjunctival or intramuscular routes at doses of 5 × 10^7 CFU or 1-2 × 10^10 CFU.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis strain S105 vaccine
c_description: A mutant strain S105 was selected from Brucella suis strain 2 after chemical mutagenesis with diethyl sulphate (DES) to reduce residual virulence. Efficacy: Strain S105 was as effective as the parent strain 2 in stimulating protective immunity to Brucella melitensis in sheep. [Ref:7076]
c_preparation: Oral vaccine formulation of the mutant strain S105.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella suis wild type outer membrane vesicle subunit vaccine
c_description: Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) from wild-type B. suis 1330 strain were characterized and evaluated as an acellular vaccine candidate against systemic and mucosal B. suis infection. Efficacy: Immunization induced antigen-specific IgG and functional antibodies that reduced bacterial adherence and invasion and enhanced phagocytosis; conferred protection against intratracheal challenge but was less protective than ΔmapB OMVs against intraperitoneal infection. [Ref:7267]
c_preparation: OMVs were isolated from wild-type B. suis using ultracentrifugation and characterized by electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, SDS-PAGE, and proteomics; no adjuvant was reported.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella TF BP26 omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: A trivalent candidate antigen formulation containing TF, BP26, and omp31 was designed and evaluated using bioinformatics, cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21, purified, and incorporated into a polyethyleneimine nanostructure targeted with LPS to stimulate selective immune responses. Efficacy: Recombinant protein and nanoparticle formulations induced significant immune responses compared to controls and showed good response upon subsequent injections with live bacterial strains. [Ref:7256]
c_preparation: Recombinant proteins encapsulated inside a polyethyleneimine nanostructure targeted with LPS; nanoparticle properties such as size, zeta potential, retention rate, diffusion efficacy, and antigen binding were characterized for injection and inhalation delivery in mice.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella trigger factor BP26 Omp31 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate immunity induced by a mannosylated niosome containing a recombinant chimeric protein composed of Brucella trigger factor, BP26, and Omp31 in a mouse model. Efficacy: Niosomal and mannosylated niosomal antigen formulations induced higher antibody levels compared to controls. The IgG2a/IgG1 ratio was greater than one for mannosylated niosome-rTBO, indicating a Th1-biased response. Cytokine production was significantly higher in vaccinated groups, especially with intraperitoneal administration, and immunization conferred protection against Brucella challenge. [Ref:7251]
c_preparation: The recombinant chimeric protein (rTBO) was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified, and loaded onto niosome and mannosylated niosome nanoparticles used as immunoadjuvants.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella trigger factor Omp31 Bp26 subunit vaccine
c_description: A recombinant chimeric protein was designed by fusing three immunodominant Brucella antigens (trigger factor, Omp31, and Bp26) using EAAAK linkers, synthesized, cloned, and expressed in E. coli. Efficacy: Immunized mice sera contained high levels of IgG antibodies against the recombinant chimeric protein. [Ref:7073]
c_preparation: Purified recombinant chimeric protein combined with an adjuvant (not specified).

c_vaccine_name: Brucella U-Omp19 subunit vaccine
c_description: The study focuses on the use of U-Omp19, a recombinant unlipidated outer membrane protein from Brucella spp., as a protease inhibitor with immunostimulatory properties used as an adjuvant in oral vaccine formulations. Efficacy: Co-administration of U-Omp19 facilitated antigen accumulation within lysosomal compartments of intestinal epithelial cells, enhanced transcellular passage of antigen without affecting epithelial barrier permeability, and induced antigen-specific IgA production in feces. [Ref:7115]
c_preparation: Oral co-administration of U-Omp19 with antigen to protect the antigen from enzymatic degradation and enhance delivery across the intestinal epithelial barrier.
c_antigen: recombinant unlipidated outer membrane protein from Brucella spp. (U-Omp19)

c_vaccine_name: Brucella U-Omp19 vaccine
c_description: U-Omp19, a bacterial protease inhibitor from Brucella spp., is used as a constituent in vaccine formulations to protect co-administered antigens from gastrointestinal protease digestion when given orally. Efficacy: Conferred mucosal protection and reduced parasite loads after oral challenge with virulent Toxoplasma gondii. [Ref:7045]
c_preparation: Oral co-administration of U-Omp19 with an antigen; U-Omp19 inhibits stomach and intestinal proteases, increasing antigen half-life at Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella urease subunit vaccine
c_description: The study examined immune response and protection elicited by recombinant Brucella urease protein as a subunit vaccine administered subcutaneously and intraperitoneally in mice. Efficacy: Subcutaneous vaccination conferred a higher degree of protection against virulent Brucella melitensis, B. abortus, and B. suis challenge compared to intraperitoneal vaccination (p ≤ 0.05). [Ref:7031]
c_preparation: Recombinant urease protein cloned in pET28a vector and administered as a subunit vaccine via subcutaneous and intraperitoneal routes.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella virB2 deletion mutant live attenuated vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to construct Brucella vaccine strain M5-90 delta virB2 mutants as a basis for developing new attenuated vaccines. [Ref:6963]
c_preparation: A virB2 deletion mutant was created using homologous recombination with a suicide plasmid pGEM-7zf-delta virB2-sacB.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB2 VirB3 VirB6 BtpA RNA vaccine
c_description: This study develops a multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting the Brucella type IV secretion system using reverse vaccinology and bioinformatics tools. Efficacy: Computational results indicate the vaccine effectively stimulates an immune response with stable interaction to TLR4 (docking score -350.15); however, no wet lab validation yet. [Ref:7278]
c_preparation: The vaccine includes epitopes from VirB2, VirB3, VirB6, and BtpA proteins linked appropriately for mRNA vaccine design; molecular docking and dynamics simulations were used to optimize vaccine-TLR4 interactions.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB7 subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine targets VirB7, a component of the type IV secretion system, a key virulence factor mediating intracellular survival of Brucella spp. Efficacy: Mice immunized with VirB7 showed almost 1 log reduction in spleen bacterial load after challenge with live Brucella abortus compared to unvaccinated controls; sera from immunized dogs mediated significant bacteriolysis of B. canis in vitro. [Ref:7021]
c_preparation: VirB7 protein administered subcutaneously in three doses with QuilA adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB8 and VirB10 multi-epitope vaccine
c_description: A multi-epitope vaccine was designed targeting antigenic epitopes of the Brucella type IV secretion system proteins VirB8 and VirB10 to address the need for improved prevention and treatment of brucellosis, especially in humans where no vaccine currently exists. Efficacy: Not experimentally tested; in silico immune simulation suggested the vaccine construct may help initiate cellular and humoral immunity in brucellosis patients. [Ref:7230]
c_preparation: The vaccine construct was composed of 2 cytotoxic T lymphocyte epitopes, 9 helper T lymphocyte epitopes, 6 linear B cell epitopes, and 6 conformational B cell epitopes spliced together with different linkers to form a multi-epitope vaccine.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB9 subunit vaccine
c_description: The vaccine targets VirB9, a component of the type IV secretion system, a key virulence factor mediating intracellular survival of Brucella spp. Efficacy: Mice immunized with VirB9 showed almost 1 log reduction in spleen bacterial load after challenge with live Brucella abortus compared to unvaccinated controls; sera from immunized dogs mediated significant bacteriolysis of B. canis in vitro. [Ref:7021]
c_preparation: VirB9 protein administered subcutaneously in three doses with QuilA adjuvant.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella VirB9 VirB10 Omp19 Omp25 IgV CTLA-4 subunit vaccine
c_description: A novel multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) was designed to prevent human Brucella infection by combining multiple epitopes from four Brucella proteins with the immunoglobulin variable region of CTLA-4 (IgV_CTLA-4) to enhance immune activation. Efficacy: V_C4MEV demonstrated favorable immunogenicity and antigenicity, showing potential to activate defensive cells and immune responses against Brucella. [Ref:7253]
c_preparation: Multiple epitopes including cytotoxic T lymphocyte, helper T lymphocyte, linear B-cell, and conformational B-cell epitopes from VirB9, VirB10, Omp19, and Omp25 were linked together to maintain correct protein folding; the MEV protein was fused with IgV_CTLA-4 to create the vaccine V_C4MEV.

c_vaccine_name: Brucella-infected macrophage-derived Exosomes vaccine
c_description: This study explored the significance of exosomes derived from Brucella-infected macrophages in the context of Brucella infection and their influence on host immune responses, proposing their potential as innovative vaccines or immune adjuvants for brucellosis. Efficacy: Exosomes enhanced the host's anti-Brucella immune response and inhibited intracellular bacterial survival. [Ref:7280]
c_preparation: Exosomes derived from Brucella-infected macrophages.

c_vaccine_name: Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella abortus combined DNA vaccine
c_description: The study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a combined DNA vaccine containing six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from M. bovis and B. abortus. Efficacy: The combined DNA vaccine significantly reduced the number of positive lymph node and spleen cultures for both pathogens compared to unvaccinated calves; provided significantly better protection than BCG vaccine against M. bovis; protection level comparable to S19 vaccine against B. abortus. [Ref:6941]
c_preparation: Combined DNA vaccine containing six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from both pathogens.
c_antigen: six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from Mycobacterium bovis and Brucella abortus

c_vaccine_name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Brucella abortus combined DNA vaccine
c_description: The study examined the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a combined DNA vaccine including six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from M. tuberculosis and B. abortus. Efficacy: DNA-IL-12(+) immunized mice showed significantly reduced CFU counts in lung and spleen for M. tuberculosis and B. abortus, respectively, with better protection than combined DNA vaccine alone or positive controls. [Ref:2294]
c_preparation: Combined DNA vaccine administered with an IL-12 expression vector as an adjuvant.
c_antigen: six genes encoding immunodominant antigens from Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Brucella abortus

c_vaccine_name: recombinant pseudorabies virus carrying Brucella melitensis bp26 vaccine
c_description: The study developed and purified a recombinant pseudorabies virus with deletions in TK and gE genes carrying the bp26 gene of Brucella melitensis. Efficacy: The recombinant virus elicited high titers of humoral antibodies against Brucella and pseudorabies virus, and induced strong Brucella-specific lymphocyte proliferation and interferon gamma production. [Ref:7029]
c_preparation: Recombinant pseudorabies virus with ΔTK/ΔgE deletions expressing Brucella melitensis bp26 gene.

c_vaccine_name: Salmonella Typhimurium recombinant vector vaccine expressing Brucella abortus BLS PrpA Omp19 and SOD proteins
c_description: This study explores the efficacy of a Salmonella Typhimurium delivery-based combination vaccine expressing four heterologous Brucella antigens targeting brucellosis in goats. Efficacy: Immunized goats showed significantly higher protection demonstrated by lower bacterial loads in most tissues, reduced expression of Brucella antigens in spleen, kidney, and lung, and ameliorated histopathological lesions compared to non-immunized controls. [Ref:7108]
c_preparation: Attenuated Salmonella Typhimurium vector expressing Brucella lumazine synthase (BLS), proline racemase subunit A (PrpA), outer-membrane protein 19 (Omp19), and Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase (SOD); administered subcutaneously at two inoculation levels (5 × 10^9 CFU/mL and 5 × 10^10 CFU/mL).

c_vaccine_name: Sheep pox virus strain NISKHI recombinant vector vaccine expressing Brucella spp. OMP25 and Foot-and-mouth disease virus VP1
c_type: Live attenuated vaccine + Recombinant vector vaccine
c_description: The study aimed to evaluate attenuated sheep pox virus strain NISKHI as a vector expressing foreign genes including Brucella spp. OMP25 and FMDV VP1. Efficacy: Mice immunized with the recombinant virus elicited specific antibodies against both sheep pox virus and the foreign antigens VP1 and OMP25. [Ref:7191]
c_preparation: Recombinant sheep pox viruses with deletions in ribonucleotide kinase (SPPV020) and thymidine kinase (SPPV066) genes were engineered to express enhanced green fluorescent protein, VP1, and OMP25 using integration plasmids and transient dominant selection.
